CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

- caveman:cavecrew-reviewer: Diff/branch/file reviewer. One line per finding, severity-tagged, no praise, no scope creep. Output format `path:line: <emoji> <severity>: <problem>. <fix>.` Use for "review this PR", "review my diff", "audit this file". Skips formatting nits unless they change meaning. (Tools: Read, Grep, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## railway
Railway MCP server. Manage your Railway projects, services, deployments, and more.

- _gstack-command: Router for the gstack skill suite. (gstack)
- agent-browser: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. - building-macapp: Builds, tests, formats, and lints the macOS app under `macapp/` via its make targets. - caveman:caveman-commit: Generate terse caveman-style commit message

- caveman:caveman-review: One-line code review comments
- caveman:caveman-stats: Real session token usage + lifetime savings + USD. Tweetable line via --share.

## 1. The views that render the VCS sidebar / inspector "Changes" panel

Everything lives in `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/`.

| File:lines | What |
|---|---|
| `ChangesPanel.swift:11-262` | **`RightInspector`** — the whole inspector pane. Maps `ActivitySection.subSections` → headers/bodies and hands them to `InspectorSplitView`. |

| `ChangesPanel.swift:123-137` | `sectionBody(for:)` — `ChangesPanel()`, `FilesPanel`, `PullRequestPanel`, `HistoryPanel`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:229-261` | `changesIndicator` / `changesIndicatorLabel` — the `+N`/`-M` + conflict/dot badge shown inline in the Changes header. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:578-785` | **`ChangesPanel`** — the Changes *body*: branch header → `Divider()` → changes list. `renderCap = 200`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:596-621` | `content(for sid:)` — empty/missing/loading/git-vs-jj dispatch. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:626-639` | `gitContent` — `VStack(spacing:10) { changesHeader; Divider(); fileList/clean/failure }.padding(12)`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:645-661` | `jjContent` — same shape, `identifier: "changes.workingCopy"`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:669-730` | **`changesHeader`** — the one shared branch/bookmark header (see §3). |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:756-768` | `fileList` — `VStack(spacing: 1)` of `ChangedFileRow`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:304-487` | **`ChangedFileRow`** — one changed-file row (letter, name, dimmed dir, hover toolbar). |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:796-804` | `inspectorMessage(_:)` — shared placeholder line, `.padding(12)`. |
| `InspectorColumn.swift:12-59` | Docked inspector column: `RightInspector()` in a `sidebarCard(topMargin: 0, leadingMargin: 2, vibrant: true)`, width 260–520, drag handle on leading edge. |
| `RootView.swift:148-173` | Composition: `HStack { SidebarColumn / detail / if showInspector { InspectorColumn() } / ActivityBar() }`. |
| `EdgeRevealSidebar.swift:287-291` | Note: the right-edge *reveal* was dropped — only the left sidebar has one now. |

## 2. Sidebar composition — sections, headers, History, pane-header helpers

**Section model** (`Core/`):
- `ActivitySection.swift:15-56` — the activity-bar rail is now only `.changes` + `.files`. `subSections` (line 42-47): `.changes → [.changes, .history, .pullRequest]`, `.files → [.files]`.
- `ActivitySection.swift:58-64` — `InspectorSectionKind.storeIndex` (changes=0, files=1, pullRequest=2, **history=3**, appended last so indices stayed stable).
- `InspectorPanePolicy.swift:7-14` — `InspectorSectionKind` enum. `:47` `headerHeight = 34`, `:52` `expandedMinHeight = 120`, `:81` `allocate`, `:128` `reallocateOnToggle`.
- `ActivityBarReducer.swift:14-38` — icon-click vs shortcut vs toggle semantics.

**Split container / pane host** (`Views/InspectorSplitView.swift`):
- `:40-114` `InspectorPaneViewController` — sticky `NSHostingController` header (fixed `headerHeight`) + body in either scroll mode or **fill** mode.
- `:135-139` `ThemedSplitView` — divider forced to `tokens.nsFg.withAlphaComponent(0.12)`.
- `:141+` `InspectorSplitContainerController` — `NSSplitViewDelegate`, weights round-trip to the store.
- **`:466-539` `SectionHeader<Accessory>`** — the pane-header helper:
  ```swift
  .accessibilityIdentifier("inspector.header.\(title)")
  .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
  .background(ThemeService.shared.tokens.surface)
  .overlay(alignment: .trailing) { accessory().padding(.trailing, 12) }
  ```
  `headerLabel` (`:521-538`): `HStack(spacing: 7) { chevron(11pt semibold, rotate 0→90°, width 12); Text(title).font(.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)); indicator; Spacer }` with `.padding(.horizontal, 12).padding(.vertical, 8)`. `collapsed: nil` ⇒ solo pane, no chevron.

**History moved into the Changes stack** (commit `0fc3b97a`):
- `HistoryPanel.swift:8-146` — body; hosted in **fill mode** (`ChangesPanel.swift:32` `fills: subs.map { $0 == .history }`) so it owns its `ScrollView` (`:78-128`).
- `AppStore.swift:303-317` `historySectionCollapsed` (persists + eager focus), `:322-324` `historySectionShown`, `:337-340` `focusHistoryIfShown()`.
- `DefaultsKeys.swift:149-150` key renamed to `"inspector.layout.v2"`; `:199-205` `InspectorPaneState { collapsed: [Bool], weights: [Double] }` (4-vectors).
- `WorkroomApp.swift:815-870` — View-menu toggles ⌥⌘C / ⌥⌘Y / ⌥⌘P now expand/collapse sections rather than switch panes.

**Store state**: `AppStore.swift:291-345` (`changesSectionCollapsed`, `filesSectionCollapsed`, `prSectionCollapsed`, `historySectionCollapsed`, `inspectorSizeWeights`), `:351-364` `activeInspectorSection`, `:780-781` `inspectorTargetID` / `inspectorTarget`.

## 3. Where the branch / bookmark name is displayed

**The "ONE layout for both git/jj" header** — `ChangesPanel.swift:663-730`:

```swift
// ChangesPanel.swift:680-696
let extraRefs = (meta?.refs ?? []).filter { $0 != name }
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
  HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 6) {
    Text(name).font(.caption)
      .lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.middle)
      .padding(.horizontal, 5).padding(.vertical, 1)
      .background(.quaternary, in: Capsule())
      .help(ancestorBookmark ? "First ancestor bookmark in history" : "Bookmark / branch")
```
Then (jj only) change-id `.purple` / commit-id `.blue` in `.system(.callout, design: .monospaced)` (`:697-705`), extra ref capsules at `.caption` (`:709-715`), and the description line at `.callout` / `"(no description set)"` `.footnote .tertiary` (`:719-726`).

Resolution — `ChangesPanel.swift:735-741`:
```swift
private func branchLabel(sid: SidebarID, status: WorkroomStatus) -> String {
  if let branch = status.branchForCI, !branch.isEmpty { return branch }
  if case .root(let p) = sid { return RootPresentation.make(store.rootRefs[p] ?? .unresolved).label }
  return "detached"
}
```
Call site + jj ancestor-bookmark discrimination: `ChangesPanel.swift:609-619`.

**Other branch-name surfaces (same capsule/label vocabulary):**
- `TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104` — `branchSegment`, `Label` + `arrow.triangle.branch`, `.truncationMode(.middle)`, help `"Current branch / bookmark"`; resolved by `AppStore.swift:1235-1255` `branchLabel(for:)`.
- `ProjectSidebar.swift:285-344` — project root row: `RootPresentation.make(store.rootRefs[...])`, `.font(.callout)`, `.truncationMode(.tail)`, plus an `arrow.up` "ahead" marker (`:302-306`).
- `Core/Models.swift:127-165` — `RootPresentation.Style { label, tooltip, accessibility, ahead, dim }`.
- `HistoryPanel.swift:222-230` — per-commit ref capsules (`.caption2`, `.quaternary` Capsule).
- `ChangesetDetailView.swift:142-150` — same ref capsules in the changeset detail header.

## 4. Existing toolbar-like rows / strips you could reuse for a 3-segment toolbar

**Grouped segmented switches (closest existing precedent — track + raised thumb):**
- `TerminalTabStrip.swift:725-767` **`DiffModeSwitch`** (internal, already shared by two callers):
  ```swift
  HStack(spacing: 0) { segment(...); segment(...) }
    .padding(1.5)
    .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(theme.tokens.surface))
  // segment: 9.5pt glyph, .padding(.horizontal, 6).padding(.vertical, 3),
  //          RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5).fill(active ? theme.tokens.bg : .clear)
  //          + .help / .accessibilityLabel / .accessibilityIdentifier / .isSelected trait
  ```
- `TerminalTabStrip.swift:769-815` **`MarkdownModeSwitch`** — a literal copy of the above for a different 2-way choice. Adding a third segment is a `segment(...)` call; there is no 3-segment control in the app yet, and these two are the pattern to generalize.

**Divided segments / hairline group separators:**
- `TitlebarBars.swift:75-84` **`TitlebarDivider`** — `Rectangle().fill(tokens.border).frame(width: 1, height: 14).padding(.horizontal, 4)`. Used in `LeadingTitlebarBar` (`:111`), `TrailingTitlebarBar` (`:157`), and `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` (`WorkroomSplitView.swift:400, 403`) with the "only when there's something on both sides" rule.
- `TerminalStatusBar.swift:37-59` — a spaced-segment strip (`HStack(spacing: 12)`, `.font(.caption)`, `.frame(height: 24)`, `.background(tokens.bg)`, `.overlay(alignment: .top) { tokens.border.frame(height: 1) }`).
- `WorkroomTabBar.swift:227-251` `showsLeadingSeparator(at:groupOf:)` — the "drop the hairline next to the selected/hovered chip and at group boundaries" logic.

**Chip brackets (rounded outline around a contiguous run):**
- `WorkroomTabBar.swift:253-308` `splitWell(groupOf:)` + `splitRunRects` — `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 7).strokeBorder(tokens.border, lineWidth: 1)` in a `ZStack(alignment: .leading)` with per-run `offset(x:)`; a11y id `workroom.tab.splitBracket.N`.
- `TerminalTabStrip.swift:329-355` `splitWell(_:)` / `splitRunRect` — the single-run twin.
- `TabReorderMath.swift:135-160` `TabStripSplitRun.rect(widths:memberIndices:spacing:)` — the unit-tested geometry both use.

**Hover wells:**
- `ToolbarIconButtonStyle.swift:10-62` — the canonical well: `wellSize = 22`, `horizontalPadding = 3`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6, style: .continuous).fill(tokens.hover)`, opacity animated only on the fill (`.easeOut(0.12)`), press dim 0.6 / disabled 0.4. Apply once to a whole `HStack` via `.buttonStyle(...)`.
- `ChangesPanel.swift:530-551` **`inspectorHeaderButtonChrome(hovering:destructive:)`** — the inspector-specific well: fixed 22×22 fill inside a fixed 28×26 target, `cornerRadius: 5`, `tokens.hover`; used by `InspectorHeaderButton` (`:506-528`) and `InspectorMenuButtonStyle` (`:557-572`). **This is the one to reuse for anything sitting in a section header.**
- `TabToolbarButton.swift:8-43` — icon-only action with its own well (`.padding(4)`, radius 5, `tokens.hover`) + `.contentShape(Rectangle())`.
- `TerminalTabStrip.swift:246-267` `addTerminalButton` (same 4pt/radius-5 well), `:701-723` `TabCloseButton` (circular well).
- `ActivityBar.swift:63-125` `ActivityBarButton` — active = `accentSoft` fill + 2pt accent capsule strip; hover = `tokens.hover`, `cornerRadius: 6`.
- `RowHighlight.swift:8-22` — shared selected/hover row fill (`tokens.surface` / `tokens.hover`, radius 6).
- `TargetDetailToolbar.swift:9-38` `PaneToolbarIcon` — `glyph = 13`, `appIcon = 18`, `disclosure = 8` with headroom notes; `:63` shows the `HStack(spacing: -8)` trick for snugging two wells.
- `WorkroomSplitView.swift:341-440` `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` — a full 3-group toolbar row today (`RunControls | TitlebarDivider | OpenInControl | TitlebarDivider | ✕`), `.frame(height: 28)`, one `.buttonStyle(ToolbarIconButtonStyle())` + one `.font(.system(size: PaneToolbarIcon.glyph))` for the whole group.

## 5. Styling conventions & design system

**Design-system files:**
- `Core/ThemeTokens.swift` — the token snapshot (the design system). `Core/ThemeService.swift:31-76` — `ThemeService.shared`, `private(set) var tokens: ThemeTokens`, `generation`; `:129` posts `.themeDidChange` (`:238`). `Core/Theme.swift` — `ThemePreference`, `ThemeFamily`, `ThemePreview`.
- Access: SwiftUI reads `ThemeService.shared.tokens` via `private let theme = ThemeService.shared` (the pervasive idiom, e.g. `ChangesPanel.swift:580`); AppKit reads the singleton and refreshes on `.themeDidChange` (e.g. `ActivityBar.swift:16-18, 47`).

**Colour tokens** (`ThemeTokens.swift:16-92`, derived in `init` at `:95-193`) — everything is theme-derived, no hard-coded hex:

| Token | Derivation | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `bg` / `fg` | theme bg/fg | base |
| `panel` | bg blended 5.5% toward fg | title bar, tab bar, activity bar |
| `fgMuted` / `fgDim` | fg @ 0.65 / 0.40 | secondary / tertiary text |
| `surface` | fg @ 0.08 | section header background, segmented-switch track, selected row |
| `border` | fg @ 0.12 | hairlines, dividers, chip brackets, split dividers |
| `hover` | fg @ 0.06 | hover wells |
| `tabActive` | fg @ 0.16 | selected tab fill |
| `rowHover` / `rowSelection` | **opaque** panel+6% fg / panel+22% accent | changed-file & history rows (opaque so a hover toolbar painted over matches exactly — `:36-38`) |
| `accent` / `accentSoft` / `accentForeground` | palette[4], @0.10, contrast-picked | selection, active activity-bar icon |
| `warning` / `failure` / `conflict` | palette[3] / palette[1] / red⊕yellow mix | dirty dot, run failure, VCS conflict |
| `diffAddFg`/`diffRemoveFg`/`diffHunkFg` + `…Bg` (@0.16) + `…EmphasisBg` (@0.40) | palette 2/1/6 | `+N`/`-M`, diff gutters |
| `splitGroupFill` / `splitGroupFocusedFill` | fg @0.06 / accent @0.10 | split member cards |
| `focused` / `terminalDim` | fg @0.3 / bg | pane focus ring, scrim |

Semantic mapping helpers: `VCSStatusBadge.swift:6-28` (`Semantic.color`, `iconTint`), `Core/ChangeBadge.swift` (`letter` / `color(_:tokens)` / `word` / `pathLine` — unit-tested).

**Typography conventions** (observed, no font token file):
- Section header title: `.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)`; chevron `.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)`.
- Header icon buttons / small glyphs: `.system(size: 11)`; segmented-switch glyphs `.system(size: 9.5)`; status dots `.system(size: 9)`.
- Row filename: `.callout`. Row directory / metadata: `.system(.caption, design: .monospaced)` + `.tertiary`. Ref pills: `.caption` (Changes header) / `.caption2` (History rows, changeset header). Ids: `.system(.callout, design: .monospaced)` purple/blue. Counts: `.caption.monospacedDigit()`. Placeholders: `.body .secondary` (`inspectorMessage`), `.footnote .tertiary` (no-description).
- Sidebar rows: `.callout`; pane title bar: `.subheadline`; status bar: `.caption`.

**Spacing / geometry conventions:**
- Section body inset: `.padding(12)`; body vertical rhythm `VStack(spacing: 10)`; header inset `.padding(.horizontal, 12).padding(.vertical, 8)`; header accessory `.padding(.trailing, 12)`.
- Row: `.padding(.vertical, 4).padding(.horizontal, 6)`, highlight bleeds full-width via `Rectangle().padding(.horizontal, -12)` (matches the 12pt section inset) — `ChangesPanel.swift:363-369`, `HistoryPanel.swift:240-248`.
- Pills/capsules: `.padding(.horizontal, 5).padding(.vertical, 1)` + `.background(.quaternary, in: Capsule())` (system material, not a token).
- Corner radii: 5 (hover wells, small fills), 6 (toolbar wells, row highlight, segmented track), 7 (chip brackets), 10 (`sidebarCard`).
- Bar heights: title bar 28 (`WorkroomTitlebar.height`), pane title bar 28, status bar 24, inspector section header 34 (`InspectorPanePolicy.headerHeight`), activity bar width 44 / icon 44×40.
- Column widths: inspector 260–520 (`InspectorColumn.swift:22-23`), sidebar 240–360 (`SidebarColumn.swift:27-28`); resize handles 12pt (`InspectorResizeHandle.swift`).
- Card chrome: `SidebarCard.swift:17-56` `sidebarCard(cornerRadius:margin:topMargin:leadingMargin:trailingMargin:vibrant:elevated:)` — `VisualEffectView().overlay(tokens.panel.opacity(0.7))` when vibrant, 1pt `tokens.border` stroke, shadow 0.10/r5/y1 docked vs 0.28/r10/y5 elevated.
- Animations: `.easeOut(0.12)` hover fills, `.easeInOut(0.12)` close buttons, `.easeInOut(0.2)` column show/hide, `.easeInOut(0.22)` divergence accordion; all gated on `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)`.

**Non-negotiable conventions to follow for any new control:** every control carries `.help(...)`, `.accessibilityLabel(...)`, and a stable `.accessibilityIdentifier(...)`; interactive glyphs need their own `.onHover` (so `.help`'s tracking area installs) plus `.contentShape(Rectangle())` (padding doesn't hit-test — see `TabToolbarButton.swift:26-35`); active state is signalled by position/brightness as well as hue (`ActivityBar.swift:59-62`). Formatting: `.swift-format` — 2-space indent, 100 columns; run `make app-format` / `make app-lint`, and `make app-generate` after adding any new `.swift` file.

# VCS engine map — Workroom (macapp + vcs)

## 1. `VCSProviding` protocol

**`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`**

The protocol is **read-only** — 8 requirements, no mutations, no branch listing, no network:

| # | Signature | file:line |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `func log(root: URL, limit: Int) throws -> VCSHistoryPage` (sync, not async) | `VCSProviding.swift:25` |
| 2 | `func changeset(root: URL, commitID: String) async throws -> VCSChangeset` | `:27` |
| 3 | `func fileDiff(root: URL, commitID: String, path: String) async throws -> String` | `:30` |
| 4 | `func workingFileDiff(root: URL, path: String, base: VCSWorkingDiffBase) async throws -> String` | `:33` |

| 7 | `func workingBaseFileContent(root: URL, base: VCSWorkingDiffBase, path: String) async throws -> String?` (default `nil` at `:61`) | `:47` |
| 8 | `func currentRef(root: URL) async throws -> VCSRef` | `:52` |

Supporting enum `VCSWorkingDiffBase { case workingCopy, parent }` at `VCSProviding.swift:8`.

**Routing** — `enum VCS` at `VCSProviding.swift:67`:
- `static func repoKind(at root: URL) -> VCSRepoKind` (`:70`) — pure filesystem: `.jj` must be a dir, `.git` may be dir **or file** (worktrees). Colocated prefers jj.
- `static func provider(for root: URL) throws -> VCSProviding` (`:87`) — `jj* → RustJJProvider()`, `plainGit → GitProvider()`, else `throw VCSError.unsupportedRepo`.

**Note:** `workingStatus` is deliberately **NOT** on the protocol. Each provider has its own, with *different return types* — see §3.

## 2. The two implementations

### git — SwiftGitX (libgit2), pure Swift
- **`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GitProvider.swift:17`** `struct GitProvider: VCSProviding` (477 lines)
- Three reads bypass SwiftGitX onto the raw libgit2 C API:
  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/LibGit2.swift:20` — `enum LibGit2`, sole `git_libgit2_init` owner; `static func withRepository<T>(_ root: URL, _ body: (OpaquePointer) -> T?) -> T?` at `:32`

  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GitCommitDiff.swift` — rename-detected commit diffs (`git_diff_find_similar`)
  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GitDiffStats.swift` — working-tree ± counts (`git_diff_get_stats`)
- SwiftGitX checkout: `macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages/checkouts/SwiftGitX/` — it *does* ship `Repository+fetch.swift`, `+push.swift`, `+checkout.swift`, `+switch.swift`, `Models/Remote.swift`, `Collections/BranchCollection.swift`. **None of these are called by the app** (verified: `grep -E "repo\.(push|fetch|pull|switch|checkout|remote)"` in `WorkroomApp/` → zero matches).

### jj — Rust `jj-lib` via UniFFI
- **`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/RustJJProvider.swift:6`** `struct RustJJProvider: VCSProviding` (339 lines), `import WrVcs`
- Rust workspace `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/vcs/`:
  - `vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/src/lib.rs` — thin façade: `probe_repo` (`:17`), `log_page` (`:31`), `changeset` (`:36`), `current_ref` (`:43`), `working_status` (`:49`)

Key fns: `open` (`:83`), `bookmark_map` (`:113`), `origin_tips` (`:134`), `pushed_revset` (`:174`), `short_change_id` (`:195`), `log_page` (`:349`), `current_ref` (`:418`), `first_bookmark_in_log_order` (`:473`), `commit_changes` (`:501`), `lock_is_held` (`:567`), `snapshot_working_copy` (`:592`), `working_status` (`:686`), `changeset` (`:736`), `changed_files` (`:777`)

  - `vcs/crates/wr-vcs-uniffi/src/lib.rs` — UniFFI export layer; **exactly 5 exported fns**: `probe_repo` (`:309`), `log_page` (`:315`), `changeset` (`:323`), `current_ref` (`:332`), `working_status` (`:341`)

```swift
// RustJJProvider.swift:232
private static func run(_ exe: String, _ args: [String], cwd: URL, timeout: TimeInterval = 30) async throws -> String {
  let result = await StatusCommandRunner().run(exe, args, in: cwd.path, timeout: timeout)
  if result.timedOut { throw VCSError.io("\(exe) timed out after \(Int(timeout))s") }
  guard result.exitCode == 0 else { throw VCSError.io("\(exe) exited \(result.exitCode): \(result.stderr)") }
  return result.stdout
}
```

The only remaining `jj` shell-out in that file is CI branch-tip resolution at `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:374-377` (`jj log -r <branch> -T commit_id`).

## 3. Feature inventory — what exists vs. what does not

### EXISTS

**Current ref only (not a list).**
```swift
func currentRef(root: URL) async throws -> VCSRef            // VCSProviding.swift:52
```
- git (`GitProvider.swift:78`): unborn HEAD → `config.defaultBranchName`; else `repo.branch.current.name` → `.branch`; else `repo.HEAD.target.id.abbreviated` → `.detached`
- jj (`jj_backend.rs:418`): bookmark on `@` → `Branch`; else first bookmark in `::@` log order → `Ancestor`; never `Detached`

**Local branch/bookmark enumeration — exists, but only as internal decoration maps, not as a listing API:**
```swift
private static func decorations(in repo: Repository) -> [String: [String]]   // GitProvider.swift:328
//   repo.branch.list(.local)  (GitProvider.swift:330) + repo.tag.list() (:335)
//   remote-tracking refs deliberately EXCLUDED as labels
```
```rust
fn bookmark_map(repo: &ReadonlyRepo) -> HashMap<String, Vec<String>>        // jj_backend.rs:113
//   repo.view().local_bookmarks()
```
Both are `private`/`fn` (not `pub`), keyed sha→names, and only feed `VCSCommit.refs`. **Neither is reachable from Swift as "give me the branches".**

**Remotes — read only, `origin`-scoped, only for push state:**
```swift
static func unpushed(root: URL, decide: Set<String>) -> PageRead?           // GitGraph.swift:43
static func isPushed(root: URL, commitID: String) -> (pushed: Bool, scope: Scope)?  // GitGraph.swift:76
private static func originTips(_ repo: OpaquePointer) -> [Tip]?            // GitGraph.swift:102
//   git_reference_iterator_glob_new(&iter, repo, "refs/remotes/origin/*")  (:106)
```
```rust
const PUSH_REMOTE: &str = "origin";                                        // jj_backend.rs:129
fn origin_tips(repo: &ReadonlyRepo) -> (Vec<CommitId>, Vec<String>)        // jj_backend.rs:134
//   repo.view().all_remote_bookmarks(), filtered on remote=="origin" && is_tracked() && is_present()
```
No `git_remote_*` call anywhere in the app; no remote *enumeration*, no URLs, no add/remove.

**Working-copy status — per-provider, NOT on the protocol, different return types:**
```swift

func workingStatus(root: URL) throws -> WorkroomStatus                     // RustJJProvider.swift:70
```
`GitProvider.swift:466-477` says explicitly: *"Git-shaped for now; the jj working status … unifies onto a shared `VCSProviding.workingStatus` in the follow-on."* This is the obvious seam if you add anything status-shaped.

**Push state (a reachability boolean, NOT ahead/behind counts):** `VCSPushState { pushed, unpushed, unknown }` + `VCSPushScope { refName, count }` — `count` is the *number of origin branches compared against*, not commits ahead.

### DOES NOT EXIST — confirmed by exhaustive grep

| Feature | Status |
|---|---|
| **List branches / bookmarks** (as an API the app can call) | ❌ Only the private sha→label decoration maps above |
| **Checkout / switch branch** | ❌ Nothing. No `checkout`, `switch`, `jj edit`, `jj new`, `git switch` anywhere in `WorkroomApp/` or `vcs/` |
| **Create / delete / rename a branch or bookmark** | ❌ |
| **Remotes** (list, URLs, add/remove) | ❌ Only the hardcoded `origin` glob/filter |
| **Fetch** | ❌ Nothing. SwiftGitX's `Repository+fetch.swift` is never called |
| **Push** | ❌ Nothing (only *push state* reads). SwiftGitX's `Repository+push.swift` never called |
| **Pull / merge / rebase** | ❌ |
| **Ahead/behind counts (tracking status)** | ❌ No `git_graph_ahead_behind`, no upstream/`@{u}` read, no counts. The only `ahead` in the codebase is a *cosmetic* `↑` glyph for jj's `.ancestor` ref kind (`Models.swift:132`, `:146`) and GitHub's PR `mergeState == .behind` (`WorkroomStatus.swift:166`, from `gh`, not local git) |

```swift
func runBlocking<T: Sendable>(
  qos: DispatchQoS.QoSClass = .userInitiated, _ work: @escaping @Sendable () throws -> T
) async throws -> T {
  try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
    DispatchQueue.global(qos: qos).async { continuation.resume(with: Result(catching: work)) }
  }
}
```

### Bottom line for a branch-selection feature
`VCSProviding` is a **pure read protocol with no branch-list and no mutation**. Adding "list branches/bookmarks + switch" means: (1) a new protocol requirement (both backends have the raw capability already — `repo.branch.list(.local)` is called at `GitProvider.swift:330`, `repo.view().local_bookmarks()` at `jj_backend.rs:115`, both currently discarded into sha→label maps); (2) for jj, a **new `#[uniffi::export]` fn** in `vcs/crates/wr-vcs-uniffi/src/lib.rs` + `wr-vcs-core/src/lib.rs` façade + a rebuild (`make app-vcs`); (3) for the *switch*, the first **mutating** op in the engine — which for jj must go through `JJSnapshotGate` and will trip `handleRootBranchChange`'s watcher (that's the desired refresh path, and `.git`/`.jj` writes are exactly what it watches). The `GitWorkingStatus`/`WorkroomStatus` split noted at `GitProvider.swift:466-468` is the pre-marked place for a unified status member.

```swift
func runBlocking<T: Sendable>(
  qos: DispatchQoS.QoSClass = .userInitiated, _ work: @escaping @Sendable () throws -> T
) async throws -> T {
  try await withCheckedThrowingContinuation { continuation in
    DispatchQueue.global(qos: qos).async { continuation.resume(with: Result(catching: work)) }
  }
}
```

# 1. SwiftGitX — exact API, and the auth answer

**Version pinned:** `macapp/project.yml:32-34` — `SwiftGitX` `exactVersion: "0.4.0"`; `macapp/project.yml:40-42` — `libgit2` `exactVersion: "1.9.2"` (linked directly *as well as* via SwiftGitX).
Checkout root: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages/checkouts/SwiftGitX/`

### Signatures

| Op | File:line | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `Sources/SwiftGitX/Repository/Repository+fetch.swift:20` | `public nonisolated func fetch(remote: Remote? = nil) async throws(SwiftGitXError)` |
| **pull** | `Repository+fetch.swift:35` | **does not exist** — literally `// TODO: Implement pull` |
| push | `Repository/Repository+push.swift:22` | `public nonisolated func push(remote: Remote? = nil, createsRefspec: Bool = true) async throws(SwiftGitXError)` |
| checkout | `Repository/Repository+checkout.swift:27, :43` | `public func checkout(to reference: any Reference) throws(SwiftGitXError)` / `public func checkout(to commit: Commit) throws(SwiftGitXError)` — updates worktree only, **not HEAD** |
| switch | `Repository/Repository+switch.swift:33, :58, :74` | `public func \`switch\`(to branch: Branch)` / `(to tag: Tag)` / `(to commit: Commit)`, all `throws(SwiftGitXError)`. Remote branch → auto-creates local tracking branch (`createTrackingBranch`, `:100`) |
| remotes | `Collections/RemoteCollection.swift:24,:33,:46,:62,:76` | `subscript(name: String) -> Remote?`, `get(named:) throws -> Remote`, `list() throws -> [Remote]`, `add(named:at:) throws -> Remote`, `remove(_:) throws` |
| branches | `Collections/BranchCollection.swift:19,:24,:35,:61,:71,:87,:131,:181,:206,:236` | `var local: BranchSequence`, `var remote: BranchSequence`, `var current: Branch` (throwing getter), `subscript(name:type:) -> Branch?`, `get(named:type:)`, `list(_ type: BranchType = .all) throws -> [Branch]`, `create(named:target:force:)`, `delete(_:)`, `rename(_:to:force:)`, `setUpstream(from:to:)` |
| repo entry | `Repository/Repository.swift:176, :232, :257` | `static func open(at: URL) throws -> Repository`; `var branch: BranchCollection`; `var remote: RemoteCollection` |

### Authentication: **NO. SwiftGitX 0.4.0 has zero credential support.**

I grepped the entire `Sources/` tree case-insensitively for `credential|callback|cred_|ssh|token|password|auth`. The **only** hits are: a `transfer_progress` callback used by *clone*, a `git_stash_cb`, doc-comment prose, `Commit.author`, and one error enum case. There is no `git_remote_callbacks`, no `git_credential_*`, no `RemoteCallbacks` type, no `git_fetch_options`, no `git_push_options` anywhere.

The smoking guns are the two network calls themselves — both pass `nil` for the options struct that would carry callbacks:

```swift
// Repository+fetch.swift:30-32
try git(operation: .fetch) {
    git_remote_fetch(remotePointer, nil, nil, nil)   // 3rd arg = git_fetch_options* → NULL
}
```
```swift
// Repository+push.swift:49-51
try git(operation: .push) {
    git_remote_push(remotePointer, nil, nil)          // 3rd arg = git_push_options*  → NULL
}
```

Also note both are marked `// TODO: Implement options as parameter` (`Repository+fetch.swift:19`) and `// TODO: Implement options of these methods` (`Repository+push.swift:21`) — options are an acknowledged gap, not an oversight you can work around from outside. `Repository.pointer` is internal, so you also can't reach in and drive `git_remote_fetch` yourself through a SwiftGitX `Repository`. (`GitGraph.swift` and `GitDiffStats.swift` already had to open their *own* raw `git_repository` for exactly this reason — see the comment at `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GitProvider.swift:7-11`.)

**What that means concretely, per transport:**

- **HTTPS: broken.** libgit2 requires the credentials callback. `libgit2/src/libgit2/transports/http.c:130-157` — `handle_auth()` only produces a credential if the URL embedded one, or `if (error > 0 && callback)`. Callback is NULL ⇒ `GIT_EAUTH`. Private HTTPS remotes will fail 100% of the time. No credential-helper integration exists in libgit2 at all beyond the callback (`credential_helpers.c` is just a userpass payload shim you must wire in yourself).
- **SSH: likely works anyway, by accident of build config.** `libgit2/Package.swift:99-101`:
  ```swift
  // SSH transport (exec-based, uses system ssh command)
  .define("GIT_SSH", to: "1", .when(platforms: [.macOS, .iOS, .linux, .android])),
  .define("GIT_SSH_EXEC", to: "1", .when(platforms: [.macOS, .iOS, .linux, .android])),
  ```
  With `GIT_SSH_EXEC`, `transports/ssh_exec.c` `exec`s the real `ssh` binary (`ssh_exec.c:154` reads `$GIT_SSH`) — so keys, `~/.ssh/config`, and ssh-agent are handled by ssh itself and never touch libgit2's credential machinery. `ssh_exec.c` contains **no** credential references. Caveat: this depends on `ssh` being resolvable and on the app's sandbox/entitlements permitting the exec + agent socket, and `libssh2` is also compiled in (`ssh_libssh2.c` present) — worth an empirical test before betting on it.
- **`GIT_HTTPS=1`** (`libgit2/Package.swift:103`) so TLS itself is fine (SecureTransport/CommonCrypto on macOS). It's purely the *credential* layer that's missing.

**Verdict:** authenticated push/fetch through SwiftGitX is **not possible for HTTPS remotes** without either forking/patching SwiftGitX, or dropping to raw libgit2 with your own `git_remote_callbacks.credentials` (you already link libgit2 directly, so this is available — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/LibGit2.swift` owns the single `git_libgit2_init`). `checkout`/`switch`/branch listing/remote listing are purely local and fully usable as-is.

# 3. `StatusCommandRunner`

`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift` (250 lines).

I grepped the entire `Sources/` tree case-insensitively for `credential|callback|cred_|ssh|token|password|auth`. The smoking guns are the two network calls themselves — both pass `nil` for the options struct that would carry callbacks:

```swift
// Repository+fetch.swift:30-32
try git(operation: .fetch) {
    git_remote_fetch(remotePointer, nil, nil, nil)   // 3rd arg = git_fetch_options* → NULL
}
```
```swift
// Repository+push.swift:49-51
try git(operation: .push) {
    git_remote_push(remotePointer, nil, nil)          // 3rd arg = git_push_options*  → NULL
}
```

Also note both are marked `// TODO: Implement options as parameter` (`Repository+fetch.swift:19`) and `// TODO: Implement options of these methods` (`Repository+push.swift:21`) — options are an acknowledged gap, not an oversight you can work around from outside. `Repository.pointer` is internal, so you also can't reach in and drive `git_remote_fetch` yourself through a SwiftGitX `Repository`. (`GitGraph.swift` and `GitDiffStats.swift` already had to open their *own* raw `git_repository` for exactly this reason — see the comment at `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GitProvider.swift:7-11`.)

**What that means concretely, per transport:**

- **HTTPS: broken.** libgit2 requires the credentials callback. `libgit2/src/libgit2/transports/http.c:130-157` — `handle_auth()` only produces a credential if the URL embedded one, or `if (error > 0 && callback)`. Callback is NULL ⇒ `GIT_EAUTH`. Private HTTPS remotes will fail 100% of the time. No credential-helper integration exists in libgit2 at all beyond the callback (`credential_helpers.c` is just a userpass payload shim you must wire in yourself).
- **SSH: likely works anyway, by accident of build config.** `libgit2/Package.swift:99-101`:
  ```swift
  // SSH transport (exec-based, uses system ssh command)
  .define("GIT_SSH", to: "1", .when(platforms: [.macOS, .iOS, .linux, .android])),
  .define("GIT_SSH_EXEC", to: "1", .when(platforms: [.macOS, .iOS, .linux, .android])),
  ```
  With `GIT_SSH_EXEC`, `transports/ssh_exec.c` `exec`s the real `ssh` binary (`ssh_exec.c:154` reads `$GIT_SSH`) — so keys, `~/.ssh/config`, and ssh-agent are handled by ssh itself and never touch libgit2's credential machinery. `ssh_exec.c` contains **no** credential references. - **`GIT_HTTPS=1`** (`libgit2/Package.swift:103`) so TLS itself is fine (SecureTransport/CommonCrypto on macOS). It's purely the *credential* layer that's missing.

**Verdict:** authenticated push/fetch through SwiftGitX is **not possible for HTTPS remotes** without either forking/patching SwiftGitX, or dropping to raw libgit2 with your own `git_remote_callbacks.credentials` (you already link libgit2 directly, so this is available — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/LibGit2.swift` owns the single `git_libgit2_init`). `checkout`/`switch`/branch listing/remote listing are purely local and fully usable as-is.

- **Output drain** (`:75-85`, `:139-153`): stdout+stderr drained concurrently on `DispatchQueue.global()` *while the process runs* (deadlock avoidance); `readCapped` retains ≤ `maxBytes` but keeps reading to EOF; uses throwing `read(upToCount:)` not `availableData` (the latter throws an uncatchable ObjC exception after `terminate()`).

### The "deterministic /etc/paths.d floor + `$SHELL -ilc` probe" mechanism

**Type name: `enum ShellEnvironment` — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ShellEnvironment.swift:26`** (424 lines).

- Doc explaining the two unequal layers: `:5-25`
- **The floor**: `static func floorPath(etcPaths: String = "/etc/paths", etcPathsD: String = "/etc/paths.d", inherited: String? = …) -> String` — `:84-111`. Reads `/etc/paths`, then every file in `/etc/paths.d` sorted, then `wellKnownExtras` (`:71-76`: `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/sbin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.local/bin`), then the inherited PATH; dedupes first-wins; falls back to `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` if empty. No subprocess.
- **The probe**: `static func probe(shell: String = loginShell(), timeout: TimeInterval = 3) -> Result<[String: String], ProbeFailure>` — `:176-232`. Runs `$SHELL -lic` (POSIX shells only, allowlist at `:40`; else `/bin/sh -lc`) with a script that brackets a raw `env -0` stream between two copies of a per-probe UUID (`:180-182`). Spawned with the *minimal* PATH `probeSpawnPath = "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin"` (`:158`) so `path_helper` composes Homebrew in the right *position*. cwd = home (`:190`), stdin = `/dev/null`. `ProbeFailure` enum at `:127-133`.
- `static func merge(probed:floor:)` — `:264-278` (probed base, denylist removed, `appOverrides` last, PATH unioned with floor).
- Two views: `static func path() -> String` (`:285-287`, used by `StatusCommandRunner`) and `static func environment() -> [String: String]` (`:292-298`, for user scripts). `static func refresh(shell:)` single-flight cache refresh at `:309-336`.
- `appOverrides = ["GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0", "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS": "0"]` — `:146-149`.
- Called at startup: `macapp/WorkroomApp/WorkroomApp.swift:23` (floor) and `:33` (background probe). Tests: `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/ShellEnvironmentTests.swift` (20 KB, incl. the `/etc/paths.d/postgresapp` regression at `:105`).

---

# 4. `gh` (GitHub CLI) — yes, extensive precedent

All via `StatusCommandRunning` (default `StatusCommandRunner`), field `let runner: StatusCommandRunning` at `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:34`, with a separate network budget `var ciTimeout: TimeInterval` (`:36`, default 10s vs 3s local).

| file:line | command |
|---|---|
| `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:194-200` | `gh api graphql -f query=<statusCheckRollup>` |
| `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:209-211` | `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner -q .nameWithOwner` |
| `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:249-255` | `gh pr list --head … --state all --limit 1 --json …` |
| `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:278-281` | `gh pr checks <number> --json name,state,bucket,link,workflow` |
| `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:295-297` | `gh api graphql -f query=<reviewURLQuery>` |
| `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:405-407` | **`func runPRCommand(_ arguments: [String], in dir: String) async -> CommandResult` — "Run a mutating `gh pr …` command (Phase 2b PR actions)"** |
| `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:426-428` | `gh auth status --active --json hosts` (run in `NSTemporaryDirectory()`) |

This is your strongest precedent: **the app already performs authenticated, network-touching, *mutating* operations by shelling out to a binary and letting that binary own the credentials** (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:168-169`: "Everything goes through the authenticated `gh` token, so private repos work with no extra config"). Two supporting pieces you'd reuse directly:

- `static func ghProbeDirectory(path:vcs:projectRoot:) -> String` — `:364-366`: `vcs == "jj" ? projectRoot : path`. A jj workspace has no `.git`, so network commands must run from the colocated project root. Fetch/push will need exactly the same rule.
- `resolveGitHubCLI()` / `classifyGitHubCLI` (`:425-444`) — the "is the tool installed and authenticated" UX pattern (127 ⇒ not installed, timeout ⇒ don't cry wolf), directly transferable to a `git`-auth precondition check.

---

# 5. `vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/src/jj_backend.rs` — existing mutation path

`snapshot_working_copy` (`:592-680`) is the **only** write path. Everything else is read-only and explicitly documented so (`:6`, `lib.rs:41-45`). Public surface is 4 reads + 1 mutating read: `log_page` (`:349`), `current_ref` (`:418`), `working_status` (`:686`, the mutating one), `changeset` (`:736`) — mirrored in `crates/wr-vcs-core/src/lib.rs:31-51` and UniFFI-exported at `crates/wr-vcs-uniffi/src/lib.rs:308-345` (only 5 `#[uniffi::export]` fns exist).

**Mutation machinery already imported and exercised** — the full transaction dance is present in `snapshot_working_copy:616-679`:

```rust
let mut locked_ws = pollster::block_on(workspace.start_working_copy_mutation())?;   // :616
let freshness = pollster::block_on(WorkingCopyFreshness::check_stale(
    locked_ws.locked_wc(), &wc_commit, &repo))?;                                    // :623-628
let (new_tree, _stats) = pollster::block_on(locked_ws.locked_wc().snapshot(&options))?; // :659
let mut tx = repo.start_transaction();                                              // :663
tx.set_is_snapshot(true);                                                           // :664
let write = tx.repo_mut().rewrite_commit(&wc_commit).set_tree(new_tree).write();     // :665-669
pollster::block_on(tx.repo_mut().rebase_descendants())?;                            // :671
let new_repo = pollster::block_on(tx.commit("snapshot working copy"))?;              // :672
pollster::block_on(locked_ws.finish(new_repo.op_id().clone()))?;                     // :673
```

So `start_transaction` / `repo_mut()` (→ `&mut MutableRepo`) / `rewrite_commit` / `rebase_descendants` / `tx.commit` / `locked_ws.finish` are all already in use. Plus the safety scaffolding you'd want to reuse: `lock_is_held` (`:567-582`, non-blocking `FileLock::try_lock` fail-fast → `VcsError::LockContention`) and the `WorkingCopyFreshness` staleness guard (`:629-649` → `VcsError::StaleSnapshot`). Swift side gates this per project root with `JJSnapshotGate` (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:37-39, :141-148`).

**Not imported:** nothing from `jj_lib::git`. Imports are `jj_backend.rs:18-43` (backend, commit, config, conflicts, copies, diff, gitignore, local_working_copy, lock, matchers, merge, repo, revset, settings, tree_merge, working_copy, workspace). No `jj_lib::git::{GitFetch, push_refs, import_refs, export_refs}`.

**Good news for feasibility — jj-lib 0.43.0 does network git via a `git` subprocess, so auth is free:**
`~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git.rs`:
- `pub struct GitFetch<'a>` (`:2983`), `GitFetch::new(mut_repo: &'a mut MutableRepo, subprocess_options: GitSubprocessOptions, import_options: &'a GitImportOptions)` (`:2992`), `pub fn fetch(&mut self, remote_name: &RemoteName, ExpandedFetchRefSpecs{…}, callback: &mut dyn GitSubprocessCallback, depth: Option<NonZeroU32>, fetch_tags_override: Option<FetchTagsOverride>) -> Result<(), GitFetchError>` (`:3015`), `pub async fn import_refs(&mut self)` (`:3119`)
- `pub fn push_refs(mut_repo: &mut MutableRepo, subprocess_options: GitSubprocessOptions, remote: &RemoteName, targets: &GitPushRefTargets, callback: &mut dyn GitSubprocessCallback, options: &GitPushOptions) -> Result<GitPushStats, GitPushError>` (`:3191`)
- Also `remove_remote` (`:2371`), `rename_remote` (`:2443`), `set_remote_urls` (`:2559`), `export_refs` (`:1245`), `import_refs` (`:566`)
- `pub struct GitSubprocessOptions { pub executable_path: PathBuf, pub environment: HashMap<OsString, OsString> }` (`git.rs:127-134`) — with the comment: *"Used by consumers of jj-lib to set environment variables like GIT_ASKPASS (for authentication callbacks) or GIT_TRACE"*. `git_subprocess.rs:48` pins `MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION = "2.41.0"`; `git_subprocess.rs:101` is `Command::new(&self.options.executable_path)`.

So the jj side gets SSH keys, credential helpers and HTTPS tokens for free (real `git` does the auth), and you get an explicit hook to inject `GIT_ASKPASS`. This is a striking asymmetry with the git/SwiftGitX side, which has no auth at all.

---

# 6. Existing tests to extend

**Swift (`macapp/WorkroomAppTests/`)** — pattern: real throwaway repos under `NSTemporaryDirectory()`, built by shelling real `git`/`jj` via a local `sh(_:in:)` helper, removed in `tearDown`. **No golden files.** Missing tool = hard `XCTFail`, not a skip.

- `VCSProviderConformanceTests.swift` (31 KB) — **the one to extend.** Cross-backend parity on a colocated jj+git repo. Helpers: `requireTool(_:)` `:459`, `colocatedFixture()` `:476`, `sh(_:in:)` `:616`; `tearDown` `:16-20`. Tests at `:22`, `:65` (documents the one sanctioned divergence), `:105`.
- `WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.swift` — real repos through the **real** `StatusCommandRunner` (`:16`: `let resolver = WorkroomStatusResolver()  // real StatusCommandRunner`). Helpers `tool(_:)` `:26`, `requireTool(_:)` `:33`, `tempDir()` `:40`, `sh(_:in:)` `:48` (pins `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null`, `PATH = ShellEnvironment.path()`).
- `BranchResolverTests.swift` — pure-unit pattern: `private struct StubProvider: VCSProviding` at `:7-23` with a closure-injected `currentRef`, injected via `BranchResolver(timeout:makeProvider:)` `:32`. **This is the seam to copy if you add fetch/push/switch to `VCSProviding`** — but note every stub conformer (this one, plus stubs inside `DiffResolverTests.swift`, `FileTreeTests.swift`, `HistoryModelTests.swift`) must gain the new members unless you give them protocol-extension defaults (there are already two such defaults at `VCSProviding.swift:55-64`).
- `DiffResolverTests.swift` (16.6 KB), `DiffResolverFileContentTests.swift`, `DiffResolverOldFileContentTests.swift` — resolver-level tests.
- `GitGraphTests.swift` (`sh` at `:36`), `GitCommitDiffTests.swift`, `GitProviderCoAuthorsTests.swift`, `VCSCommitTests.swift`, `JJSnapshotGateTests.swift`, `StatusCommandRunnerTests.swift` (real shell tools, no repo — the drain/timeout/SIGKILL/cancel guarantees), `FileTreeTests.swift` (fake runner keyed by executable name: `"git": CommandResult(…)` at `:93`, `:101`).

**Rust (`vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/tests/`)** — same philosophy: real throwaway jj repos built with the `jj` CLI.
- `common/mod.rs` — the skip policy. `skip_without(tools:what:)` `:52`, and the deliberately-loud `#[test] fn jj_is_on_path()` `:66-75` compiled into every test binary so a machine without `jj` can never show green. Read its 33-line module doc before adding a file.
- `working_status.rs` (11 tests) — the mutation-path test, closest analogue for a new write op. Fixture: `jj(args:dir:config:)` `:20` (per-`Command` `JJ_CONFIG`, never `set_var`, because cargo runs tests in parallel threads of one process), `init_repo(tag:)` `:31-49` (unique temp dir + isolated jjconfig with an author so snapshot ops can commit + `jj git init`), `parent_id` `:52`.
- `push_state.rs` (7), `line_stats.rs` (11), `log_order.rs` (8), `error_taxonomy.rs` (5). Unit tests for `probe_repo` inline at `crates/wr-vcs-core/src/lib.rs:53-125` with a `scratch(tag:)` helper (`:62`, no `tempfile` dev-dep by policy).

---

# Feasibility summary

- **Branch listing + switching (git): easy.** Fully supported locally by SwiftGitX — `branch.list(_:)`, `branch.local`/`.remote`, `switch(to:)` incl. auto tracking-branch creation. Purely local, no auth. Add to `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`) and implement in `GitProvider` (`GitProvider.swift:17`) using the existing `runBlocking { Repository.open(at: root) … }` shape (`GitProvider.swift:78-99`).
- **Fetch/push (git): the hard part.** SwiftGitX's `fetch`/`push` exist but pass `nil` options, so there is **no** credential path — HTTPS will fail on anything private; SSH probably works only because libgit2 was built with `GIT_SSH_EXEC`. `pull` doesn't exist at all. Realistic options: (a) shell `git fetch/push` through `StatusCommandRunner` — exactly the `gh` precedent, gets credential helpers/SSH/tokens for free, needs `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` relaxed or `GIT_ASKPASS` supplied; (b) raw libgit2 with your own `git_remote_callbacks.credentials` (you already link libgit2 directly and own init via `LibGit2.swift`); (c) fork SwiftGitX.
- **Fetch/push (jj): straightforward and auth-clean.** jj-lib 0.43 already delegates network git to a `git` subprocess (`GitFetch`/`push_refs` + `GitSubprocessOptions.environment` for `GIT_ASKPASS`), and `jj_backend.rs` already contains the whole transaction/lock/staleness pattern these need. Cost is new `wr-vcs-core` fns + new `#[uniffi::export]`s + an xcframework rebuild (`vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh`).
- **Cross-cutting:** any network op must respect `ghProbeDirectory`'s rule (jj → colocated project root), and jj writes must go through `JJSnapshotGate` per project root.

## Feature
A new 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector needs this data + actions:
- List of branches (git) / bookmarks (jj) for a workroom, so the user can pick one and switch to it.
- Current branch (already available).
- Ahead/behind counts vs the upstream/origin tracking ref.
- Last-fetch timestamp ("last fetched 9 minutes ago").
- Actions: fetch, push to origin, pull from origin with rebase, switch branch.

## Established facts from exploration (trust these)

`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16` — `VCSProviding` protocol, 8 requirements, all READ-ONLY, no branch listing, no mutation, no network. Two defaulted members at `:55-64` (`commitParentFileContent`, `workingBaseFileContent` default to nil) — precedent for adding defaulted members so existing stub conformers in tests don't all break.
`VCSProviding.swift:67` — `enum VCS` with `repoKind(at:)` (`:70`) and `provider(for:)` (`:87`) routing `jj*` → `RustJJProvider`, `plainGit` → `GitProvider`.

`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GitProvider.swift:17` — `struct GitProvider: VCSProviding`, SwiftGitX 0.4.0. Has a NON-protocol `func workingStatus(root:) throws -> GitWorkingStatus` at `:271`; `GitProvider.swift:466-477` has a comment saying the Git-shaped working status "unifies onto a shared VCSProviding.workingStatus in the follow-on".
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/RustJJProvider.swift:6` — `struct RustJJProvider: VCSProviding`, `import WrVcs` (UniFFI). Non-protocol `workingStatus(root:) throws -> WorkroomStatus` at `:70`. Private `static func run(_ exe:_ args:cwd:timeout:) async throws -> String` at `:232` shells `jj` via `StatusCommandRunner` for 4 things jj-lib doesn't expose well.

CRITICAL AUTH FINDING: SwiftGitX 0.4.0's `fetch`/`push` pass NULL for the options struct (`Repository+fetch.swift:30-32`, `Repository+push.swift:49-51`) so there is ZERO credential support — HTTPS auth is impossible through it; `pull` doesn't exist (`// TODO: Implement pull`). SwiftGitX's LOCAL ops are fine: `branch.list(_ type:) throws -> [Branch]` (`Collections/BranchCollection.swift:87`), `branch.local`/`.remote` sequences, `branch.current`, `switch(to: Branch)` (`Repository+switch.swift:33`, auto-creates a local tracking branch for a remote branch via `createTrackingBranch`), `remote.list()`.

Precedent for shelling out to network-touching binaries: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift` already runs `gh` for CI/PR data (`:194`, `:209`, `:249`, `:278`, `:295`) INCLUDING a mutating helper `runPRCommand(_ arguments:in:) -> CommandResult` at `:405`, and `gh auth status` at `:426` with `classifyGitHubCLI` at `:425-444` (exit 127 ⇒ not installed, timeout ⇒ don't cry wolf). It also already shells `git` at `:379` (`rev-parse HEAD`) and `:394` (`symbolic-ref`), with `static let gitHardening = ["-c", "core.fsmonitor="]` at `:63`. `FileTree.swift:162` shells `git ls-files`.

`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift` — `protocol StatusCommandRunning` (`:24`) with `func run(_ executable:_ args:in directory:timeout:) async -> CommandResult`; `CommandResult` (`:9`) has `stdout/stderr/exitCode/timedOut/ok`, sentinels `commandNotFound = 127`, `gitFatal = 128`. Launches via `/usr/bin/env` (`:45`), PATH from `ShellEnvironment.path()` (`:49-57`), and sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` + `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` unconditionally (also in `ShellEnvironment.appOverrides`, `ShellEnvironment.swift:146-149`). Three-layer timeout: SIGTERM at +timeout, SIGKILL tree at +timeout+2, bounded 2s drain.
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/Timeout.swift:65` — `runBlocking(qos:_:)` GCD helper; `:21` `withTimeout(seconds:_:)`. Blocking libgit2/jj-lib reads MUST use `runBlocking`, never the cooperative pool (a past bug: "History pane loads forever").
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/JJSnapshotGate.swift:39` — `actor JJSnapshotGate`, `.shared`, `run<T>(projectRoot:_:)`, serializes MUTATING jj ops per project root.
`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/LibGit2.swift:20` — `enum LibGit2`, sole `git_libgit2_init` owner, `static func withRepository<T>(_ root: URL, _ body: (OpaquePointer) -> T?) -> T?` at `:32`. libgit2 1.9.2 is linked DIRECTLY too (`macapp/project.yml:40-42`), so raw C calls like `git_graph_ahead_behind` are available. Existing raw-C users: `Core/GitGraph.swift` (revwalk + `git_graph_reachable_from_any`, `originTips` globbing `refs/remotes/origin/*` at `:102-106`), `Core/GitCommitDiff.swift`, `Core/GitDiffStats.swift`.

- Avoid touching the Rust workspace if a CLI shell-out gets the same result — a `make app-vcs` rebuild is expensive.
- Everything must be injectable/testable (the app's whole style is closure-injected seams + stub runners).
- The app is macOS 15+ SwiftUI, Swift 6 strict concurrency (`Sendable`, `@MainActor`).

1. Decide: extend `VCSProviding` vs a NEW separate protocol (e.g. `VCSRemoteOperating` / a `RemoteResolver` service) for branch-list + remote ops. Argue it. Note that adding non-defaulted members to `VCSProviding` breaks 4+ test stub conformers.

For jj, be explicit about bookmark-vs-branch semantics and what "switch" and "pull with rebase" even mean there (`jj edit` vs `jj new`; jj auto-rebases descendants).
4. Where last-fetch time comes from concretely (e.g. `.git/FETCH_HEAD` mtime — and what the jj colocated equivalent path is). State the failure mode when it's never been fetched.
5. The service/store layer: a new resolver or model class, its debounce/TTL, how results reach SwiftUI, how it's refreshed (existing FSEvents watchers? a timer for the relative "9 minutes ago" text?), and how in-flight fetch/push state is represented (so the UI can show a spinner and disable the button).

7. Test plan: which existing files to extend, what new files, and what's a unit test vs a real-repo integration test.
8. Sequencing: what's phase 1 (minimum to light up the UI) vs later.

### Reusable chrome
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TitlebarBars.swift:75-84` `TitlebarDivider` — `Rectangle().fill(tokens.border).frame(width: 1, height: 14).padding(.horizontal, 4)`; used in `LeadingTitlebarBar` (`:111`), `TrailingTitlebarBar` (`:157`), `WorkroomSplitView.swift:400,403` — with the rule "only when there's something on both sides".

### Design tokens (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ThemeTokens.swift`, accessed via `ThemeService.shared.tokens`, idiom `private let theme = ThemeService.shared`)
`bg`/`fg`; `panel` (bg +5.5% fg — title bar, tab bar, activity bar); `fgMuted` (fg@0.65) / `fgDim` (fg@0.40); `surface` (fg@0.08 — section header background, segmented track, selected row); `border` (fg@0.12 — hairlines, dividers, brackets); `hover` (fg@0.06); `rowHover`/`rowSelection` (OPAQUE); `accent`/`accentSoft`/`accentForeground`; `warning`/`failure`/`conflict`; `diffAddFg`/`diffRemoveFg` (+`…Bg` @0.16). `ThemeService.shared.tokens`, `generation`, posts `.themeDidChange`.
Typography: section header title `.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)`; header icon glyphs `.system(size: 11)`; row filename `.callout`; metadata `.system(.caption, design: .monospaced)` + `.tertiary`; ref pills `.caption` / `.caption2`; counts `.caption.monospacedDigit()`.
Geometry: section body inset `.padding(12)`; body rhythm `VStack(spacing: 10)`; header inset `.padding(.horizontal, 12).padding(.vertical, 8)`; corner radii 5/6/7/10; bar heights — title bar 28, pane title bar 28, status bar 24, inspector section header 34 (`InspectorPanePolicy.headerHeight`); inspector column width 260–520.
Animations `.easeOut(0.12)` hover / `.easeInOut(0.12)` / `.easeInOut(0.2)` / `.easeInOut(0.22)`, all gated on `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)`.

### Non-negotiable conventions
Every control needs `.help(...)` + `.accessibilityLabel(...)` + a stable `.accessibilityIdentifier(...)`. Interactive glyphs need their own `.onHover` (so `.help`'s tracking area installs) AND `.contentShape(Rectangle())`. Active state must be signalled by position/brightness, not hue alone. Formatting: `.swift-format`, 2-space indent, 100 columns; run `make app-format` / `make app-lint`; `make app-generate` (xcodegen) after adding any new `.swift` file.

### Known traps (from hard-won project memory — respect these)
- A SwiftUI window-`toolbar` item's overflow `menuFormRepresentation` caused a 2s AppHang; the window toolbar is kept an EMPTY AppKit `NSToolbar`. So this new "toolbar" must be a plain SwiftUI view INSIDE the inspector, never a `.toolbar` modifier.
- `.textSelection(.enabled)` text swallows real mouseDown so SwiftUI taps don't fire (real-mouse-only bug; synthetic XCUITest clicks pass on buggy code).
- `.onHover` controls are NOT drivable from XCUITest; an accessibility id on an `NSViewRepresentable` wrapper is not queryable.
- `@Default` invalidates SwiftUI ASYNCHRONOUSLY — use `@State` for click-immediate UI.
- Pixel-perfect alignment is expected — fix by construction (uniform insets, centered icons), don't eyeball.
- Joel wants XCUITest coverage for new macapp UI, not just unit tests. See `macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/` — and note `make app-uitest` IGNORES `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so scoped runs need a direct `xcodebuild -only-testing:<Class>/<method>`. There's a `UITestFixture` seam (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/UITestFixture.swift`, `isActive`, `static let vcsProvider` at `:630`, `FixtureVCSProvider` at `:636`) — launch arg `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1`.

### Engine reality (a parallel agent is planning this half — assume the data will exist)
Today `VCSProviding` is read-only with NO branch listing, NO fetch/push/pull, NO ahead/behind counts, NO last-fetch time. Assume a new service will provide: a branch/bookmark list, current upstream, ahead/behind counts, a last-fetch `Date?`, and async fetch/push/pull actions with in-flight + error state. Design the UI against a clean injectable view-model/observable and SAY exactly what shape you need from it.

## What I need from you
1. Exact placement decision + how to implement it. Key question: `RightInspector` composes section headers/bodies into an `InspectorSplitView` (an AppKit `NSSplitView` host). Does the toolbar go above the whole split view inside `RightInspector`, or inside `InspectorColumn`? What happens with the `.files` activity section (should the toolbar show there too, or only for `.changes`)? Give a recommendation.
2. Full view decomposition: new file(s) under `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/`, the segment sub-views, the divider approach, exact heights/insets/fonts/tokens so it matches the screenshot AND the app's existing look. Two-line segments in a ~30-40pt bar is tight — give real numbers.
3. The branch dropdown: `Menu` vs a custom popover. Consider that a repo can have hundreds of branches (filter field? grouping local vs remote? a "new branch" affordance?). Note the AppHang trap above and whether `Menu`'s lazy content is safe here. Recommend one.
4. The middle segment's state machine: enumerate every state (no remote / no upstream / never fetched / clean / ahead N / behind N / diverged / fetching / pushing / failed) and the exact title+subtitle+badge for each. Include the relative-time formatting approach and how it stays live ("9 minutes ago" must tick).
5. Store/state wiring: where the observable lives (`AppStore`? a new `@Observable`?), how it keys off the inspector target (`AppStore.inspectorTargetID`/`inspectorTarget`, `AppStore.swift:780-781`), and how it avoids doing work when the inspector is hidden (there's an existing precedent: `focusHistoryIfShown()` gated on `inspectorIsVisible && historySectionShown`).
6. Interaction/feedback: hover wells, disabled states, spinner during fetch/push, error presentation (inline? tooltip? the existing `inspectorMessage(_:)` at `ChangesPanel.swift:796-804`?), and whether push/pull needs a confirmation.
7. Layout robustness: the inspector is 260–520pt wide. How do three segments with two-line text degrade at 260pt? Give the truncation/priority rules.
8. Keyboard shortcuts + menu items — should Fetch/Push/Pull get View/VCS menu entries? Note the project memory: every new shortcut MUST also be added to `GhosttySurfaceView.isAppShortcut` or a focused TUI swallows it.
9. Test plan: unit tests (pure state-machine mapping — the app has precedent for pure mapping types like `Core/ChangeBadge.swift` being unit-tested) plus XCUITest coverage, with the fixture seam.
10. Sequencing: phase 1 = minimum shippable, later phases.

Be concrete and opinionated. Give real numbers, not "appropriate spacing".
