## 9. Where your assumptions need correcting

1. **`jj git fetch` passes `--no-write-fetch-head`**, so `FETCH_HEAD` is *not* the jj last-fetch source. (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`; confirmed empirically on your `platform` repo — op-log fetches at 14:44/20:07 vs a `FETCH_HEAD` mtime of 16:57.) Use the op-log scan (§4).
2. **jj's ahead/behind are inverted.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means *the remote is ahead of local* = git's **behind**; `tracking_behind_count()` = git's **ahead**. jj's own default template proves it: `format_tracked_remote_ref_distances` prints `"ahead by N commits"` next to `@origin`. Swap on ingest, comment the swap, pin it with a cross-backend integration test.
3. **`FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree.** A fetch in the project root is invisible to a workroom's `FETCH_HEAD` and vice versa. Run fetch at the project root always — which also makes "last fetched" a per-project fact all workrooms agree on. (`ghProbeDirectory`'s rule extends to git, not just jj, for this one op.)
4. **You don't need a second command for ahead/behind, and you don't need `@{u}`.** `git for-each-ref`'s `%(push:short)`/`%(push:track)` resolve to `<remote>/<same-name>` and its divergence *even with no upstream configured* — verified on your `platform` repo. That's the fallback chain you were going to hand-roll, plus `[gone]`, plus per-row counts for the picker, plus `%(worktreepath)`, plus `%(HEAD)`, in one 30 ms process.
5. **"SwiftGitX's LOCAL ops are fine" does not extend to `switch`.** `Repository.switch(to:)` → `git_checkout_tree` + `git_repository_set_head`, and **libgit2 does not enforce git's "already used by worktree at" guard**. Workroom's entire model is `git worktree add -b`, so a picker offering `main` would happily give you two worktrees on `main` where the CLI refuses. It's also non-atomic (checkout then set-HEAD; a failure between leaves a half-switched repo) and skips the DWIM/hook/submodule behaviour users expect. Shell out.
6. **`Repository.push` silently writes repo config.** Its `addPushRefspec` calls `git_remote_add_push`, persisting `remote.origin.push = refs/heads/x:refs/heads/x` into the repo's config — for every branch you push. Independent of the credentials problem, that alone disqualifies it.
7. **jj workrooms have no bookmark, so git's and jj's Push buttons are not symmetric.** A jj workroom is `jj workspace add --name workroom/<n>` (`internal/vcs/jj.go:30`) — no bookmark is created. So `currentRef.kind == .ancestor` and `jj git push -b <ancestor>` would push the *project's* `master`, not your work. Disable Push with `.nothingToPush` in phase 1; the phase-4 `--named workroom/<n>=@-` is the real fix. A git workroom, by contrast, is a real branch and `push --set-upstream` just works.
8. **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the git import/export lock**, even a read: `jj git remote list` failed with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export … git_import_export.lock"* under the sandbox. So don't reach for `jj git remote list`/`jj git root` in the read path — derive the remote list from `jj bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes (free) and locate the git dir by reading `.jj/repo/store/git_target` (verified: contains `../../../.git` on your colocated `platform` repo). `jj bookmark list --ignore-working-copy` takes no lock.
9. **`SwiftGitX.Branch.init` is eager and expensive** — one `ObjectFactory.lookupObject`, one `git_branch_upstream` that *recursively constructs another `Branch`* (another object lookup), plus a `git_remote_lookup`, **per branch**. `branch.list(.local)` on a 500-branch repo is ~1500 libgit2 object lookups on a blocking thread. Beyond the runner-injection problem, that's a bad way to fill a menu.
10. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocess ops**, and you should say so where you write it or it'll read as a bug. The rule exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, so the gate would release while the abandoned call still held the lock. `StatusCommandRunner` SIGKILLs the process tree at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely gone and the lock genuinely released. Compose `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }` with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Separately: the gate is key-based and backend-agnostic, so if git's `packed-refs.lock` contention shows up in practice, route git remote ops through it too — at which point renaming it (`RepoWriteGate`) costs 3 call sites + `JJSnapshotGateTests.swift`. I'd defer the rename rather than churn it speculatively.
11. **Never auto-fetch.** No TTL-driven, focus-driven, or sweep-driven network call. It burns rate limits, can trigger credential/SSH prompts on a machine nobody's watching, and the existing `refreshWorkroomStatuses` sweep has no business growing a network mutation.

## 5. Service / store layer

### `Core/RemoteStateModel.swift`

A store-owned `@MainActor ObservableObject`, third sibling to `fileTree` (`AppStore:400`) and `commitHistory` (`AppStore:407`). Modelled on `HistoryModel` — same `State` enum, same **0.3 s pre-dispatch trailing debounce**, same cancel-and-replace, same `awaitCurrentLoad()` test hook.

```swift
@MainActor final class RemoteStateModel: ObservableObject {
  enum State: Equatable { case idle, loading, loaded, failed(String); var isSettled: Bool { … } }

  struct Target: Equatable, Sendable {
    let sid: SidebarID
    let path: String
    let vcs: String
    let projectRoot: String
  }

  @Published private(set) var snapshot: VCSRemoteState?
  @Published private(set) var state: State = .idle
  /// The single in-flight action, or nil. Drives both the spinner (on the matching button) and the
  /// disable (on ALL of them) — one action at a time per model, so a click can't double-fire and
  /// Push can't race Pull.
  @Published private(set) var inFlight: VCSRemoteAction?
  /// The last action failure, for an inline banner. Cleared on the next action or refresh. Kept
  /// SEPARATE from `state`: a failed push must not blank a good snapshot (the `keepPrior` rule).
  @Published private(set) var lastFailure: VCSRemoteFailure?

  private(set) var target: Target?
  /// Wired by the store post-init (the `lazy var workroomFileWatcher` idiom) so the model needs no
  /// AppStore to be unit-tested. Fires on every SUCCESSFUL mutation.
  var onDidMutate: (@MainActor (VCSRemoteAction) -> Void)?

  init(resolver: VCSRemoteResolver = VCSRemoteResolver(),
       debounce: TimeInterval = 0.3,
       ttl: TimeInterval = 15)

  func focus(_ target: Target?)          // re-point; no-op if unchanged; clears on nil
  func activate(_ target: Target?)       // the panel's `.task`: refresh on settled re-entry
  func refresh(force: Bool = false)      // TTL-gated unless forced
  func awaitCurrentLoad() async
  func perform(_ action: VCSRemoteAction)
  func switchTo(_ ref: VCSBranchRef)

  // Derived, pure-ish, so the view holds no policy
  var canFetch: Bool  // primaryRemote != nil && inFlight == nil
  var canPush: Bool   // + jj: current.kind == .branch  (§9.7)
  var canPull: Bool   // + tracking?.comparedTo != nil && !gone
}
```

**TTL = 15 s**, matching `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:14`'s `localStatusTTL`. Justified: the whole read is *local* — one `for-each-ref` / one `bookmark list`, no network — so it's the same cost class as the local status probe. (`ciStatusTTL = 300` is for network reads; nothing here is one.)

**Refresh triggers — reuse the existing watchers, add none:**

1. **Selection change** → `focus(...)`, debounced 0.3 s (`AppStore.selectedTargetID.didSet`).
2. **The existing per-project `.git`/`.jj` FSEvents watcher.** `rootBranchWatchers` (`AppStore:2307-2331`) already watches `vcsMetadataDir(path:vcs:)` **recursively**. That single watcher per project covers everything this feature cares about, for every workroom of that project:
   - git fetch → `<project>/.git/FETCH_HEAD` + `refs/remotes/*` ✓
   - git switch in a workroom → `<project>/.git/worktrees/<n>/HEAD` ✓ (inside the watched tree)
   - git commit/push → `refs/heads/*`, `packed-refs`, `logs/` ✓
   - jj anything → `<project>/.jj/repo/op_heads` + `op_store` ✓ (a workroom's `.jj/repo` is a *file* pointing there — verified on `/Users/joelmoss/workrooms/light-star`)

   So: in `handleRootBranchChange(projectID:)`, right beside the existing `commitHistory.refresh()` block, add a visibility-gated `remoteState.refresh(force: true)`. Zero new watchers, zero new FSEvents cost.
3. **After a successful action** → `onDidMutate` → the store does `remoteState.refresh(force: true)` + `refreshWorkroomStatuses(force: true)` (the dirty/conflict badge after switch/pull) + `commitHistory.refresh()` (new commits after pull). The watcher would eventually do this anyway, but its coalesce window is ~1 s and the UI should feel instant. Belt and braces.

**Visibility gate.** Copy `focusHistoryIfShown()` (`AppStore:337`) verbatim in spirit:

called from `selectedTargetID.didSet`, `activeInspectorSection.didSet`, and `refreshSelectionHasTabs()` — the same three sites `focusHistoryIfShown` uses. This matters for the same reason it mattered for History: without it, every selection change spawns a process for a toolbar nobody can see.

Add `UITestFixture.remoteState` beside `rootStatus`/`workroomStatus`, and make the actions no-op-with-optimistic-update (the `performPRAction` fixture branch, `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:190`).

**The relative "9 minutes ago" text: no timer in the engine.**

Wrap only the timestamp `Text` in `TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: 30))` and call the pure `VCSRemoteResolver.lastFetchLabel(snapshot.lastFetch, now: context.date)`. That gets you: self-updating copy, redraws confined to that one `Text`, automatic pause when off-screen, no `Task`/`Timer` lifecycle to leak, and a pure unit-testable formatter. A `@Published var clock` on the model would re-render every observer every 30 s for a string; a `@Published` on `AppStore` would re-render `RootView`. Don't.

**Cross-window.** `AppStore` is per-window, so two windows showing the same project each have their own `inFlight`. The real serialization is `JJSnapshotGate.shared` (process-global, keyed by project root) for jj; for git, two concurrent `git fetch` on the same `.git` contend on `packed-refs.lock` → `.locked` → the UI offers Retry. Acceptable in phase 1; if it shows up, widen the gate (§9.10).

---

## 6. Error surfacing

`static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?` — one pure function, `nil` for success. Ordered checks, matched against strings I verified in the git 2.55 binary on this machine:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| `r.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing("git"/"jj")` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| stderr ∋ `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username` \| `could not read Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired(stderr)` |
| stderr ∋ `'…' is already used by worktree at '…'` (also legacy `already checked out`) | `.alreadyCheckedOut(path:)` |
| stderr ∋ `Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten` \| `The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree(stderr)` |
| stderr ∋ `There is no tracking information for the current branch.` | `.noUpstream` |
| stderr ∋ `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| `no such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| stderr ∋ `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected(stderr)` |
| stderr ∋ `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists` \| `Unable to create`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<gitdir>/rebase-merge` or `rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other(trimmed stderr, else stdout, else "…exited N")` |

**Deliberately a new enum, not `VCSError`.** `VCSError`'s seven cases are the *backend read* taxonomy and `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)` (`:90`) switches over them exhaustively to pick a sidebar badge. `.authRequired` has no sidebar badge; adding it would force an arbitrary answer in a function that currently has a principled one for every case. Same reasoning that put `CIResolution`/`PRResolution` beside their resolver instead of in `VCSModels.swift`. **Do** reuse the `CommandResult.commandNotFound`/`gitFatal` sentinels (`StatusCommandRunner:15-17`).

**Surfacing policy:**
- **A failed action never blanks a good snapshot.** `lastFailure` is a separate `@Published`; `snapshot` is untouched. Exactly the `.keepPrior` philosophy already in `applyCIStatus`/`applyPRStatus`.
- Hard failures also raise the store's existing alert (`errorTitle`/`errorMessage`), the `performPRAction:210` pattern: `"Couldn't fetch"` + trimmed stderr, or a hand-written line for the cases where raw stderr is unhelpful:
  - `.authRequired` → "Git couldn't authenticate. Workroom never prompts for credentials — configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`) or use SSH." **This is your #1 failure mode and it needs bespoke copy.** `StatusCommandRunner:53` sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` unconditionally, and a GUI app has no tty, so HTTPS-without-a-helper fails instantly. That's correct behaviour (never hang), but the raw stderr is baffling.
  - `.toolMissing` → "`git` isn't on Workroom's PATH." Note the app *already* hard-requires both binaries — the Go CLI shells `git worktree add` (`internal/vcs/git.go:29`) and `jj workspace add` (`internal/vcs/jj.go:30`) to create a workroom at all — so this is a real-but-already-fatal condition, not a new dependency. That's also the argument that settles §9.4: no libgit2 fallback needed.
  - `.rebaseInProgress` → "A rebase is in progress in this workroom. Run `git rebase --abort` (or `--continue`) in its terminal." **Do not offer Retry** — it will fail identically.
  - `.nothingToPush` (jj) → "`@` has no bookmark, so there's nothing to push. Set one first."
  - `.alreadyCheckedOut` → "`<branch>` is already checked out in `<path>`."
- **`.timedOut(.pull)` is the dangerous one.** SIGKILLing `git fetch` mid-transfer is safe (git is crash-safe; worst case a stale `objects/pack/tmp_*`). SIGKILLing `git pull --rebase` is **not** — it can leave `rebase-merge/` behind. Hence the generous 300 s budget, and the post-failure `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` probe that upgrades `.timedOut` to `.rebaseInProgress` so the message tells the truth.
- **jj conflicts are not errors.** `jj rebase` exits 0 having written conflicts into commits. So after a jj pull, `classify` returns `nil` and you must ask the working copy: the `onDidMutate` → `refreshWorkroomStatuses(force: true)` already re-reads `WorkroomStatus.conflicted` through `RustJJProvider.workingStatus`. Return `.okWithConflicts` when that comes back conflicted, and lean on jj's `jj undo` in the copy ("Undo in the terminal with `jj undo`") — jj's recovery story here is genuinely better than git's and worth saying out loud.
- `.rejected` → the toast/banner offers **Pull**, never Force.

---

Copy `MockStatusRunner` and `RecordingStatusRunner` from `WorkroomStatusResolverTests.swift:7-41` (they're `private` there; duplication across test files is already this suite's convention).

## 8. Sequencing

**Phase 1 — read-only + Fetch (lights up all three toolbar segments)**
1. Models into `VCSModels.swift`.
2. `Core/VCSRemoteResolver.swift`: `resolveState` for both backends (one process each) + last-fetch + all pure parsers/arg-builders + `classify` + `opDirectory`.
3. `Core/RemoteStateModel.swift`: focus/activate/refresh/debounce/TTL, `inFlight`, `lastFailure`.
4. Store wiring in `AppStore.swift`: `let remoteState`, `onDidMutate`, `remoteToolbarShown`, `focusRemoteStateIfShown()` at the three call sites, the `handleRootBranchChange` hook, fixture seed.
5. `fetch` only. It's the sole non-destructive mutation, it's what makes the timestamp mean anything, and it's the cheapest way to validate the whole gate + timeout + auth-error path.
6. Tests: all unit tests + the read/fetch integration tests.

Deliverable: branch picker populated, current branch, `↑2 ↓1`, "last fetched 9 minutes ago", working Fetch with a spinner. Push/Pull/Switch present but disabled with "coming soon" — or omitted.

**Phase 2 — Push + Switch**
Both are per-ref and need the full error taxonomy: `.rejected`, `.alreadyCheckedOut`, `.dirtyWorkingTree`, `.nothingToPush`. `--set-upstream` policy. The jj asymmetry (Push disabled for `.ancestor`; switch never refuses on dirty). Integration tests against the `file://` origin.

**Phase 3 — Pull with rebase**
The riskiest: `--autostash`, the `rebase-merge` post-failure probe, the SIGKILL hazard, jj's two-step fetch+rebase, jj's exit-0-with-conflicts. Ship with a confirmation for the dirty-tree case and an "undo" hint.

**Phase 4 — hardening / nice-to-have**
- jj commit count above the ancestor bookmark (turn `hasUnbookmarkedWork: Bool` into a number via a `<bm>..@` revset count).
- jj "Create bookmark & push" — `jj git push --named workroom/<n>=@-`, which is semantically perfect for Workroom since the workspace is already named `workroom/<n>` (`internal/vcs/jj.go:30`).
- Per-project branch-list cache (the list is repo-shared; N workrooms currently each read it).
- `checkedOutIn` annotations + disabled rows in the picker.
- Triangular-remote handling (surface `pullFrom` separately in the UI).
- Widen the gate for git remote ops if `.locked` shows up in reports.

---

## 9. Where your assumptions need correcting

1. **`jj git fetch` passes `--no-write-fetch-head`**, so `FETCH_HEAD` is *not* the jj last-fetch source. (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`; confirmed empirically on your `platform` repo — op-log fetches at 14:44/20:07 vs a `FETCH_HEAD` mtime of 16:57.) Use the op-log scan (§4).
2. **jj's ahead/behind are inverted.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means *the remote is ahead of local* = git's **behind**; `tracking_behind_count()` = git's **ahead**. jj's own default template proves it: `format_tracked_remote_ref_distances` prints `"ahead by N commits"` next to `@origin`. Swap on ingest, comment the swap, pin it with a cross-backend integration test.
3. **`FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree.** A fetch in the project root is invisible to a workroom's `FETCH_HEAD` and vice versa. Run fetch at the project root always — which also makes "last fetched" a per-project fact all workrooms agree on. (`ghProbeDirectory`'s rule extends to git, not just jj, for this one op.)
4. **You don't need a second command for ahead/behind, and you don't need `@{u}`.** `git for-each-ref`'s `%(push:short)`/`%(push:track)` resolve to `<remote>/<same-name>` and its divergence *even with no upstream configured* — verified on your `platform` repo. That's the fallback chain you were going to hand-roll, plus `[gone]`, plus per-row counts for the picker, plus `%(worktreepath)`, plus `%(HEAD)`, in one 30 ms process.
5. **"SwiftGitX's LOCAL ops are fine" does not extend to `switch`.** `Repository.switch(to:)` → `git_checkout_tree` + `git_repository_set_head`, and **libgit2 does not enforce git's "already used by worktree at" guard**. Workroom's entire model is `git worktree add -b`, so a picker offering `main` would happily give you two worktrees on `main` where the CLI refuses. It's also non-atomic (checkout then set-HEAD; a failure between leaves a half-switched repo) and skips the DWIM/hook/submodule behaviour users expect. Shell out.
6. **`Repository.push` silently writes repo config.** Its `addPushRefspec` calls `git_remote_add_push`, persisting `remote.origin.push = refs/heads/x:refs/heads/x` into the repo's config — for every branch you push. Independent of the credentials problem, that alone disqualifies it.
7. **jj workrooms have no bookmark, so git's and jj's Push buttons are not symmetric.** A jj workroom is `jj workspace add --name workroom/<n>` (`internal/vcs/jj.go:30`) — no bookmark is created. So `currentRef.kind == .ancestor` and `jj git push -b <ancestor>` would push the *project's* `master`, not your work. Disable Push with `.nothingToPush` in phase 1; the phase-4 `--named workroom/<n>=@-` is the real fix. A git workroom, by contrast, is a real branch and `push --set-upstream` just works.
8. **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the git import/export lock**, even a read: `jj git remote list` failed with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export … git_import_export.lock"* under the sandbox. So don't reach for `jj git remote list`/`jj git root` in the read path — derive the remote list from `jj bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes (free) and locate the git dir by reading `.jj/repo/store/git_target` (verified: contains `../../../.git` on your colocated `platform` repo). `jj bookmark list --ignore-working-copy` takes no lock.
9. **`SwiftGitX.Branch.init` is eager and expensive** — one `ObjectFactory.lookupObject`, one `git_branch_upstream` that *recursively constructs another `Branch`* (another object lookup), plus a `git_remote_lookup`, **per branch**. `branch.list(.local)` on a 500-branch repo is ~1500 libgit2 object lookups on a blocking thread. Beyond the runner-injection problem, that's a bad way to fill a menu.
10. **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocess ops**, and you should say so where you write it or it'll read as a bug. The rule exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, so the gate would release while the abandoned call still held the lock. `StatusCommandRunner` SIGKILLs the process tree at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely gone and the lock genuinely released. Compose `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }` with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Separately: the gate is key-based and backend-agnostic, so if git's `packed-refs.lock` contention shows up in practice, route git remote ops through it too — at which point renaming it (`RepoWriteGate`) costs 3 call sites + `JJSnapshotGateTests.swift`. I'd defer the rename rather than churn it speculatively.
11. **Never auto-fetch.** No TTL-driven, focus-driven, or sweep-driven network call. It burns rate limits, can trigger credential/SSH prompts on a machine nobody's watching, and the existing `refreshWorkroomStatuses` sweep has no business growing a network mutation.

---

### Critical Files for Implementation

- `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift` — the template for `VCSRemoteResolver`: injected runner, `resolveGit`/`resolveJJ`, `static` pure classifiers, `opDirectory` ≈ `ghProbeDirectory:364`, `gitHardening:63` to reuse verbatim.

content.content:
# macapp/CLAUDE.md

The Workroom macOS app: a SwiftUI (macOS 15+) front-end that bundles the `workroom`
Go binary and drives it over the CLI's `--json` contract. See README.md for full
architecture, signing, and notarization detail — this file is the quick reference.

## Dev tasks (Makefile)

Every dev task runs through the **repo-root `Makefile`**, namespaced `app-*` (run from the repo
root, not `macapp/`):

```bash
make app-run        # canonical local loop: xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug) → relaunch
make app-build      # xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug)
make app-test       # xcodebuild test (WorkroomAppTests) — parallel; APP_TEST_FLAGS= to serialize
make app-generate   # force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
make app-vcs        # build the Rust VCS core → WrVcs SwiftPM package (auto-run before app builds)
make app-format     # swift-format, rewrite sources in place
make app-lint       # swift-format --strict (non-zero on any violation — the hard gate)
make app-release    # Release build → notarize → staple → DMG installer (Scripts/release.sh)
make app-icon       # regenerate AppIcon PNGs (Scripts/make-icon.swift)
make app-clean      # remove DerivedData + .xcodeproj
```

Builds reuse `macapp/DerivedData/` so the Swift packages (incl. the GhosttyKit xcframework)
aren't re-resolved/re-downloaded every build. (`cli-*` targets cover the Go CLI — see the root
CLAUDE.md.)

## VCS core (Rust jj + SwiftGitX git)

Workroom reads VCS data through **two backends behind one Swift layer** (the app is growing into a
VCS-first IDE — issue #59 is the first brick):

- **jj → Rust `jj-lib` via UniFFI.** The `vcs/` Rust workspace (jj-only) builds a static xcframework
  + generated Swift into the local SwiftPM package `vcs/swift/WrVcs` — the app does `import WrVcs`.
- **git → SwiftGitX (libgit2), pure Swift.** git has a mature native Swift path; jj has none — so
  only jj needs the Rust/UniFFI bridge. (An all-Rust core with gix was tried and dropped: gix bought
  no real unification and libgit2 is the more complete git engine.)

**Three reads reach past SwiftGitX**, all linking the `libgit2` C API **directly** (its own SPM package
in `project.yml`, URL + version identical to SwiftGitX's own dependency so SwiftPM sees one package
identity). `Core/LibGit2.swift` owns the single `git_libgit2_init` and hands out raw `git_repository`
handles (SwiftGitX inits inside `Repository.open`, which a direct C caller can't rely on); these four
files are the only ones in the app touching raw libgit2:

- **Push state — `Core/GitGraph.swift`.** SwiftGitX cannot express a commit *range*: its
  `CommitSequence` only calls `git_revwalk_push`, never `git_revwalk_hide`, it exposes no
  merge-base/graph helper, and its repository pointer is `internal` — so "which commits aren't on
  `origin` yet" (`HEAD --not refs/remotes/origin/*`) needs the C API. The jj side answers the same
  question natively with one `ancestors(<tracked @origin tips>)` revset. Push state is
  **origin-scoped** and any unreadable ref degrades the WHOLE page to "unknown" (no badge) rather than
  a partial answer.
- **Commit diffs — `Core/GitCommitDiff.swift`.** Rename detection is `git_diff_find_similar` run over a
  live `git_diff`, and a SwiftGitX `Diff` materializes its deltas/patches in an `internal` init and
  frees the `git_diff` before returning, so there's nothing left to detect on. Without it a committed
  rename read as delete + add while `git show` showed one rename row (git defaults to
  `diff.renames=true`), and a root commit's diff came back empty (SwiftGitX diffs it against itself).
  Detection options are NULL, which is what makes libgit2 read the repo's own `diff.renames` /
  `diff.renamelimit` — naming a flag explicitly suppresses that config read, so a repo set to
  `diff.renames=false` or `=copies` would silently disagree with its own CLI. Typechanges are included
  (`GIT_DIFF_INCLUDE_TYPECHANGE`); without it libgit2 splits a file↔symlink change into delete + add
  on the SAME path, giving the file list two rows with one `id`. `GitProvider.changeset`/`.fileDiff`
  both read through it, so the History file list and the patch text can't disagree.
- **Working-tree ± line counts — `Core/GitDiffStats.swift`**, via `git_diff_get_stats`. SwiftGitX
  surfaces no diffstat, and its `Diff` is **eager**: `Diff.init` builds a `Patch` per delta and
  materializes every hunk line into a Swift `String` before the caller sees it. Summing those for the
  badge cost one `String` per changed line of the whole worktree on **every** status refresh, so the
  counts moved to libgit2, which counts in C and allocates nothing Swift-side. The diff itself is
  irreducible — that's what `git diff --shortstat` costs too. With `changeset` now counting through
  `GitCommitDiff`, **no** `+N −M` in the app is summed off SwiftGitX hunk lines any more, which also
  ends a real bug: that sum counted the EOFNL markers (`\ No newline at end of file`) as lines, so
  changing only a file's trailing newline reported two deletions where git reports `1 insertion(+),
  1 deletion(-)`. libgit2 skips them, as `git diff --shortstat`/`--numstat` do. It runs
  `git_diff_find_similar` too, for the same reason `GitCommitDiff` does: the file list beside these
  counts already pairs renames (libgit2 status' `.renamesIndex`/`.renamesWorkingTree`), so without it
  a staged rename rendered as one "renamed" row badged `+N −N` while `git diff HEAD --shortstat`
  reported `0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.

**Read surface & routing.** `Core/VCSProviding.swift` is the one Swift protocol; `VCS.provider(for:)`
routes by repo kind. `RustJJProvider` maps `WrVcs.*` → app-native models, `GitProvider` wraps
SwiftGitX. `WorkroomStatusResolver` and `BranchResolver` read through this layer — **the jj CLI
parsers are gone** (log/changeset/currentRef/workingStatus are all native jj-lib).

**The one mutating read: `RustJJProvider.workingStatus`.** jj's working copy is itself a commit, so
on-disk edits don't exist to jj-lib until snapshotted — a working-copy status read therefore *must*
snapshot `@` first: it takes the working-copy lock and rewrites `@` (modeled on jayjay's
`refresh_working_copy`). Everything else (log/changeset/currentRef) is a read-only `load_at_head`
with no lock. Because it mutates, **only test snapshot changes on throwaway repos** (corruption
risk). Line counts come from the SAME native read — `changed_files` materializes each changed file's
two sides and counts them, so `resolveJJ` fires no `jj diff --stat` process (it used to; see
`40456bae`). Oversized and binary files report no count rather than being read whole. Cargo coverage:
`vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/tests/working_status.rs` + `line_stats.rs`; Swift coverage:
`WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.testJJ*`.

`make app-vcs` (→ `vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh`) builds the Rust artifacts and **runs automatically
before `app-build`/`app-test`/`app-generate`** (a Makefile prerequisite). Requirements:

- **`protoc`** on PATH (`brew install protobuf`) — a build-time dep of jj-lib.
- arm64 by default; **`make app-release` builds universal** (`VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal`), which
  needs **rustup `stable` ≥ 1.93** + `rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin aarch64-apple-darwin`
  (Homebrew's rust can't cross-compile; the script preflights this and errors clearly).
- **Unchanged inputs are a no-op.** The script hashes the Rust sources, manifests/lockfile, itself,
  `rustc --version` and the arch flavour into `vcs/swift/WrVcs/Frameworks/.build-stamp`, and exits
  early when that matches and the outputs exist. `WR_VCS_FORCE=1 make app-vcs` rebuilds regardless.
  CI leans on this: it caches the *outputs* keyed on the same inputs, so a commit that doesn't touch
  `vcs/` skips the ~4-minute crate-graph build (and `make app-test`'s own `app-vcs` prerequisite
  stays free).
- **Xcode-driven builds are gated, not auto-fixed.** ⌘R/⌘U (and a raw `xcodebuild`) skip the
  Makefile, so they'd otherwise link the last-built core. A `Rust VCS core up to date` pre-build
  phase runs `build-apple.sh --check` and **fails the build** with `run 'make app-vcs'` when the
  stamp doesn't match `vcs/`. It can't rebuild for you: SPM extracts the binaryTarget's xcframework
  before target build phases run, so a fresh `.a` wouldn't reach that build's link. Silently linking
  a stale core cost a debugging session once — conflicted files read as `.modified` because the
  linked core predated a merged per-file-conflict fix.

The xcframework + generated Swift are **gitignored and regenerated**; only `Package.swift` + a
`shim.c` are tracked. Packaging note: the xcframework is **library-only** (no headers) and the FFI
Clang module (`wr_vcs_uniffiFFI`) is a separate SPM C target — a headers-bearing static xcframework
copies its `module.modulemap` into the shared `Debug/include/` and collides with GhosttyKit's
("Multiple commands produce include/module.modulemap").

## Formatting & linting

Swift is formatted/linted with **swift-format** (bundled with the Xcode toolchain — run via
`xcrun swift-format`, no install). Config `macapp/.swift-format` (2-space, 100 cols) covers
`WorkroomApp/` + `WorkroomAppTests/` only (not the `Scripts/*.swift` tools). Use `make app-format`
/ `make app-lint`. Every Xcode/`xcodebuild` build also runs a `swift-format lint` pre-build phase
that surfaces violations as **warnings** (non-fatal — `make app-lint` is the hard gate). Run
`make app-format` before committing.

## Gotchas

- **The Swift module is `Workroom`** (the target is `WorkroomApp`; `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME` is pinned
  to `Workroom` in `project.yml`). Tests use `@testable import Workroom`. The pin matters because
  `PRODUCT_NAME` is **per-config**: `Workroom` for Release, `Workroom Dev` for Debug (see below) —
  without the pin the Debug module would become `Workroom_Dev` and break the import. A test
  target's `TEST_HOST` must point at the Debug product (`Workroom Dev.app/Contents/MacOS/Workroom
  Dev`); XcodeGen's auto-derived (target-name-based) host is wrong and fails with "Could not find
  test host".
- **Debug builds run side by side with the release build.** The Debug config has a distinct
  identity — bundle id `com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, product/display name `Workroom Dev`,
  and the amber `AppIcon-Dev` icon set — so a local build doesn't fight the installed release
  `Workroom` for activation, the key window, preferences (separate UserDefaults domain via the
  bundle id), or the system-wide ⌘§ hotkey. The Debug build deliberately **doesn't register ⌘§**
  and **doesn't run Sparkle scheduled checks** (`#if DEBUG` in `WorkroomApp.swift` / `Updater.swift`)
  so it can't grab the global hotkey or try to "update" itself to the release DMG. Both builds
  still share the CLI config at `~/.config/workroom/config.json` (the bundled CLI has no
  config-path override), so they show the same projects/workrooms. `make app-run` only kills the
  `Workroom Dev` instance, never your release build. The two app icons (`make app-icon` renders
  both) are identical except for the tile gradient.
- **Adding/removing/renaming a `.swift` file needs an `xcodegen generate`.** XcodeGen
  expands the source glob into explicit file refs in the (gitignored) `.xcodeproj`, so
  the change is invisible (or, for a deleted/renamed file, a hard "Build input file
  cannot be found" error) until the project is regenerated. The `make app-*` build
  targets now run `xcodegen generate` every time, so this is handled automatically —
  it only bites when building from Xcode directly (regenerate, or run `make app-generate`).
- **SourceKit "Cannot find type X in scope" is usually noise.** The single-file indexer
  doesn't see sibling files; a clean `xcodebuild` is authoritative.
- **The terminal is libghostty** (`libghostty-spm`'s `GhosttyKit` xcframework, pinned
  `exactVersion: 1.2.3` in project.yml). The embedding C API is not yet stable, so pin EXACT —
  don't float it. The terminal surface (`Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`) + runtime
  (`GhosttyApp`/`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter`) are ours; the bundled `Resources/ghostty` (terminfo +
  shell-integration) must ship for the engine to start. Pre-GA, the plan is to move to a
  self-built xcframework from a pinned Ghostty fork.
- **The child environment has two layers, and only one of them is reliable** (`Core/ShellEnvironment.swift`).
  A Finder-launched `.app` gets a minimal PATH, so: the **floor** (`floorPath()`) reads `/etc/paths`
  + `/etc/paths.d/*` — `path_helper`'s own inputs — with no shell at all, and that alone resolves
  Postgres.app's `psql`; the **probe** (`refresh()`) then runs one `$SHELL -ilc` for what only an
  interactive login shell knows (`.zshrc` PATH entries, mise shims). The probe is best-effort by
  design: its failures degrade to the floor, so a `.zshrc` that ends `exec tmux` costs enrichment
  and never the bug. Three traps worth knowing: **`path_helper` APPENDS** the PATH it's handed, so
  the probe must be spawned with a *cleared* `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` or Homebrew ends
  up at the tail; the payload is a **raw `env -0` stream between UUID markers** because command
  substitution strips NULs and the user's `base64` may be GNU's (wraps at 76 cols); and the deadline
  is a `DispatchWorkItem` **inside** the blocking closure, because `withTimeout` cannot cancel a
  `runBlocking` call and would leak a shell per invocation. `setenv("PATH", …)` happens exactly once,
  in `WorkroomApp.init` — a later write would race the status sweep's `ProcessInfo.environment`
  reads. Everything else reads `ShellEnvironment.path()` (PATH only, for the automatic sweep) or
  `.environment()` (the full environment, for setup/teardown scripts).
- **Menu enable/disable must flow through `focusedSceneValue` + `@FocusedValue`**
  (see `WorkroomApp.swift`); a `Commands` body does not re-evaluate when the shared
  `AppStore` mutates. ⌘1–9 are handled by an `NSEvent` local monitor in `AppDelegate`,
  not menu items, so they fire before the terminal swallows the keys.

## Layout

**VCS info that only the GUI needs** (e.g. the sidebar root row's current branch/bookmark)
is resolved app-side in `Core/BranchResolver.swift` (per project, async, with a per-call
timeout) — deliberately NOT added to the `workroom --json` contract, which the human CLI
never shows.

`WorkroomApp/Core/` — store, CLI wrapper, terminal sessions, models, theme.
`WorkroomApp/Views/` — `NavigationSplitView` tree sidebar + terminal detail.
`Scripts/` — `run.sh` (local), `build-helper.sh` (embeds+signs the Go binary), `release.sh`
(build → notarize → staple → DMG → EdDSA-sign for Sparkle), `appcast.sh` (publishes the Sparkle
appcast to the fixed `appcast` release), `appcast-notes.sh` (re-renders a published item's
`<description>` from the current release body — see "Auto-update" below), `make-icon.swift`
(regenerates the `AppIcon` PNGs in `Assets.xcassets` — run `swift Scripts/make-icon.swift`).

## Auto-update (Sparkle)

`Core/Updater.swift` wraps Sparkle's `SPUStandardUpdaterController` (the "Check for Updates…"
menu item + the Settings toggle bind to it). The `SU*` keys in `project.yml` (`SUFeedURL`,
`SUPublicEDKey`, `SUEnableAutomaticChecks`) configure it. **Versioning is tag-driven** —
`CFBundleShortVersionString`/`CFBundleVersion` resolve from `$(MARKETING_VERSION)`/
`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`, which `release.sh` injects from the git tag (build number =
commit count, so it only ever increases — Sparkle compares it). The appcast feed is an asset
on the fixed `appcast` GitHub release. See `README.md` ("Auto-update") for the one-time keypair
setup and the `SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY` secret.

**Release channels (issue #91) — two build identities.** The **main** app (`Release` config)
switches `stable`⟷`pre` at runtime via the *Settings ▸ General ▸ Release channel* picker
(`ReleaseChannel.pickerCases` = stable/pre only). **Workroom Nightly** is a separate side-by-side
product — the `Nightly` build config in `project.yml` (bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, name, violet
`AppIcon-Nightly`, `WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL=nightly` → the `WorkroomReleaseChannel` Info.plist
marker read by `ReleaseChannel.current`/`isNightlyBuild`), extending the Debug/"Workroom Dev"
per-config identity pattern to a third identity.

`Updater.allowedChannels(for:)` returns `{nightly}` on the nightly build and the picked stable/pre
floor otherwise; one appcast feed carries all channels (`Scripts/appcast.sh` tags items via the
shared `Scripts/channel-helper.sh`; stable stays untagged = Sparkle default), and Sparkle's
bundle-id check stops either identity installing the other's DMG. Nightly is a single **rolling**
item; appcast idempotency keys on `(channel, build)`. `build-helper.sh` bakes both
`-X main.version=$(MARKETING_VERSION)` and `-X main.channel=$(WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL)` into the
bundled CLI, and `CommandLineInstaller` symlinks it as `workroom` (main) or `workroom-nightly`
(nightly build) so both coexist in PATH. `Updater.migrateReleaseChannelIfNeeded` opts an upgrading
beta user into `pre` and coerces a legacy `.nightly` selection to `.stable` (main build only).

**Release-notes in the update dialog.** Sparkle's dialog renders the appcast item's
`<description>`. `appcast.sh` (run during the release) embeds the GitHub release body as that
description — but at release time the body is still goreleaser's raw commit list, since the
curated notes are written afterwards. So a second path keeps them in sync: the
`.github/workflows/appcast-notes.yml` workflow fires on every `release: edited` event and runs
`Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`, which re-renders the matching item's `<description>` from the
release's *current* body. Curating a release's notes therefore auto-refreshes what the update
dialog shows; no rebuild needed. To fix an already-published feed by hand, run it directly:
`TAG=vX.Y.Z REPO=owner/repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) macapp/Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`.

questions.question: The engine has NO branch listing, NO fetch/push/pull, NO ahead/behind counts, and NO last-fetch time today — `VCSProviding` is read-only. All of that has to be built. How much in this pass?

options.label: Everything (fetch + push + pull + switch)
options.description: Full toolbar as specced: branch dropdown with switch, ahead/behind counts, last-fetch time, and working Fetch / Push origin / Pull origin with rebase. Biggest pass — new resolver, new model, new views, ~3 new test files. Pull-with-rebase is the riskiest piece (autostash, interrupted-rebase recovery, jj conflicts-exit-0).

options.label: Read-only toolbar + Fetch only
options.description: All three segments render with real data (branch name, branch dropdown listing branches, ahead/behind pills, live "last fetched N minutes ago") and Fetch works. Push/Pull show the right title but are disabled. Branch dropdown is read-only — no switching. Smallest correct increment; the whole read path and error taxonomy get proven by the one safe mutation.

options.label: Fetch + Push + branch switch, Pull later
options.description: Everything except pull-with-rebase. Push and branch-switch are per-ref and need the full error taxonomy (rejected, already-checked-out-in-another-worktree, dirty tree). Pull is deferred because it's the one op that can leave the repo mid-rebase if killed.

questions.question: jj workrooms have no bookmark — `jj workspace add --name workroom/x` creates a workspace, not a bookmark, so `@` is unbookmarked and `jj git push` has literally nothing to send. (Git workrooms are real branches, so push just works.) What should jj's Push do?

options.label: Create the bookmark on first push
options.description: `jj git push --named workroom/<name>=@-` — creates a bookmark named after the workspace and pushes it. Semantically right for Workroom (the workspace already carries that name) and makes Push work identically for both backends. Extra work: bookmark-naming policy, and the toolbar needs a "Publish" state distinct from "Push".

options.label: Disable Push for unbookmarked jj @
options.description: Push greys out with "@ has no bookmark, so there's nothing to push. Set one first." Honest and cheap, but a jj user's Push button is dead until they run `jj bookmark set` in the terminal themselves.

options.label: Skip jj for now — git only
options.description: Toolbar renders branch name for jj (already available) but all remote actions and the branch dropdown are git-only. Half the app's supported backends get a dead toolbar; the Changes panel is deliberately one unified layout for both, so this breaks that.

questions.question: The inspector's activity rail has two sections: Changes (which stacks Changes + History + Pull Request) and Files. Where should the new toolbar appear?

options.label: Always visible at top of the inspector
options.description: Shows for both Changes and Files. Branch/remote state is repo-level, not Changes-level, and hiding it would jump the layout 36pt on every activity-bar click. Recommended.

options.label: Only when the Changes section is active
options.description: Hidden on the Files section. Keeps the Files tree at full height, but the branch name vanishes while browsing that same repo's tree and the inspector reflows on section switch.

content.content:
Push to a Git remote

By default, pushes tracking bookmarks pointing to `remote_bookmarks(remote=<remote>)..@`. Use
`--bookmark` to push specific bookmarks. Use `--all` to push all bookmarks. Use `--change` to
generate bookmark names based on the change IDs of specific commits.

When pushing a bookmark, the command pushes all commits in the range from the remote's current
position up to and including the bookmark's target commit. Any descendant commits beyond the
bookmark are not pushed.

If the local bookmark has changed from the last fetch, push will update the remote bookmark to the
new position after passing safety checks. This is similar to `git push --force-with-lease` - the
remote is updated only if its current state matches what Jujutsu last fetched.

Unlike in Git, the remote to push to is not derived from the tracked remote bookmarks. Use
`--remote` to select the remote Git repository by name. There is no option to push to multiple
remotes.

Before the command actually moves, creates, or deletes a remote bookmark, it makes several [safety
checks]. If there is a problem, you may need to run `jj git fetch --remote <remote name>` and/or
resolve some [bookmark conflicts].

[safety checks]: https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/bookmarks/#pushing-bookmarks-safety-checks

[bookmark conflicts]: https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/bookmarks/#conflicts

Usage: jj git push [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --remote <REMOTE>
          The remote to push to (only named remotes are supported)
          
          This defaults to the `git.push` setting. If that is not configured, and if there are
          multiple remotes, the remote named "origin" will be used.

  -b, --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Push only this bookmark, or bookmarks matching a pattern (can be repeated)
          
          If a bookmark isn't tracking anything yet, the remote bookmark will be tracked
          automatically.
          
          By default, the specified pattern matches bookmark names with glob syntax. You can also
          use other [string pattern syntax].
          
          [string pattern syntax]: https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/revsets/#string-patterns

      --all
          Push all bookmarks (including new bookmarks)

      --tracked
          Push all tracked bookmarks
          
          This usually means that the bookmark was already pushed to or fetched from the [relevant
          remote].
          
          [relevant remote]: https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/bookmarks#remotes-and-tracked-bookmarks

      --deleted
          Push all deleted bookmarks
          
          Only tracked bookmarks can be successfully deleted on the remote. A warning will be
          printed if any untracked bookmarks on the remote correspond to missing local bookmarks.

      --allow-empty-description
          Allow pushing commits with empty descriptions

      --allow-private
          Allow pushing commits that are private
          
          The set of private commits can be configured by the `git.private-commits` setting. The
          default is `none()`, meaning all commits are eligible to be pushed.

  -r, --revision <REVSETS>
          Push bookmarks pointing to these commits (can be repeated)

  -c, --change <REVSETS>
          Push this commit by creating a bookmark (can be repeated)
          
          The created bookmark will be tracked automatically. Use the `templates.git_push_bookmark`
          setting to customize the generated bookmark name. The default is `"push-" ++

          By default, Jujutsu snapshots the working copy at the beginning of every command. The

          working-copy commit (`@`). If you want to avoid snapshotting the working copy and instead
          see a possibly stale working-copy commit, you can use `--ignore-working-copy`. This may be

          working copy.
          
          Loading the repository at a specific operation with `--at-operation` implies
          `--ignore-working-copy`.

      --no-integrate-operation
          Run the command as usual but don't integrate any operations
          
          When this option is given, the operations will still be created as usual but they will not
          be integrated to the operation log. The working copy will also not be updated.
          
          The command will print the resulting operation ID. You can pass that to e.g. `jj --at-op`
          to inspect the resulting repo state, or you can pass it to `jj op restore` to restore the
          repo to that state. You can also pass the ID to `jj op integrate` to integrate the
          operation.
          
          Note that this does *not* prevent side effects outside the repo. For example, `jj git push
          --no-integrate-operation` will still perform the push.

          Allow rewriting immutable commits
          
          By default, Jujutsu prevents rewriting commits in the configured set of immutable commits.
          This option disables that check and lets you rewrite any commit but the root commit.
          
          This option only affects the check. It does not affect the `immutable_heads()` revset or

input.content:
# VCS toolbar: branch selection + push/pull/fetch status

## Context

The VCS inspector today can only *read*. `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`)
is a strictly read-only protocol — 8 members, no mutations, no network. There is **no** branch
listing, **no** fetch/push/pull, **no** ahead/behind counts, and **no** last-fetch time anywhere in
the app or the Rust core. The only place a branch name appears is a `.caption` capsule in the Changes
body (`ChangesPanel.swift:669-730`) and the status bar (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`), both
display-only.

So a user working in a workroom has to leave the app for every remote interaction: they can see what
changed but not whether it's pushed, how far behind origin they are, when they last fetched, or what
other branches exist — let alone act on any of it.

**Outcome:** a 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector, GitHub-Desktop shaped — current
branch as a dropdown that switches branches, a sync segment that reads "Push origin / Last fetched 9
minutes ago" with an ahead/behind count pill and performs the action on click, and a fetch icon
button. Working for **both** git and jj.

Scope confirmed with the user: **everything** — fetch, push, pull-with-rebase, and branch switch.
Toolbar shows **only when the Changes activity section is active**.

---

## Decisions

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Extend `VCSProviding`? | **No — zero changes.** New `VCSRemoteResolver` struct modelled 1:1 on `WorkroomStatusResolver`. |
| Backend | `git` / `jj` **CLI** via `StatusCommandRunning`. Auth comes free (credential helpers, ssh-agent, tokens); matches the existing `gh` precedent. |
| SwiftGitX for network? | **No.** `Repository+fetch.swift:30` / `+push.swift:49` pass `NULL` for the options struct ⇒ zero credential support, HTTPS impossible. `pull` doesn't exist (`// TODO: Implement pull`). |
| SwiftGitX for `switch`? | **No.** libgit2 doesn't enforce git's "already used by worktree at" guard — fatal given Workroom *is* worktrees. Also non-atomic, and `Repository.push` silently writes `remote.origin.push` into repo config. |
| Rust / UniFFI | **Zero changes.** No `make app-vcs`. |
| Auto-fetch | **Never.** Explicit user action only. |
| Toolbar visibility | Only when `store.activeInspectorSection == .changes`. |

---

## Engine

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSRemoteResolver.swift`

Shaped exactly like `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`: one `struct`, an injected
`StatusCommandRunning`, private `resolveGit`/`resolveJJ`, and `static` pure arg-builders/parsers/
classifiers that carry all the semantics (the `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` testability pattern).

```swift
struct VCSRemoteResolver: Sendable {
  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
  /// For `currentRef` only — reuse the app's canonical answer incl. `.ancestor`/`.detached`.
  /// Same seam + default as `BranchResolver.swift:20`.
  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5       // local ref listing
  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300    // network + rebase; SIGKILL here is dangerous
  var switchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared
  var refCap: Int = 500

  func resolveState(path:vcs:projectRoot:) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
  func fetch(path:vcs:projectRoot:remote:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func push(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:setUpstream:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func pullRebase(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:tracking:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func switchRef(path:vcs:projectRoot:to:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult

  /// THE placement rule (the `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory:364` pattern).
  static func opDirectory(_ action:path:vcs:projectRoot:) -> String
}
```

Reuse `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`:63`, `["-c","core.fsmonitor="]`) verbatim on every
git call. Every jj call gets `--color never --no-pager`; **reads** get `--ignore-working-copy`,
**mutations must not** (they need to snapshot).

#### git — one process answers list + current + ahead/behind

```
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate --count=<cap+1>
  --format=%(refname)%00%(refname:short)%00%(objectname)%00%(committerdate:unix)%00%(HEAD)%00%(worktreepath)%00%(upstream:short)%00%(upstream:track)%00%(push:short)%00%(push:track)%00%(symref)
  refs/heads refs/remotes
```

- `%00` NUL separators — `%(worktreepath)` is a path and can contain a tab. Skip records whose field
  count ≠ 11 rather than crashing.
- `--count=cap+1` to learn `refsTruncated` (the `GitProvider.log:25` idiom).
- **`%(push:short)`/`%(push:track)` is the whole ballgame.** Under the default `push.default=simple`
  they resolve to `<remote>/<same-name>` and its divergence **even with no upstream configured** —
  which is every Workroom branch, since a workroom is `git worktree add -b` (`internal/vcs/git.go:30`).
  Take `push:*` first, fall back to `upstream:*`, record which in `comparedTo`, set `pullFrom` only
  when they differ. No second `rev-list`, no `@{u}`.
- Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose short name is
  the bare `origin` (junk picker row). Its target gives the default branch for free.
- `%(worktreepath)` includes the *current* worktree, so nil it when it equals the workroom's own path.
  Non-nil ⇒ a `git switch` **will** fail ⇒ the picker disables that row.
- Current ref comes from `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)`, **not** `%(HEAD)` — that returns
  nothing for detached/unborn HEAD, both already handled at `GitProvider.swift:78-98`. `%(HEAD)` is
  only the per-row `isCurrent` marker.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git … fetch <remote>` | **project root** |
| push | `git … push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| pull | `git … pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <remoteBranch>` | workroom |
| switch (local) | `git … switch <name>` | workroom |
| switch (remote-only) | `git … switch --track <remote>/<name>` | workroom |

- **No `--prune`, no `--no-write-fetch-head`** — let the repo's own `fetch.prune` decide, and we
  need `FETCH_HEAD`.
- `--set-upstream` **only** when no upstream exists yet; otherwise it rewrites config on every push.
- **Never** `--force` / `--force-with-lease`. Rejection ⇒ `.rejected` ⇒ the UI offers Pull.
- `--autostash` on pull is mandatory — workroom trees are always dirty.
- Explicit `<remote> <remoteBranch>` on pull (from `pullFrom ?? comparedTo`) so an upstream-less
  workroom can still pull.

#### jj — one process answers list + ahead/behind

`jj bookmark list --all-remotes --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager -T '<template>'`,
emitting NUL-separated: `name`, `remote`, `commit_id`, `committer timestamp`, `present`, `conflict`,
`tracked`, `tracking_ahead_count`, `tracking_behind_count`.

Four traps, all verified against jj 0.43 locally:
- The template keyword is **`self`**, not `ref` (`ref.name()` errors).
- `tracking_*_count()` on a non-remote ref renders the literal `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>`
  into the output — the `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing.
- **Drop `remote == "git"`** — a colocated repo has a pseudo-remote called `git` that `--all-remotes`
  includes. Not a remote; also keeps `remotes` clean.
- **jj's counts are inverted relative to git.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means
  *the remote is ahead* = git's **behind**. Swap on ingest, in one commented line, pinned by a
  cross-backend integration test.

Plus `present == 0` on an `@origin` row ⇒ `gone` (jj's `[gone]`); `tracked == 0` ⇒ `comparedTo` set
but counts `nil`. One record per `(name, remote)`; fold in Swift.

**Anonymous-branch counts.** When `currentRef.kind == .ancestor` (jj `@` carries no bookmark — the
normal workroom state, since `jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark), the bookmark row's
counts describe the *ancestor bookmark*, not the user's work. So when and only when `.ancestor`, run
two extra cheap local revset counts:

```
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@'  -T '"x\n"'  → ahead
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r '@..remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)'  -T '"x\n"'  → behind
```

`remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@` is exactly what bare `jj git push` sends, so the ahead count and
the Push button agree by construction.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | **project root** |
| push (bookmarked `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --bookmark <name>` | **project root** |
| push (anonymous `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --change <rev>` | **project root** |
| pull step 1 | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | project root |
| pull step 2 | `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote>` | workroom |
| switch | `jj new <name>` / `jj new <name>@<remote>` | workroom |

- **`--change` is jj's built-in anonymous-branch push** (confirmed on 0.43): it creates the bookmark,
  tracks it automatically, and names it via `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
  `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`). This is the answer for the unbookmarked workroom `@` — no
  hand-rolled naming policy, and the user's own template config is honoured.
- **Revision choice:** `@` if it has changes or a description, else `@-`. jj refuses to push a
  commit with an empty description, and a fresh `@` after `jj new` has neither. `WorkroomStatus
  .jjWorkingCopy` (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`) already carries `description` + `files`, so the model
  decides this with no extra process.
- **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock** — even a read (`jj git
  remote list` fails with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export … git_import_export.lock"*).
  So all jj mutations go through `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`, and the read path derives
  the remote list from `bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes instead of calling `jj git remote list`.
  `jj bookmark list --ignore-working-copy` takes no lock.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocesses** — it
  exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, so the gate would release while the abandoned
  call still held the lock. `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout` and `ProcessTree.killTree`s
  at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely dead. Compose `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }`
  with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Document this where written — it reads like a violation and isn't.
- **`jj new`, not `jj edit`.** `jj edit <bookmark>` makes the bookmarked (probably-pushed) commit
  itself the working copy. `jj new` puts a fresh `@` on top and leaves `kind == .ancestor`, which is
  exactly what the sidebar already renders as `"main ↑"` (`Models.swift:146`).
- **`jj new` must not get `--ignore-working-copy`** — it snapshots first, which is what preserves
  uncommitted edits into the old `@`.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`** — `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@`, the pull-rebase shape.
  Run it unconditionally: already-a-descendant prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts** — jj records conflicts *inside* commits. Never infer success
  from the exit code; re-read `workingStatus().conflicted` and return `.okWithConflicts`.

#### Last-fetch time — differs per backend

**git:** mtime of `<worktree gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD` via `FileManager.attributesOfItem`. No subprocess.
Resolve the gitdir purely: `.git` as directory ⇒ `<path>/.git/FETCH_HEAD`; `.git` as **file** (the
worktree case) ⇒ read it, strip `gitdir: `, trim.

`FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree**, which is why fetch runs at the project root for git too: fetching
inside workroom A would otherwise leave the project and every sibling workroom reading "never
fetched" while their `refs/remotes/*` are perfectly fresh. Running at the root makes "last fetched" a
per-**project** fact all workrooms agree on.

**jj: `FETCH_HEAD` is never written.** jj-lib 0.43 shells `git fetch --porcelain --prune
--no-write-fetch-head` (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`, *"ensures our request is invisible
to other parties"*). Verified empirically. So scan the op log instead:

```
jj op log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager --limit 200
  -T 'self.time().end().format("%s") ++ "\x00" ++ self.description().first_line() ++ "\n"'
```

Newest-first; take the first line whose description starts with `fetch from git remote`. Fragile
against a jj rewording — mitigated by prefix matching, a graceful failure mode (one absent label,
never a wrong one), and an integration test that turns red on a jj bump.

`VCSLastFetch` is a three-way enum (`.at(Date)` / `.never` / `.unknown`), not `Date?` — `.unknown`
must never render as "never" (the `VCSPushState.unknown` rule). No persisted stamp: after our own
fetch, set `.at(Date())` optimistically (the `applyOptimisticPRAction` pattern,
`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:220`) and let the re-read confirm — which also means a `git fetch`
typed in the workroom's own terminal moves the number.

`VCSBranchRef { name, scope: .local/.remote(String), commitID, committedAt, isCurrent, checkedOutIn, tracking }`.

### Error classification — `static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?`

One pure function, `nil` on success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `is already used by worktree at` | `.alreadyCheckedOut(path:)` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `no tracking information for the current branch` | `.noUpstream` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<gitdir>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

`.authRequired` is the **#1 expected failure** and needs bespoke copy: `StatusCommandRunner:53` sets
`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` unconditionally and a GUI app has no tty, so HTTPS-without-a-helper fails
instantly (correct — never hang) with baffling stderr. Say: *"Workroom never prompts for credentials
— configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`) or use SSH."*

`.rebaseInProgress` must **not** offer Retry; it needs `git rebase --abort`. `.timedOut(.pull)` gets
upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` by the post-failure probe, because SIGKILLing a rebase mid-flight is
the one genuinely unsafe timeout.

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSSyncPresentation.swift` — pure mapper

`static func make(_ snapshot: VCSSyncSnapshot, now: Date) -> VCSSyncPresentation`. No SwiftUI, no
`Date()` read — `now` is a parameter so the whole thing is unit-testable at fixed instants (the
`Core/ChangeBadge.swift` precedent). Returns `titleVariants: [String]` (longest first, `[]` ⇒
single-line mode), `subtitle`, `subtitleShort`, `symbol`, `badge`/`secondaryBadge`, `action`,
`isEnabled`, `tone`, `help`, `accessibility`, `accessibilityValue`.

| # | Condition | Title | Subtitle | Badge | Click |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | no target | — | "No workroom selected" | — | — |
| 2 | not a repo | — | "No repository" | — | — |
| 3 | no remote | — | "No remote configured" | — | — |
| 4 | no upstream / `gone` | "Publish branch" | "`<branch>` isn't on origin yet" | `N ↑` | push `--set-upstream` |
| 5 | never fetched, clean | — | "Never fetched" | — | fetch |
| 6 | clean, fetched | — | "Last fetched \(rel)" | — | fetch |
| 7 | ahead only | **"Push origin"** | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `N ↑` | push |
| 8 | behind only | "Pull origin with rebase" | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` | pull |
| 9 | **diverged** | "Pull origin with rebase" | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` then `N ↑` | **pull** |
| 10-12 | fetching/pushing/pulling | "Fetching…"/"Pushing…"/"Pulling…" | "from/to origin" | kept | disabled |
| 13 | failed, idle | previous title | error first line, `tone: .failure` | kept | retry |

Precedence: 13 > 10-12 > 1 > 2 > 3 > 4 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 5 > 6.

Two calls worth pinning with tests:
- **Diverged ⇒ Pull, not Push.** git refuses a non-fast-forward push anyway.
- **No upstream + ahead ⇒ `.publish`, not `.push`.** This is *the* workroom case — a git workroom is
  `git worktree add -b` with no upstream, ever. Getting it wrong makes every workroom read "Push
  origin" against an upstream that doesn't exist.

Relative time: `static func fetchedAgo(_ date:now:short:)` over two `static let
RelativeDateTimeFormatter`s (`.full` / `.abbreviated`); under 60 s ⇒ "just now". Do **not** reuse
`NotificationsList.timeAgo` — it's private and reads `Date()` internally, so it's untestable.

### Layout degradation, 260 → 520pt

At 260 the ideal widths sum to ~287, so it *must* degrade. In firing order:
1. **Sync wins** — `layoutPriority(1)` vs branch `0`. A truncated branch name is still identifiable
   and its full name is repeated in the Changes header 40pt below plus its own tooltip.
2. Truncate, never wrap; every `Text` is `.lineLimit(1)`.
3. Subtitle abbreviates before truncating: "Last fetched 9 minutes ago" → "Fetched 9 min. ago".
4. Title abbreviates: "Pull origin with rebase" → "Pull with rebase" → "Pull".
5. **The "Current Branch" caption drops first** (below ~120pt of branch width) → name only, centred.
   At 260 the caption is not shown. Stated out loud rather than shipping a clipped caption.
6. The sync glyph drops next — the pill's arrow already carries direction.
7. The pill never yields (`.fixedSize()`).
8. Fixed 36pt height at every width; no reflow of the split view below.

Growing to 520: branch caps at 220 so a short name doesn't hoard dead space; sync takes
`maxWidth: .infinity` and absorbs the rest — the extra goes to the segment that can use it.
