# VCS toolbar: branch selection + push/pull/fetch status

## Context

The VCS inspector today can only *read*. `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`)
is a strictly read-only protocol — 8 members, no mutations, no network. There is **no** branch
listing, **no** fetch/push/pull, **no** ahead/behind counts, and **no** last-fetch time anywhere in
the app or the Rust core. The only place a branch name appears is a `.caption` capsule in the Changes
body (`ChangesPanel.swift:669-730`) and the status bar (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`), both
display-only.

So a user working in a workroom has to leave the app for every remote interaction: they can see what
changed but not whether it's pushed, how far behind origin they are, when they last fetched, or what
other branches exist — let alone act on any of it.

**Outcome:** a 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector, GitHub-Desktop shaped — current
branch as a dropdown that switches branches, a sync segment that reads "Push origin / Last fetched 9
minutes ago" with an ahead/behind count pill and performs the action on click, and a fetch icon
button. Working for **both** git and jj.

Scope confirmed with the user: **everything** — fetch, push, pull-with-rebase, and branch switch.
Toolbar shows **only when the Changes activity section is active**.

---

## Decisions

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Extend `VCSProviding`? | **No — zero changes.** New `VCSRemoteResolver` struct modelled 1:1 on `WorkroomStatusResolver`. |
| Backend | `git` / `jj` **CLI** via `StatusCommandRunning`. Auth comes free (credential helpers, ssh-agent, tokens); matches the existing `gh` precedent. |
| SwiftGitX for network? | **No.** `Repository+fetch.swift:30` / `+push.swift:49` pass `NULL` for the options struct ⇒ zero credential support, HTTPS impossible. `pull` doesn't exist (`// TODO: Implement pull`). |
| SwiftGitX for `switch`? | **No.** libgit2 doesn't enforce git's "already used by worktree at" guard — fatal given Workroom *is* worktrees. Also non-atomic, and `Repository.push` silently writes `remote.origin.push` into repo config. |
| Rust / UniFFI | **Zero changes.** No `make app-vcs`. |
| Auto-fetch | **Never.** Explicit user action only. |
| Toolbar visibility | Only when `store.activeInspectorSection == .changes`. |

---

## Engine

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSRemoteResolver.swift`

Shaped exactly like `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`: one `struct`, an injected
`StatusCommandRunning`, private `resolveGit`/`resolveJJ`, and `static` pure arg-builders/parsers/
classifiers that carry all the semantics (the `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` testability pattern).

```swift
struct VCSRemoteResolver: Sendable {
  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
  /// For `currentRef` only — reuse the app's canonical answer incl. `.ancestor`/`.detached`.
  /// Same seam + default as `BranchResolver.swift:20`.
  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5       // local ref listing
  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300    // network + rebase; SIGKILL here is dangerous
  var switchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared
  var refCap: Int = 500

  func resolveState(path:vcs:projectRoot:) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
  func fetch(path:vcs:projectRoot:remote:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func push(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:setUpstream:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func pullRebase(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:tracking:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func switchRef(path:vcs:projectRoot:to:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult

  /// THE placement rule (the `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory:364` pattern).
  static func opDirectory(_ action:path:vcs:projectRoot:) -> String
}
```

Reuse `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`:63`, `["-c","core.fsmonitor="]`) verbatim on every
git call. Every jj call gets `--color never --no-pager`; **reads** get `--ignore-working-copy`,
**mutations must not** (they need to snapshot).

#### git — one process answers list + current + ahead/behind

```
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate --count=<cap+1>
  --format=%(refname)%00%(refname:short)%00%(objectname)%00%(committerdate:unix)%00%(HEAD)%00%(worktreepath)%00%(upstream:short)%00%(upstream:track)%00%(push:short)%00%(push:track)%00%(symref)
  refs/heads refs/remotes
```

- `%00` NUL separators — `%(worktreepath)` is a path and can contain a tab. Skip records whose field
  count ≠ 11 rather than crashing.
- `--count=cap+1` to learn `refsTruncated` (the `GitProvider.log:25` idiom).
- **`%(push:short)`/`%(push:track)` is the whole ballgame.** Under the default `push.default=simple`
  they resolve to `<remote>/<same-name>` and its divergence **even with no upstream configured** —
  which is every Workroom branch, since a workroom is `git worktree add -b` (`internal/vcs/git.go:30`).
  Take `push:*` first, fall back to `upstream:*`, record which in `comparedTo`, set `pullFrom` only
  when they differ. No second `rev-list`, no `@{u}`.
- Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose short name is
  the bare `origin` (junk picker row). Its target gives the default branch for free.
- `%(worktreepath)` includes the *current* worktree, so nil it when it equals the workroom's own path.
  Non-nil ⇒ a `git switch` **will** fail ⇒ the picker disables that row.
- Current ref comes from `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)`, **not** `%(HEAD)` — that returns
  nothing for detached/unborn HEAD, both already handled at `GitProvider.swift:78-98`. `%(HEAD)` is
  only the per-row `isCurrent` marker.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git … fetch <remote>` | **project root** |
| push | `git … push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| pull | `git … pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <remoteBranch>` | workroom |
| switch (local) | `git … switch <name>` | workroom |
| switch (remote-only) | `git … switch --track <remote>/<name>` | workroom |

- **No `--prune`, no `--no-write-fetch-head`** — let the repo's own `fetch.prune` decide, and we
  need `FETCH_HEAD`.
- `--set-upstream` **only** when no upstream exists yet; otherwise it rewrites config on every push.
- **Never** `--force` / `--force-with-lease`. Rejection ⇒ `.rejected` ⇒ the UI offers Pull.
- `--autostash` on pull is mandatory — workroom trees are always dirty.
- Explicit `<remote> <remoteBranch>` on pull (from `pullFrom ?? comparedTo`) so an upstream-less
  workroom can still pull.

#### jj — one process answers list + ahead/behind

`jj bookmark list --all-remotes --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager -T '<template>'`,
emitting NUL-separated: `name`, `remote`, `commit_id`, `committer timestamp`, `present`, `conflict`,
`tracked`, `tracking_ahead_count`, `tracking_behind_count`.

Four traps, all verified against jj 0.43 locally:
- The template keyword is **`self`**, not `ref` (`ref.name()` errors).
- `tracking_*_count()` on a non-remote ref renders the literal `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>`
  into the output — the `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing.
- **Drop `remote == "git"`** — a colocated repo has a pseudo-remote called `git` that `--all-remotes`
  includes. Not a remote; also keeps `remotes` clean.
- **jj's counts are inverted relative to git.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means
  *the remote is ahead* = git's **behind**. Swap on ingest, in one commented line, pinned by a
  cross-backend integration test.

Plus `present == 0` on an `@origin` row ⇒ `gone` (jj's `[gone]`); `tracked == 0` ⇒ `comparedTo` set
but counts `nil`. One record per `(name, remote)`; fold in Swift.

**Anonymous-branch counts.** When `currentRef.kind == .ancestor` (jj `@` carries no bookmark — the
normal workroom state, since `jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark), the bookmark row's
counts describe the *ancestor bookmark*, not the user's work. So when and only when `.ancestor`, run
two extra cheap local revset counts:

```
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@'  -T '"x\n"'  → ahead
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r '@..remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)'  -T '"x\n"'  → behind
```

`remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@` is exactly what bare `jj git push` sends, so the ahead count and
the Push button agree by construction.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | **project root** |
| push (bookmarked `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --bookmark <name>` | **project root** |
| push (anonymous `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --change <rev>` | **project root** |
| pull step 1 | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | project root |
| pull step 2 | `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote>` | workroom |
| switch | `jj new <name>` / `jj new <name>@<remote>` | workroom |

- **`--change` is jj's built-in anonymous-branch push** (confirmed on 0.43): it creates the bookmark,
  tracks it automatically, and names it via `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
  `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`). This is the answer for the unbookmarked workroom `@` — no
  hand-rolled naming policy, and the user's own template config is honoured.
- **Revision choice:** `@` if it has changes or a description, else `@-`. jj refuses to push a
  commit with an empty description, and a fresh `@` after `jj new` has neither. `WorkroomStatus
  .jjWorkingCopy` (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`) already carries `description` + `files`, so the model
  decides this with no extra process.
- **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock** — even a read (`jj git
  remote list` fails with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export … git_import_export.lock"*).
  So all jj mutations go through `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`, and the read path derives
  the remote list from `bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes instead of calling `jj git remote list`.
  `jj bookmark list --ignore-working-copy` takes no lock.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocesses** — it
  exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, so the gate would release while the abandoned
  call still held the lock. `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout` and `ProcessTree.killTree`s
  at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely dead. Compose `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }`
  with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Document this where written — it reads like a violation and isn't.
- **`jj new`, not `jj edit`.** `jj edit <bookmark>` makes the bookmarked (probably-pushed) commit
  itself the working copy. `jj new` puts a fresh `@` on top and leaves `kind == .ancestor`, which is
  exactly what the sidebar already renders as `"main ↑"` (`Models.swift:146`).
- **`jj new` must not get `--ignore-working-copy`** — it snapshots first, which is what preserves
  uncommitted edits into the old `@`.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`** — `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@`, the pull-rebase shape.
  Run it unconditionally: already-a-descendant prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts** — jj records conflicts *inside* commits. Never infer success
  from the exit code; re-read `workingStatus().conflicted` and return `.okWithConflicts`.

#### Last-fetch time — differs per backend

**git:** mtime of `<worktree gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD` via `FileManager.attributesOfItem`. No subprocess.
Resolve the gitdir purely: `.git` as directory ⇒ `<path>/.git/FETCH_HEAD`; `.git` as **file** (the
worktree case) ⇒ read it, strip `gitdir: `, trim.

`FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree**, which is why fetch runs at the project root for git too: fetching
inside workroom A would otherwise leave the project and every sibling workroom reading "never
fetched" while their `refs/remotes/*` are perfectly fresh. Running at the root makes "last fetched" a
per-**project** fact all workrooms agree on.

**jj: `FETCH_HEAD` is never written.** jj-lib 0.43 shells `git fetch --porcelain --prune
--no-write-fetch-head` (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`, *"ensures our request is invisible
to other parties"*). Verified empirically. So scan the op log instead:

```
jj op log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager --limit 200
  -T 'self.time().end().format("%s") ++ "\x00" ++ self.description().first_line() ++ "\n"'
```

Newest-first; take the first line whose description starts with `fetch from git remote`. Fragile
against a jj rewording — mitigated by prefix matching, a graceful failure mode (one absent label,
never a wrong one), and an integration test that turns red on a jj bump.

`VCSLastFetch` is a three-way enum (`.at(Date)` / `.never` / `.unknown`), not `Date?` — `.unknown`
must never render as "never" (the `VCSPushState.unknown` rule). No persisted stamp: after our own
fetch, set `.at(Date())` optimistically (the `applyOptimisticPRAction` pattern,
`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:220`) and let the re-read confirm — which also means a `git fetch`
typed in the workroom's own terminal moves the number.

### New models — appended to `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSModels.swift`

`VCSTracking { comparedTo, ahead: Int?, behind: Int?, gone, pullFrom }` — counts always from the
*local* ref's view; `nil` means unanswerable, never zero.
`VCSBranchRef { name, scope: .local/.remote(String), commitID, committedAt, isCurrent, checkedOutIn, tracking }`.
`VCSLastFetch { at(Date), never, unknown }`.
`VCSRemoteState { current: VCSRef, tracking, hasUnbookmarkedWork, refs, remotes, primaryRemote, lastFetch, resolvedAt, refsTruncated }`.

At the top of `VCSRemoteResolver.swift` (the `CIResolution`/`PRResolution` placement precedent):
`VCSRemoteAction { fetch, push, pull, switchRef }`,
`VCSRemoteFailure { toolMissing, timedOut, authRequired, noRemote, noUpstream, rejected, dirtyWorkingTree, alreadyCheckedOut, rebaseInProgress, locked, other }`,
`VCSRemoteResolution { state, absent, keepPrior, failed }`,
`VCSRemoteActionResult { ok, okWithConflicts, failed }`.

**Deliberately not folded into `VCSError`** — that enum is the *backend read* taxonomy and
`WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)` (`:90`) switches over it exhaustively to pick a sidebar badge.
`.authRequired` has no sidebar badge; adding it would force a meaningless answer there.

### Error classification — `static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?`

One pure function, `nil` on success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `is already used by worktree at` | `.alreadyCheckedOut(path:)` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `no tracking information for the current branch` | `.noUpstream` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<gitdir>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

`.authRequired` is the **#1 expected failure** and needs bespoke copy: `StatusCommandRunner:53` sets
`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` unconditionally and a GUI app has no tty, so HTTPS-without-a-helper fails
instantly (correct — never hang) with baffling stderr. Say: *"Workroom never prompts for credentials
— configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`) or use SSH."*

`.rebaseInProgress` must **not** offer Retry; it needs `git rebase --abort`. `.timedOut(.pull)` gets
upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` by the post-failure probe, because SIGKILLing a rebase mid-flight is
the one genuinely unsafe timeout.

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/RemoteStateModel.swift`

`@MainActor final class RemoteStateModel: ObservableObject`, owned by `AppStore` as a third sibling
to `fileTree` (`AppStore.swift:400`) and `commitHistory` (`:407`). Cloned structurally from
`Core/HistoryModel.swift`: same `State` enum + `isSettled`, the same **0.3 s pre-dispatch trailing
debounce** and cancel-and-replace, `focus`/`activate`/`refresh(force:)`/`awaitCurrentLoad()`, and the
`resolver`-injection seam.

Published: `snapshot: VCSRemoteState?`, `state`, `inFlight: VCSRemoteAction?` (one action at a time —
drives the spinner on the matching button and disables all of them), `lastFailure: VCSRemoteFailure?`
(kept **separate** from `state` so a failed push never blanks a good snapshot — the `.keepPrior` rule).
Derived: `canFetch` / `canPush` / `canPull`.

**TTL 15 s**, matching `localStatusTTL` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:14`) — the whole read is
local, same cost class as the status probe. Nothing here is a network read.

`var onDidMutate: (@MainActor (VCSRemoteAction) -> Void)?` wired by the store post-init (the
`lazy var workroomFileWatcher` idiom) so the model unit-tests with no `AppStore`.

**ObservableObject, not `@Observable`** — the whole tree is `@EnvironmentObject`, and `HistoryModel`/
`FileTreeModel` are `ObservableObject`. Mixing observation systems buys nothing.

### Store wiring — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift`

- `let remoteState: RemoteStateModel`, plus an `init(remoteState:)` parameter (the reason
  `commitHistory` is one).
- `var remoteToolbarShown: Bool { activeInspectorSection == .changes }` and
  `focusRemoteStateIfShown()`, gated on `inspectorIsVisible && remoteToolbarShown` — the
  `focusHistoryIfShown()` pattern verbatim (`:325-340`). Call at the same three sites:
  `selectedTargetID.didSet` (`:175`), `activeInspectorSection.didSet` (`:361`), and the
  `selectionHasTabs` flip (`:794`). Plus a `refreshRemoteStateIfActive()` twin beside
  `refreshHistoryIfActive()` (`:3659`), called from `RootView.swift:386`'s `didBecomeActiveNotification`.
- **Reuse the existing watcher, add none.** `rootBranchWatchers` (`:2307-2331`) already watches
  `vcsMetadataDir(path:vcs:)` recursively, which covers every signal this feature cares about for
  every workroom of that project: git `FETCH_HEAD` + `refs/remotes/*` + `worktrees/<n>/HEAD` +
  `packed-refs`, and jj `.jj/repo/op_heads` + `op_store` (a workroom's `.jj/repo` is a file pointing
  there). Add one visibility-gated `remoteState.refresh(force: true)` inside

# VCS toolbar: branch selection + push/pull/fetch status

## Context

The VCS inspector today can only *read*. `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`)
is a strictly read-only protocol — 8 members, no mutations, no network. There is **no** branch
listing, **no** fetch/push/pull, **no** ahead/behind counts, and **no** last-fetch time anywhere in
the app or the Rust core. The only place a branch name appears is a `.caption` capsule in the Changes
body (`ChangesPanel.swift:669-730`) and the status bar (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`), both
display-only.

So a user working in a workroom has to leave the app for every remote interaction: they can see what
changed but not whether it's pushed, how far behind origin they are, when they last fetched, or what
other branches exist — let alone act on any of it.

**Outcome:** a 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector, GitHub-Desktop shaped — current
branch as a dropdown that switches branches, a sync segment that reads "Push origin / Last fetched 9
minutes ago" with an ahead/behind count pill and performs the action on click, and a fetch icon
button. Working for **both** git and jj.

Scope confirmed with the user: **everything** — fetch, push, pull-with-rebase, and branch switch.
Toolbar shows **only when the Changes activity section is active**.

## Decisions

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Extend `VCSProviding`? | **No — zero changes.** New `VCSRemoteResolver` struct modelled 1:1 on `WorkroomStatusResolver`. |
| Backend | `git` / `jj` **CLI** via `StatusCommandRunning`. Auth comes free (credential helpers, ssh-agent, tokens); matches the existing `gh` precedent. |
| SwiftGitX for network? | **No.** `Repository+fetch.swift:30` / `+push.swift:49` pass `NULL` for the options struct ⇒ zero credential support, HTTPS impossible. `pull` doesn't exist (`// TODO: Implement pull`). |
| SwiftGitX for `switch`? | **No.** libgit2 doesn't enforce git's "already used by worktree at" guard — fatal given Workroom *is* worktrees. Also non-atomic, and `Repository.push` silently writes `remote.origin.push` into repo config. |
| Rust / UniFFI | **Zero changes.** No `make app-vcs`. |
| Auto-fetch | **Never.** Explicit user action only. |
| Toolbar visibility | Only when `store.activeInspectorSection == .changes`. |

## Engine

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSRemoteResolver.swift`

Shaped exactly like `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`: one `struct`, an injected
`StatusCommandRunning`, private `resolveGit`/`resolveJJ`, and `static` pure arg-builders/parsers/
classifiers that carry all the semantics (the `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` testability pattern).

```swift
struct VCSRemoteResolver: Sendable {
  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
  /// For `currentRef` only — reuse the app's canonical answer incl. `.ancestor`/`.detached`.
  /// Same seam + default as `BranchResolver.swift:20`.
  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5       // local ref listing
  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300    // network + rebase; SIGKILL here is dangerous
  var switchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
  var gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared
  var refCap: Int = 500

  func resolveState(path:vcs:projectRoot:) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
  func fetch(path:vcs:projectRoot:remote:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func push(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:setUpstream:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func pullRebase(path:vcs:projectRoot:current:remote:tracking:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func switchRef(path:vcs:projectRoot:to:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult

  /// THE placement rule (the `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory:364` pattern).
  static func opDirectory(_ action:path:vcs:projectRoot:) -> String
}
```

Reuse `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`:63`, `["-c","core.fsmonitor="]`) verbatim on every
git call. Every jj call gets `--color never --no-pager`; **reads** get `--ignore-working-copy`,
**mutations must not** (they need to snapshot).

#### git — one process answers list + current + ahead/behind

```
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate --count=<cap+1>
  --format=%(refname)%00%(refname:short)%00%(objectname)%00%(committerdate:unix)%00%(HEAD)%00%(worktreepath)%00%(upstream:short)%00%(upstream:track)%00%(push:short)%00%(push:track)%00%(symref)
  refs/heads refs/remotes
```

- `%00` NUL separators — `%(worktreepath)` is a path and can contain a tab. Skip records whose field
  count ≠ 11 rather than crashing.
- `--count=cap+1` to learn `refsTruncated` (the `GitProvider.log:25` idiom).
- **`%(push:short)`/`%(push:track)` is the whole ballgame.** Under the default `push.default=simple`
  they resolve to `<remote>/<same-name>` and its divergence **even with no upstream configured** —
  which is every Workroom branch, since a workroom is `git worktree add -b` (`internal/vcs/git.go:30`).
  Take `push:*` first, fall back to `upstream:*`, record which in `comparedTo`, set `pullFrom` only
  when they differ. No second `rev-list`, no `@{u}`.
- Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose short name is
  the bare `origin` (junk picker row). Its target gives the default branch for free.
- `%(worktreepath)` includes the *current* worktree, so nil it when it equals the workroom's own path.
  Non-nil ⇒ a `git switch` **will** fail ⇒ the picker disables that row.
- Current ref comes from `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)`, **not** `%(HEAD)` — that returns
  nothing for detached/unborn HEAD, both already handled at `GitProvider.swift:78-98`. `%(HEAD)` is
  only the per-row `isCurrent` marker.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git … fetch <remote>` | **project root** |
| push | `git … push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| pull | `git … pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <remoteBranch>` | workroom |
| switch (local) | `git … switch <name>` | workroom |
| switch (remote-only) | `git … switch --track <remote>/<name>` | workroom |

- **No `--prune`, no `--no-write-fetch-head`** — let the repo's own `fetch.prune` decide, and we
  need `FETCH_HEAD`.
- `--set-upstream` **only** when no upstream exists yet; otherwise it rewrites config on every push.
- **Never** `--force` / `--force-with-lease`. Rejection ⇒ `.rejected` ⇒ the UI offers Pull.
- `--autostash` on pull is mandatory — workroom trees are always dirty.
- Explicit `<remote> <remoteBranch>` on pull (from `pullFrom ?? comparedTo`) so an upstream-less
  workroom can still pull.

#### jj — one process answers list + ahead/behind

`jj bookmark list --all-remotes --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager -T '<template>'`,
emitting NUL-separated: `name`, `remote`, `commit_id`, `committer timestamp`, `present`, `conflict`,
`tracked`, `tracking_ahead_count`, `tracking_behind_count`.

Four traps, all verified against jj 0.43 locally:
- The template keyword is **`self`**, not `ref` (`ref.name()` errors).
- `tracking_*_count()` on a non-remote ref renders the literal `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>`
  into the output — the `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing.
- **Drop `remote == "git"`** — a colocated repo has a pseudo-remote called `git` that `--all-remotes`
  includes. Not a remote; also keeps `remotes` clean.
- **jj's counts are inverted relative to git.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means
  *the remote is ahead* = git's **behind**. Swap on ingest, in one commented line, pinned by a
  cross-backend integration test.

Plus `present == 0` on an `@origin` row ⇒ `gone` (jj's `[gone]`); `tracked == 0` ⇒ `comparedTo` set
but counts `nil`. One record per `(name, remote)`; fold in Swift.

**Anonymous-branch counts.** When `currentRef.kind == .ancestor` (jj `@` carries no bookmark — the
normal workroom state, since `jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark), the bookmark row's
counts describe the *ancestor bookmark*, not the user's work. So when and only when `.ancestor`, run
two extra cheap local revset counts:

```
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@'  -T '"x\n"'  → ahead
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r '@..remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)'  -T '"x\n"'  → behind
```

`remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@` is exactly what bare `jj git push` sends, so the ahead count and
the Push button agree by construction.

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | **project root** |
| push (bookmarked `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --bookmark <name>` | **project root** |
| push (anonymous `@`) | `jj git push --remote <r> --change <rev>` | **project root** |
| pull step 1 | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | project root |
| pull step 2 | `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote>` | workroom |
| switch | `jj new <name>` / `jj new <name>@<remote>` | workroom |

- **`--change` is jj's built-in anonymous-branch push** (confirmed on 0.43): it creates the bookmark,
  tracks it automatically, and names it via `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
  `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`). This is the answer for the unbookmarked workroom `@` — no
  hand-rolled naming policy, and the user's own template config is honoured.
- **Revision choice:** `@` if it has changes or a description, else `@-`. jj refuses to push a
  commit with an empty description, and a fresh `@` after `jj new` has neither. `WorkroomStatus
  .jjWorkingCopy` (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`) already carries `description` + `files`, so the model
  decides this with no extra process.
- **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock** — even a read (`jj git
  remote list` fails with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export … git_import_export.lock"*).
  So all jj mutations go through `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`, and the read path derives
  the remote list from `bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes instead of calling `jj git remote list`.
  `jj bookmark list --ignore-working-copy` takes no lock.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocesses** — it
  exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, so the gate would release while the abandoned
  call still held the lock. `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout` and `ProcessTree.killTree`s
  at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely dead. Compose `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }`
  with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Document this where written — it reads like a violation and isn't.
- **`jj new`, not `jj edit`.** `jj edit <bookmark>` makes the bookmarked (probably-pushed) commit
  itself the working copy. `jj new` puts a fresh `@` on top and leaves `kind == .ancestor`, which is
  exactly what the sidebar already renders as `"main ↑"` (`Models.swift:146`).
- **`jj new` must not get `--ignore-working-copy`** — it snapshots first, which is what preserves
  uncommitted edits into the old `@`.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`** — `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@`, the pull-rebase shape.
  Run it unconditionally: already-a-descendant prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts** — jj records conflicts *inside* commits. Never infer success
  from the exit code; re-read `workingStatus().conflicted` and return `.okWithConflicts`.

#### Last-fetch time — differs per backend

**git:** mtime of `<worktree gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD` via `FileManager.attributesOfItem`. No subprocess.
Resolve the gitdir purely: `.git` as directory ⇒ `<path>/.git/FETCH_HEAD`; `.git` as **file** (the
worktree case) ⇒ read it, strip `gitdir: `, trim.

`FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree**, which is why fetch runs at the project root for git too: fetching
inside workroom A would otherwise leave the project and every sibling workroom reading "never
fetched" while their `refs/remotes/*` are perfectly fresh. Running at the root makes "last fetched" a
per-**project** fact all workrooms agree on.

**jj: `FETCH_HEAD` is never written.** jj-lib 0.43 shells `git fetch --porcelain --prune
--no-write-fetch-head` (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`, *"ensures our request is invisible
to other parties"*). Verified empirically. So scan the op log instead:

```
jj op log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager --limit 200
  -T 'self.time().end().format("%s") ++ "\x00" ++ self.description().first_line() ++ "\n"'
```

Newest-first; take the first line whose description starts with `fetch from git remote`. Fragile
against a jj rewording — mitigated by prefix matching, a graceful failure mode (one absent label,
never a wrong one), and an integration test that turns red on a jj bump.

`VCSLastFetch` is a three-way enum (`.at(Date)` / `.never` / `.unknown`), not `Date?` — `.unknown`
must never render as "never" (the `VCSPushState.unknown` rule). No persisted stamp: after our own
fetch, set `.at(Date())` optimistically (the `applyOptimisticPRAction` pattern,
`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:220`) and let the re-read confirm — which also means a `git fetch`
typed in the workroom's own terminal moves the number.

### New models — appended to `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSModels.swift`

`VCSTracking { comparedTo, ahead: Int?, behind: Int?, gone, pullFrom }` — counts always from the
*local* ref's view; `nil` means unanswerable, never zero.
`VCSBranchRef { name, scope: .local/.remote(String), commitID, committedAt, isCurrent, checkedOutIn, tracking }`.
`VCSLastFetch { at(Date), never, unknown }`.
`VCSRemoteState { current: VCSRef, tracking, hasUnbookmarkedWork, refs, remotes, primaryRemote, lastFetch, resolvedAt, refsTruncated }`.

At the top of `VCSRemoteResolver.swift` (the `CIResolution`/`PRResolution` placement precedent):
`VCSRemoteAction { fetch, push, pull, switchRef }`,
`VCSRemoteFailure { toolMissing, timedOut, authRequired, noRemote, noUpstream, rejected, dirtyWorkingTree, alreadyCheckedOut, rebaseInProgress, locked, other }`,
`VCSRemoteResolution { state, absent, keepPrior, failed }`,
`VCSRemoteActionResult { ok, okWithConflicts, failed }`.

**Deliberately not folded into `VCSError`** — that enum is the *backend read* taxonomy and
`WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)` (`:90`) switches over it exhaustively to pick a sidebar badge.
`.authRequired` has no sidebar badge; adding it would force a meaningless answer there.

### Error classification — `static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?`

One pure function, `nil` on success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `is already used by worktree at` | `.alreadyCheckedOut(path:)` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `no tracking information for the current branch` | `.noUpstream` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<gitdir>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

`.authRequired` is the **#1 expected failure** and needs bespoke copy: `StatusCommandRunner:53` sets
`GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` unconditionally and a GUI app has no tty, so HTTPS-without-a-helper fails
instantly (correct — never hang) with baffling stderr. Say: *"Workroom never prompts for credentials
— configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`) or use SSH."*

`.rebaseInProgress` must **not** offer Retry; it needs `git rebase --abort`. `.timedOut(.pull)` gets
upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` by the post-failure probe, because SIGKILLing a rebase mid-flight is
the one genuinely unsafe timeout.

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSSyncPresentation.swift` — pure mapper

`static func make(_ snapshot: VCSSyncSnapshot, now: Date) -> VCSSyncPresentation`. No SwiftUI, no
`Date()` read — `now` is a parameter so the whole thing is unit-testable at fixed instants (the
`Core/ChangeBadge.swift` precedent). Returns `titleVariants: [String]` (longest first, `[]` ⇒
single-line mode), `subtitle`, `subtitleShort`, `symbol`, `badge`/`secondaryBadge`, `action`,
`isEnabled`, `tone`, `help`, `accessibility`, `accessibilityValue`.

| # | Condition | Title | Subtitle | Badge | Click |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | no target | — | "No workroom selected" | — | — |
| 2 | not a repo | — | "No repository" | — | — |
| 3 | no remote | — | "No remote configured" | — | — |
| 4 | no upstream / `gone` | "Publish branch" | "`<branch>` isn't on origin yet" | `N ↑` | push `--set-upstream` |
| 5 | never fetched, clean | — | "Never fetched" | — | fetch |
| 6 | clean, fetched | — | "Last fetched \(rel)" | — | fetch |
| 7 | ahead only | **"Push origin"** | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `N ↑` | push |
| 8 | behind only | "Pull origin with rebase" | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` | pull |
| 9 | **diverged** | "Pull origin with rebase" | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` then `N ↑` | **pull** |
| 10-12 | fetching/pushing/pulling | "Fetching…"/"Pushing…"/"Pulling…" | "from/to origin" | kept | disabled |
| 13 | failed, idle | previous title | error first line, `tone: .failure` | kept | retry |

Precedence: 13 > 10-12 > 1 > 2 > 3 > 4 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 5 > 6.

Two calls worth pinning with tests:
- **Diverged ⇒ Pull, not Push.** git refuses a non-fast-forward push anyway.
- **No upstream + ahead ⇒ `.publish`, not `.push`.** This is *the* workroom case — a git workroom is
  `git worktree add -b` with no upstream, ever. Getting it wrong makes every workroom read "Push
  origin" against an upstream that doesn't exist.

Relative time: `static func fetchedAgo(_ date:now:short:)` over two `static let
RelativeDateTimeFormatter`s (`.full` / `.abbreviated`); under 60 s ⇒ "just now". Do **not** reuse
`NotificationsList.timeAgo` — it's private and reads `Date()` internally, so it's untestable.

mouseDown, so the segment would stop being clickable with a real mouse while synthetic XCUITest
clicks kept passing. Offer `.contextMenu { Button("Copy Branch Name") }` instead.

**The relative timestamp ticks via `TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: 30))` wrapping only that
one `Text`**, calling the pure `fetchedAgo`. Redraws stay confined to the `Text`, it pauses
off-screen, and there's no `Timer`/`Task` lifecycle to leak. A `@Published clock` would re-render
every observer for a string.

### Layout degradation, 260 → 520pt

At 260 the ideal widths sum to ~287, so it *must* degrade. In firing order:
1. **Sync wins** — `layoutPriority(1)` vs branch `0`. A truncated branch name is still identifiable
   and its full name is repeated in the Changes header 40pt below plus its own tooltip.
2. Truncate, never wrap; every `Text` is `.lineLimit(1)`.
3. Subtitle abbreviates before truncating: "Last fetched 9 minutes ago" → "Fetched 9 min. ago".
4. Title abbreviates: "Pull origin with rebase" → "Pull with rebase" → "Pull".
5. **The "Current Branch" caption drops first** (below ~120pt of branch width) → name only, centred.
   At 260 the caption is not shown. Stated out loud rather than shipping a clipped caption.
6. The sync glyph drops next — the pill's arrow already carries direction.
7. The pill never yields (`.fixedSize()`).
8. Fixed 36pt height at every width; no reflow of the split view below.

Growing to 520: branch caps at 220 so a short name doesn't hoard dead space; sync takes
`maxWidth: .infinity` and absorbs the rest — the extra goes to the segment that can use it.

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/BranchPickerPopover.swift`

**`.popover`, not `Menu`.** A filter field is mandatory at hundreds of branches and `Menu` can't host
a `TextField` (it's NSMenu-backed); opening a `Menu` over ~800 `Button`s materializes ~800
NSMenuItems synchronously on the main thread — the shape of the recorded 2 s AppHang. `Menu` is
otherwise fine in this app (`prActionsMenu`, `ChangesPanel.swift:174`); it's the size and the text
field that rule it out.

300 × 360, structurally cloned from `Views/OpenWorkroomDialog.swift` — the app's existing
searchable-grouped-list picker. Reuse its `searchField` verbatim (`:153-181`), `ScrollViewReader` +
`LazyVStack(spacing: 2)`, group headers (`.system(size: 10, weight: .semibold)`, `fgMuted`,
uppercase), and `.onKeyPress(.upArrow/.downArrow/.return)` wiring (`:129-144`).

- **`PickerModel.filtered` (plain substring), not `fuzzyFiltered`** — branch names are hierarchical
  and users type prefixes; fuzzy would let `mnfx` hit `main-fix`, which is bad when a wrong pick
  checks out the wrong branch.
- Groups: `LOCAL`, then `REMOTE` listing only remotes with no local counterpart (so `main` isn't
  shown twice).
- Rows: leading 14pt slot with a `checkmark` for the current ref, name at
  `.system(size: 12, weight: .medium)` `.truncationMode(.middle)`, trailing dim `N ↑ M ↓`.
  **Rows with a non-nil `checkedOutIn` are disabled** with a "already checked out in `<path>`"
  tooltip — for git a switch *will* fail; for jj it's advisory (jj allows two workspaces on one
  bookmark), so jj rows stay enabled with the hint.
- `@State private var showPicker` — **never `@Default`** (async invalidation wouldn't open the
  popover on the same click).
- Branch list loads **only when the popover opens** (`.task { await model.loadBranches() }`).
- A "New branch…" footer is out of scope for this pass.

```swift

  let subs = store.activeInspectorSection.subSections

    InspectorSplitView(headers: …)                    // unchanged, verbatim
      .frame(minWidth: 260, maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)
```

Zero AppKit changes: `InspectorSplitView.sizeThatFits` (`:432-437`) returns the proposal, so the
`VStack` simply offers it 36pt less, and `InspectorPanePolicy.allocate` reads `splitView.bounds.height`
live at `viewDidLayout` (`:289-294`) — drag, weights persistence and `reallocateOnToggle` all keep
working.

**Not a section header** — `SectionHeader` is hosted at a hard 34pt constraint
(`InspectorSplitView.swift:95`), collapses with its pane, and lives behind an `NSHostingController`
boundary that doesn't inherit `@EnvironmentObject`. **Not `InspectorColumn`** — that owns only docked
chrome (width clamp, card, resize handle); the toolbar is inspector *content*. **Never a `.toolbar`
modifier** — the window toolbar is deliberately an empty AppKit `NSToolbar` because a SwiftUI toolbar
item's `menuFormRepresentation` caused a 2 s AppHang.

### Confirmation & error surfacing

- Fetch, Push, Publish: **never** confirm (non-destructive, and it's the point of the button).
- **Pull and branch-switch: confirm only when the working tree is dirty**
  (`store.workroomStatuses[sid]?.dirty == true`). Reuse `RightInspector`'s existing mechanism — a
  second `@State pendingVCSConfirm` + `.confirmationDialog` beside the PR one (`:15-16`, `:48-58`).
  Zero new machinery. Note the asymmetry: jj's switch never refuses on a dirty tree (it snapshots
  first); git's always might.
- Three tiers, and **not** `inspectorMessage(_:)` (a `.body`-sized full-width section-body
  placeholder — wrong shape for a 36pt bar):
  1. **Inline** in the sync subtitle: error's first line, `tokens.failure`,
     `exclamationmark.triangle.fill`, segment stays clickable to retry.
  2. **Full text in `.help(...)`**, since the subtitle truncates.
  3. **Escalate to the store's existing alert** (`errorTitle`/`errorMessage` → `RootView.swift:180-198`)
     only for state-changing failures — push rejected, auth failure, pull produced conflicts.
     Transient read failures stay inline. Rationale: a silently rejected push is a real problem.
- `.rejected` offers **Pull**, never Force. jj conflicts get *"Undo in the terminal with `jj undo`"* —
  jj's recovery story here is genuinely better and worth saying.

convention).

- `parseGitRefs`: real NUL-record fixture — symref rows dropped, `%(HEAD)=="*"` ⇒ `isCurrent`,

  preferred over `upstream:*`, `pullFrom` set only when they differ, `cap+1` ⇒ `truncated`, wrong

  `--rebase --autostash`; push carries `--set-upstream` only when asked and **never** `--force`;

## Build order

1. Models into `VCSModels.swift`.
2. `Core/VCSRemoteResolver.swift` — `resolveState` (both backends, one process each + the jj
   anonymous-count pair), last-fetch, all pure parsers/arg-builders, `classify`, `opDirectory`.
   **Write `VCSRemoteResolverTests` alongside** — this is where every semantic lives.
3. `Core/VCSSyncPresentation.swift` + its tests. State machine is the risky part and is fully
   testable headless, before any view exists.
4. `Core/RemoteStateModel.swift` + tests.
5. `AppStore` wiring + trigger tests + the fixture seed.
6. `Views/VCSToolbar.swift`, the 4-line `ChangesPanel.swift` insertion.
7. `Views/BranchPickerPopover.swift`.
8. Actions in order of risk: **fetch** (proves gate + timeout + auth path with the one safe
   mutation), then **push** + **switch**, then **pull-with-rebase** last (autostash, the
   `rebase-merge` probe, jj's two-step, jj's exit-0-with-conflicts).
9. `CommandMenu("Source Control")` + `isAppShortcut` + focused values.
10. Integration + XCUITest suites.

```bash

make app-format
make app-lint          # the hard gate
make app-test          # read summary from the .xcresult via xcresulttool; app-test hides it
```
`make app-*` needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`. No `make app-vcs` — zero Rust changes.

Then run it for real (`make app-run`) against this repo (git) **and** a throwaway colocated jj repo:
- branch name matches `git branch --show-current`; the dropdown lists what `git branch -a` lists;
- ahead/behind pills match `git rev-list --left-right --count @{push}...HEAD`;
- "Last fetched" matches `stat -f %Sm .git/FETCH_HEAD`, and moves after a terminal `git fetch`
  (proving the FSEvents path, not just our own optimistic write);
- fetch/push/pull/switch each work, and the failure copy is legible for: an HTTPS remote with no
  credential helper (`.authRequired`), switching to a branch held by a sibling workroom
  (`.alreadyCheckedOut`), and a diverged branch (Push ⇒ `.rejected` ⇒ offered Pull);
- **jj specifically:** an unbookmarked workroom `@` pushes via `--change` and creates a tracked
  `push-<id>` on the origin; `jj new` switching preserves uncommitted edits on the old `@`; a pull
  that conflicts surfaces as conflicted rather than silently "ok".
- Resize the inspector 260 → 520 and confirm the degradation ladder (caption drops at 260, no
  horizontal scroll, fixed 36pt height throughout).
- Toolbar hover/tooltips **with a real mouse** — synthetic hover lies in this codebase.

```bash
if [ -n "${CLAUDE_PLAN_FILE:-}${GSTACK_PLAN_MODE_FORCE:-}" ]; then
  export GSTACK_PLAN_MODE="active"
elif [ "${GSTACK_PLAN_MODE:-}" = "active" ]; then
  export GSTACK_PLAN_MODE="active"
else
  export GSTACK_PLAN_MODE="inactive"
fi
echo "GSTACK_PLAN_MODE: $GSTACK_PLAN_MODE"
[ -n "$OPENCLAW_SESSION" ] && echo "SPAWNED_SESSION: true" || true
```

## AskUserQuestion Format

### Tool resolution (read first)

"AskUserQuestion" can resolve to two tools at runtime: the **host MCP variant** (e.g. `mcp__conductor__AskUserQuestion` — appears in your tool list when the host registers it) or the **native** Claude Code tool.

**Conductor rule (read before the MCP rule):** if `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` was echoed by the preamble, do NOT call AskUserQuestion at all — neither native nor any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant. Render EVERY decision brief as the **prose form** below and STOP. This is proactive, not a reaction to a failure: Conductor disables native AUQ and its MCP variant is flaky (it returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`), so prose is the reliable path. **Auto-decide preferences still apply first:** if a `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` result has already surfaced for a question, proceed with that option (no prose). Because in Conductor you go straight to prose without ever calling the tool, this auto-decide-first ordering is enforced HERE, not only by the PreToolUse hook. When you render a Conductor prose brief, also capture it with `bin/gstack-question-log` (the PostToolUse capture hook never fires on a prose path, so `/plan-tune` history/learning depends on this call).

**Rule (non-Conductor):** if any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant is in your tool list, prefer it. Hosts may disable native AUQ via `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` (Conductor does, by default) and route through their MCP variant; calling native there silently fails. Same questions/options shape; same decision-brief format applies.

If AskUserQuestion is unavailable (no variant in your tool list) OR a call to it fails, do NOT silently auto-decide or write the decision to the plan file as a substitute. Follow the **failure fallback** below.

### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails

Tell three outcomes apart:

1. **Auto-decide denial (NOT a failure).** The result contains `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` — the preference hook working as designed. Proceed with that option. Do NOT retry, do NOT fall back to prose.
2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).
   - If it was present and **errored** (not absent), retry the SAME call **once** — but only if no answer could have surfaced (a missing-result error can arrive after the user already saw the question; retrying would double-prompt, so if it may have reached them, treat as pending, don't retry).
   - Then branch on `SESSION_KIND` (echoed by the preamble; empty/absent ⇒ `interactive`):
     - `spawned` → defer to the **Spawned session** block: auto-choose the recommended option. Never prose, never BLOCKED.
     - `headless` → `BLOCKED — AskUserQuestion unavailable`; stop and wait (no human can answer).
     - `interactive` → **prose fallback** (below).

**Prose fallback — render the decision brief as a markdown message, not a tool call.** Same information as the tool format below, different structure (paragraphs, not ✅/❌ bullets). It MUST surface this triad:

1. **A clear ELI10 of the issue itself** — plain English on what's being decided and why it matters (the question, not per-choice), naming the stakes. Lead with it.
2. **Completeness scores per choice** — explicit `Completeness: X/10` on EACH choice (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 3 shortcut); use the kind-note when options differ in kind not coverage, but never silently drop the score.
3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-line note to reply with a letter (in Conductor this is the normal path; elsewhere it means AskUserQuestion was unavailable or errored); the issue ELI10; the Recommendation line; then ONE paragraph per choice carrying its `(recommended)` marker, its `Completeness: X/10`, and 2-4 sentences of reasoning — never a bare bullet list; a closing `Net:` line. Split chains / 5+ options: one prose block per per-option call, in sequence. Then STOP and wait — the user's typed answer is the decision. In plan mode this satisfies end-of-turn like a tool call.

**Continuation — mapping a typed reply back to a brief.** Each brief carries a stable label (`D<N>`, or `D<N>.k` in a split chain). The user references it (e.g. "3.2: B"). A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Treat silence or "ok"/"sure" without the explicit choice as not-yet-confirmed.

### Format

Every AskUserQuestion is a decision brief and must be sent as tool_use, not prose — unless the documented failure fallback above applies (interactive session + the call is unavailable/erroring), in which case the prose fallback is the correct output.

```
D<N> — <one-line question title>
Project/branch/task: <1 short grounding sentence using _BRANCH>
ELI10: <plain English a 16-year-old could follow, 2-4 sentences, name the stakes>
Stakes if we pick wrong: <one sentence on what breaks, what user sees, what's lost>
Recommendation: <choice> because <one-line reason>
Completeness: A=X/10, B=Y/10   (or: Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score)
Pros / cons:
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)


## Artifacts Sync (skill start)

```bash
_GSTACK_HOME="${GSTACK_HOME:-$HOME/.gstack}"
# Prefer the v1.27.0.0 artifacts file; fall back to brain file for users
# upgrading mid-stream before the migration script runs.
if [ -f "$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt" ]; then
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt"
else
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-brain-remote.txt"
fi
_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync"
_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config"

# /sync-gbrain context-load: teach the agent to use gbrain when it's available.
# Per-worktree pin: post-spike redesign uses kubectl-style `.gbrain-source` in the
# git toplevel to scope queries. Look for the pin in the worktree (not a global
# state file) so that opening worktree B without a pin doesn't claim "indexed"
# just because worktree A was synced. Empty string when gbrain is not
# configured (zero context cost for non-gbrain users).
_GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"
if [ -f "$_GBRAIN_CONFIG" ] && command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _GBRAIN_VERSION_OK=$(gbrain --version 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^gbrain ' || echo 0)
  if [ "$_GBRAIN_VERSION_OK" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH=""
    _REPO_TOP=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$_REPO_TOP" ] && [ -f "$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source" ]; then
      _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH="$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source"
    fi
    if [ -n "$_GBRAIN_PIN_PATH" ]; then
      echo "GBrain configured. Prefer \`gbrain search\`/\`gbrain query\` over Grep for"
      echo "semantic questions; use \`gbrain code-def\`/\`code-refs\`/\`code-callers\` for"
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."
      echo "Run /sync-gbrain to refresh."
    else
      echo "GBrain configured but this worktree isn't pinned yet. Run \`/sync-gbrain --full\`"
      echo "before relying on \`gbrain search\` for code questions in this worktree."
      echo "Falls back to Grep until pinned."
    fi
  fi
fi

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

# Detect remote-MCP mode (Path 4 of /setup-gbrain). Local artifacts sync is
# a no-op in remote mode; the brain server pulls from GitHub/GitLab on its
# own cadence. Read claude.json directly to keep this preamble fast (no
# subprocess to claude CLI on every skill start).
_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="none"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude.json" ]; then
  _GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.type // .mcpServers.gbrain.transport // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in
    url|http|sse) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="remote-http" ;;
    stdio) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="local-stdio" ;;
  esac
fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
  if [ -n "$_BRAIN_NEW_URL" ]; then
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: artifacts repo detected: $_BRAIN_NEW_URL"
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: run 'gstack-brain-restore' to pull your cross-machine artifacts (or 'gstack-config set artifacts_sync_mode off' to dismiss forever)"
  fi
fi

if [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE="$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-pull"
  _BRAIN_NOW=$(date +%s)
  _BRAIN_DO_PULL=1
  if [ -f "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" ]; then
    _BRAIN_LAST=$(cat "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    _BRAIN_AGE=$(( _BRAIN_NOW - _BRAIN_LAST ))
    [ "$_BRAIN_AGE" -lt 86400 ] && _BRAIN_DO_PULL=0
  fi
  if [ "$_BRAIN_DO_PULL" = "1" ]; then
    ( cd "$_GSTACK_HOME" && git fetch origin >/dev/null 2>&1 && git merge --ff-only "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) || true
    echo "$_BRAIN_NOW" > "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE"
  fi
  "$_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN" --once 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if [ "$_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE" = "remote-http" ]; then
  # Remote-MCP mode: local artifacts sync is a no-op (brain admin's server
  # pulls from GitHub/GitLab). Show the user this is by design, not broken.
  _GBRAIN_HOST=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.url // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's|^https?://([^/:]+).*|\1|')
  echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: remote-mode (managed by brain server ${_GBRAIN_HOST:-remote})"
elif [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=0
  [ -f "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl" ] && _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=$(wc -l < "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl" | tr -d ' ')
```

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.

## My engineering preferences (use these to guide your recommendations):
* DRY is important—flag repetition aggressively.
* Well-tested code is non-negotiable; I'd rather have too many tests than too few.
* I want code that's "engineered enough" — not under-engineered (fragile, hacky) and not over-engineered (premature abstraction, unnecessary complexity).

## Cognitive Patterns — How Great Eng Managers Think

These are not additional checklist items. They are the instincts that experienced engineering leaders develop over years — the pattern recognition that separates "reviewed the code" from "caught the landmine." Apply them throughout your review.

1. **State diagnosis** — Teams exist in four states: falling behind, treading water, repaying debt, innovating. Each demands a different intervention (Larson, An Elegant Puzzle).
2. **Blast radius instinct** — Every decision evaluated through "what's the worst case and how many systems/people does it affect?"
3. **Boring by default** — "Every company gets about three innovation tokens." Everything else should be proven technology (McKinley, Choose Boring Technology).
4. **Incremental over revolutionary** — Strangler fig, not big bang. Canary, not global rollout. Refactor, not rewrite (Fowler).
5. **Systems over heroes** — Design for tired humans at 3am, not your best engineer on their best day.
6. **Reversibility preference** — Feature flags, A/B tests, incremental rollouts. Make the cost of being wrong low.
7. **Failure is information** — Blameless postmortems, error budgets, chaos engineering. Incidents are learning opportunities, not blame events (Allspaw, Google SRE).
8. **Org structure IS architecture** — Conway's Law in practice. Design both intentionally (Skelton/Pais, Team Topologies).
9. **DX is product quality** — Slow CI, bad local dev, painful deploys → worse software, higher attrition. Developer experience is a leading indicator.
10. **Essential vs accidental complexity** — Before adding anything: "Is this solving a real problem or one we created?" (Brooks, No Silver Bullet).
11. **Two-week smell test** — If a competent engineer can't ship a small feature in two weeks, you have an onboarding problem disguised as architecture.
12. **Glue work awareness** — Recognize invisible coordination work. Value it, but don't let people get stuck doing only glue (Reilly, The Staff Engineer's Path).
13. **Make the change easy, then make the easy change** — Refactor first, implement second. Never structural + behavioral changes simultaneously (Beck).
14. **Own your code in production** — No wall between dev and ops. "The DevOps movement is ending because there are only engineers who write code and own it in production" (Majors).
15. **Error budgets over uptime targets** — SLO of 99.9% = 0.1% downtime *budget to spend on shipping*. Reliability is resource allocation (Google SRE).

When evaluating architecture, think "boring by default." When reviewing tests, think "systems over heroes." When assessing complexity, ask Brooks's question. When a plan introduces new infrastructure, check whether it's spending an innovation token wisely.

content.content:
- Post `NSAccessibility.post(element:notification:)` `.selectedTextChanged` on selection change
  (we already detect mouseUp / copy-on-select) and a throttled `.valueChanged` on output so
  VoiceOver follows along; keep the role/label and report focus.
- Skip the full `NSAccessibility` text protocol (line/char-range/bounds geometry) — overkill for a
  terminal, and Muxy keeps it minimal too.

**Caveat:** terminal a11y is inherently partial (dynamic output, scrollback, full-screen TUIs);
target "announce output + selection, navigable text", not a perfect document model.

**Depends on:** the read APIs already present in 1.2.3 (`ghostty_surface_read_selection`,
`ghostty_surface_read_text`, `extractString`) in `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`;
best done after CMT-2 to use ghostty's `selection_changed` hook.

**Priority:** P2 (accessibility regression — address before GA, not blocking the beta).

## P2 — perf, correctness, and the next VCS phase

### VCS write actions — Phase 2 (macapp) — roadmap pointer

**What:** The next VCS phase: turn the read-only foundation into a full in-app VCS UI. Write methods
behind `VCSProviding` — commit/amend, push/pull/fetch, branch (git) / bookmark (jj) management — then
the deep jj ops (undo/op-log, split, absorb, evolog, interdiff). A `CLIVCSProvider` fallback is
introduced here for ops the libraries don't expose ergonomically (each with tests), NOT as a parallel
read path.

**Why:** This is a roadmap phase, not a tactical follow-up — it's tracked in full in the issue #59
plan (Phase 2 section) + the `vcs-foundation-rust-core` design notes. This entry is only a pointer so
Phase 2 is discoverable from `TODOS.md`; the authoritative scope + sequencing live in the plan.

**How to start:** Read the plan's "Phase 2 — VCS write actions" section and issue #59. The read
foundation (this file's other VCS entries) is the prerequisite; land the deferred read follow-ups
first where they'd otherwise bite the write UI. All three that gated this — jj **rename detection**,
**conflict status**, and the **error taxonomy** — have now shipped, so nothing in the read layer blocks
Phase 2. What's left of the taxonomy is one-sided (git still flattens to `.io`) and the stale-working-copy
**repair** is itself a write, so it belongs to this phase, not before it.

**Depends on:** the VCS read foundation (shipped, Phase 1). Spans `vcs/` (Rust), `WrVcs` UniFFI,
`Core/VCSProviding.swift` + both providers, and new write-flow UI.

**Priority:** P2 (the product direction; large, sequenced after the read follow-ups — see the plan for the real breakdown).

### `withTimeout` doesn't observe the CALLER's own cancellation (macapp) — VCS-foundation eng-review, /review follow-up

**Status:** the original version of this entry (a `withThrowingTaskGroup` awaiting a detached
operation child past its own deadline) is **fixed** — `Core/Timeout.swift` now races via a single
`withCheckedThrowingContinuation` + a `TimeoutGate`, exactly the fix this entry used to recommend.
Re-audited during the jj-snapshot-serialization `/review` (2026-07-24, cross-model: Codex found it)
and found a **different, still-live** gap in that same seam.

**What:** `withTimeout`'s `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` only resolves on ITS OWN internal race
(the operation finishing vs. its own `seconds` deadline firing) — it never wires up
`withTaskCancellationHandler`, so it does not observe the CALLING task being cancelled from outside.
Concretely: `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`'s `statusSweepTask?.cancel()` (a new sweep replacing an
old one) propagates into `runLocalSweep`'s `withTaskGroup` children structurally, but a cancelled
child's in-flight `withTimeout(seconds:) { … }` call (inside `resolveJJ`/`resolveGit`) keeps running
to completion (or its own `seconds` timeout) regardless — it doesn't stop early just because the
enclosing task gave up.

**Why:** Wastes CPU/time re-running a probe nobody wants anymore, and — post the jj-snapshot-gate
fix — adds unnecessary extra contention pressure on `JJSnapshotGate` (an unwanted, already-abandoned
caller still occupies a project's queue slot for up to its full timeout). Not corruption-causing
today: every call site already checks `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result
(`runLocalSweep`'s `if Task.isCancelled { break }`, etc.), so state stays correct — this is a
responsiveness/efficiency gap, not a data-integrity one.

**How to start:** Wrap `withTimeout`'s continuation in `withTaskCancellationHandler` so cancelling
the calling task settles the `TimeoutGate` early (same shape `JJSnapshotGate.run` already uses to
propagate cancellation into its own chained `Task`). Verify the existing "operation keeps running,
result dropped" contract still holds — this only makes the WAIT responsive to cancellation, not the
underlying synchronous native call (still uncancellable, unchanged).

**Depends on:** —. Touches `Core/Timeout.swift`. Broad blast radius (every `withTimeout` caller:
`WorkroomStatusResolver`, `BranchResolver`, `JJSnapshotGate`'s own internal use) — needs its own
careful review/testing, not a drive-by fix.

**Priority:** P2 (efficiency/responsiveness, not correctness; no user-visible bug today).

## P3 — VCS engine, diffs, and status

### Structured diff model (`FileDiff` hunks) for the diff viewer (macapp) — 47b / VCS-foundation follow-up

**What:** `withTimeout`'s `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` only resolves on ITS OWN internal race
(the operation finishing vs. its own `seconds` deadline firing) — it never wires up
`withTaskCancellationHandler`, so it does not observe the CALLING task being cancelled from outside.
Concretely: `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`'s `statusSweepTask?.cancel()` (a new sweep replacing an
old one) propagates into `runLocalSweep`'s `withTaskGroup` children structurally, but a cancelled
child's in-flight `withTimeout(seconds:) { … }` call (inside `resolveJJ`/`resolveGit`) keeps running
to completion (or its own `seconds` timeout) regardless — it doesn't stop early just because the
enclosing task gave up.

**Why:** Wastes CPU/time re-running a probe nobody wants anymore, and — post the jj-snapshot-gate
fix — adds unnecessary extra contention pressure on `JJSnapshotGate` (an unwanted, already-abandoned
caller still occupies a project's queue slot for up to its full timeout). Not corruption-causing
today: every call site already checks `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result
(`runLocalSweep`'s `if Task.isCancelled { break }`, etc.), so state stays correct — this is a
responsiveness/efficiency gap, not a data-integrity one.

**How to start:** Wrap `withTimeout`'s continuation in `withTaskCancellationHandler` so cancelling
the calling task settles the `TimeoutGate` early (same shape `JJSnapshotGate.run` already uses to
propagate cancellation into its own chained `Task`). Verify the existing "operation keeps running,
result dropped" contract still holds — this only makes the WAIT responsive to cancellation, not the
underlying synchronous native call (still uncancellable, unchanged).

**Depends on:** —. Touches `Core/Timeout.swift`. Broad blast radius (every `withTimeout` caller:
`WorkroomStatusResolver`, `BranchResolver`, `JJSnapshotGate`'s own internal use) — needs its own
careful review/testing, not a drive-by fix.

**Priority:** P2 (efficiency/responsiveness, not correctness; no user-visible bug today).

## P3 — VCS engine, diffs, and status

### Structured diff model (`FileDiff` hunks) for the diff viewer (macapp) — 47b / VCS-foundation follow-up

**Priority:** P3 (the state is now self-explaining; this saves the trip to a terminal).

### Background fetch so push state isn't stale (macapp) — unpushed-badge follow-up

**What:** A periodic / on-focus `git fetch` (and `jj git fetch`) so remote-tracking refs — and
therefore the History pane's unpushed badge — reflect the server rather than the last manual fetch.

**Why:** Every push-state answer in the app is local knowledge: `GitGraph` walks
`HEAD --not refs/remotes/origin/*` and the jj core evaluates `ancestors(<tracked @origin tips>)`.
Neither touches the network. So a commit pushed from another machine keeps its badge until you fetch,
and a commit that was force-pushed away still reads as pushed. The badge tooltip is honest about this
("based on your local remote-tracking refs"), but admitting it isn't fixing it.

**Pros:** The badge (and anything later built on the same reads — ahead/behind counts, a push action)
becomes truthful without the user doing anything.

**Cons:** This turns a pure local read into a network feature: auth prompts for private remotes, rate
limits, timeouts, and partial failures on a path that today cannot fail. It needs a cadence policy and
almost certainly a Settings toggle — "just add a fetch" is the wrong shape.

**Context / how to start:** The read path itself needs no change — a fetch only has to write refs; the
per-project watcher (`AppStore.handleRootBranchChange`, which watches each project's `.git`/`.jj`) then
repaints History automatically, exactly as it does after a local push. So the work is entirely about
*when* to fetch and how to fail quietly: pick the trigger (app focus + an interval), keep it off the
synchronous log-read path, decide the credential story (the status sweep already shells `gh`, so there
is precedent for network reads), and surface failure without a modal. Deliberately NOT done as part of
the badge: see the "Staleness" trap in the unpushed-badge plan.

**Depends on:** the unpushed badge (shipped). Likely wants a `Defaults` key + Settings row.

**Priority:** P3 (the badge is useful without it; multi-machine users feel this first).

### Three independent change-badge palettes (macapp) — jj conflict-status follow-up

content.text:
## Step 0 — Scope challenge

**Complexity check: TRIGGERS.** 19 files (12 source + 7 test), 3 new services (`VCSRemoteResolver`, `RemoteStateModel`, `VCSSyncPresentation`) plus ~7 view structs.

**Existing code that already solves sub-problems** (all correctly reused in the plan): `WorkroomStatusResolver` is the resolver template + owns `gitHardening` and the `ghProbeDirectory` jj-root rule; `HistoryModel` is the debounce/`runBlocking`/focus template; `rootBranchWatchers` + `handleRootBranchChange` already watch exactly the dirs that change on fetch/push/switch; `OpenWorkroomDialog` is the searchable-picker to clone; `currentRef` already answers the branch name incl. `.ancestor`/`.detached`.

**TODOS.md cross-reference — two hits:**

- **`TODOS.md:118-127` "VCS write actions — Phase 2" conflicts with this plan.** It says write ops go *"each behind `VCSProviding` write methods. A `CLIVCSProvider` fallback is introduced here for ops the libraries don't expose ergonomically … NOT as a parallel read path."* The living plan at `~/.claude/plans/https-github-com-joelmoss-workroom-issue-generic-plum.md:89-93` says the same and is named authoritative. My plan does the opposite — a standalone resolver, CLI as primary, `VCSProviding` untouched. This is the review's biggest finding.
- **`TODOS.md:324` "Background fetch so push state isn't stale"** overlaps but doesn't conflict — it wants *automatic* fetch and concludes *"'just add a fetch' is the wrong shape"*. A manual Fetch button plus a visible "last fetched" label is the smaller, safer thing and delivers that entry's stated pros ("ahead/behind counts, a push action") without its cons. It should be narrowed to *background* fetch afterward, not closed.

**Verified against this repo** (`push.default=current`, not `simple` as the plan states — fix that line): `%(push:short)` and `%(upstream:short)` both resolve to `origin/master`, `%(push:track)` = `[ahead 5]`. Your screenshot's "5 ↑" is this repo. The one-command read works.

**Search check:** skipped WebSearch — the two candidate approaches were both verified empirically against the installed git 2.55 / jj 0.43 rather than from docs. **[Layer 1]** for the CLI shell-out (git/jj themselves are the tried-and-true tool, and `gh` is existing in-repo precedent); **[Layer 3]** for the jj ahead/behind inversion and `--no-write-fetch-head` findings, both discovered from first principles by reading jj-lib source and reproducing.

**Genuinely reducible complexity — 4 dead or premature fields, no features:**

| Item | Why cut |
|---|---|
| `VCSBranchRef.tracking` | Per-row `↑2 ↓1` in picker rows. You asked for "a list of branches" — this is mine, and it's 500 allocations for it |
| `VCSTracking.pullFrom` | Triangular-remote field the plan itself defers surfacing to phase 4. Verified equal to `upstream` here. Use `upstream:short` for pull, `push:short` for push |
| `VCSRemoteState.hasUnbookmarkedWork` | Redundant — `current.kind == .ancestor` is already in the same struct |
| `VCSRemoteFailure.noUpstream` | Dead. We always pass explicit `<remote> <branch>`, so git never emits "no tracking information" |

The rest of the count is irreducible for the scope you chose, and 7 of 19 files are tests — which you want.

questions.question:
D3 — Complexity check tripped, and the plan contradicts a recorded decision. Reduce, or proceed as-is? <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-scope-reduction>

Project/branch: workroom on `master`. 19 files, 3 new services. Your feature scope (fetch + push + pull + switch) is settled and I'm not re-asking it — this is about the plan's shape.

ELI10: A "seam" is the single place code goes through to reach something — here, VCS operations. Today all VCS reads go through one protocol, `VCSProviding`, and `VCS.provider(for:)` decides git-or-jj once. Your own recorded roadmap (TODOS.md:118 and the issue #59 living plan) says write operations — push/pull/fetch now, then commit/amend, branch management, jj split/absorb/undo later — should all land behind that same protocol, with a CLI-backed conformer for what the libraries can't do. My plan ignored that and built a standalone resolver instead. The agent that proposed it didn't know your roadmap existed.

Why it matters beyond this feature: if each write op gets its own standalone resolver, Phase 2's six-or-so remaining operations each re-derive repo kind and each wire their own runner. You end up with six resolvers where you planned one seam.

Stakes if we pick wrong: proceeding as-is ships a working toolbar but quietly forks your VCS architecture, and the fork gets 6x more expensive to undo with every Phase 2 op. Over-correcting onto the read protocol re-introduces the thing that made me avoid it: nothing then structurally stops a read path firing a network mutation.
