37	  /// confirmation into this, so it needs its own copy — telling the user to configure a credential
38	  /// helper would be wrong advice.
39	  case hostKeyUnverified(String)
40	  case noRemote
41	  /// Push rejected (non-fast-forward). The engine NEVER force-pushes; the UI offers Pull.
42	  case rejected(String)
43	  /// git refused because tracked files would be overwritten.
44	  case dirtyWorkingTree(String)
45	  /// A failed or killed `git pull --rebase` left `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` behind. The repo needs
46	  /// `git rebase --abort`, so the UI must offer that instead of a retry that will fail identically.
47	  case rebaseInProgress

79	/// **reads** VCS data through", and four resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no
80	/// gate. Putting `fetch` there would mean nothing structurally prevented a read path from firing a

+  /// An empty resolver answer must not blank the label — it should fall through, not win with "".
+  func testEmptyResolvedNameDoesNotWin() {
+    let store = makeStore()
+    let sid = SidebarID.workroom(project: "/p", name: "feat")
+    store.workroomStatuses[sid] = WorkroomStatus(branchForCI: "from-sweep")
+    store.setResolvedBranchName("", for: sid)

+  /// **The performance guard.** Reading a branch label must cost NOTHING — every source is a cache
+  /// already filled by something else. The sidebar and status bar render this per row, so a read that
+  /// quietly opened a repo would reproduce the recorded `history-eager-focus-is-a-full-vcs-read`
+  /// starvation, which is invisible in tests unless something asserts it.
+  func testBranchNameNeverTouchesAVCSProvider() {
+    let counter = ProviderCallCounter()
+    let store = makeStore()
+    let sid = SidebarID.workroom(project: "/p", name: "feat")
+    store.workroomStatuses[sid] = WorkroomStatus(branchForCI: "feature/login")
+    store.workroomStatuses[.root(project: "/p")] = WorkroomStatus(branchForCI: "main")
+    // Read every shape: workroom, project root, unresolved, and through the wrapper.
+    _ = store.branchName(for: sid)
+    _ = store.branchName(for: .root(project: "/p"))
+    _ = store.branchName(for: .workroom(project: "/p", name: "does-not-exist"))
+    _ = store.branchLabel(for: store.target(for: sid)!)
+    XCTAssertEqual(
+      counter.calls, 0,
+      "branchName must read caches only — it is called per sidebar row and per status-bar render")

+/// that `branchName` has no seam through which a provider could be reached at all, so if a future edit
+/// adds one, it will have to be given this stub and the count assertion will start failing.
+private final class ProviderCallCounter: @unchecked Sendable {
+  private(set) var calls = 0
+  func record() { calls += 1 }

Halfway through the build, all green. Where things stand:

**Completed (1501 tests passing, lint clean):**

| Step | What landed |
|---|---|
| 1 | Remote-state models — `VCSTracking`, `VCSLastFetch`, `VCSRemoteState` |
| 2 | Runner hardening — stdin pinned, ssh `BatchMode`, auth vars forwarded (+8 tests) |
| 3 | Version floor — git ≥ 2.41 required / jj ≥ 0.43 optional, per-VCS scoped (+26 tests) |
| 4 | `VCSWriting` protocol + `CLIVCSWriter` — both P1 bug fixes (+54 tests) |
| 5 | `VCSSyncPresenter` — 13-state machine (+29 tests) |
| 6 | One branch-name accessor, 4 surfaces (+5 tests, 4 originals still green) |

**Three things I verified against real tools rather than trusting the plan:**

1. **The jj templates work** — including that `main@git` (the colocated pseudo-remote) really does appear in `--all-remotes` output and must be dropped.
2. **`jj git fetch` doesn't write `FETCH_HEAD`** — confirmed absent, so the op-log scan is genuinely necessary.
3. **The git read path end-to-end on this repo** — `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` is present as a symref (confirming the drop is needed), and `rev-list --left-right --count` returns `5\t0`, matching your screenshot exactly and identically under `push.default=simple`.

**One new bug found and fixed, which the plan had wrong:**

A `jj git fetch` that brings nothing prints `Nothing changed.` and records **no operation at all**. So the op-log scan means "last fetch that *changed* something" — a user clicking Fetch with nothing new would watch a stale timestamp sit there. git doesn't have this problem (it rewrites `FETCH_HEAD` on every fetch, verified). Fixed with a `vcs.lastFetch` Defaults key: the writer reports the backend's own evidence, and the model will take `max(that, our own recorded fetch)`, so a terminal-side fetch still wins when it's newer.

**Two of my own tests I caught being bad and rewrote:**
- A BatchMode assertion that would flake on any machine exporting `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` → made differential.
- The "no VCS calls" guard was **vacuous** — I built a counter, never wired it to anything, and asserted zero. Replaced with a cost assertion: 2000 reads must finish in under 0.5s, which a single subprocess would blow past. Runs in 0.013s.

**Remaining:** `RemoteStateModel` + store wiring (7), the toolbar itself with fetch live (8), push and pull (9), UI + `file://` integration tests (10), `TODOS.md` (11), final gate (12).

Per-project ref cache (D12), 15s TTL. Post-gate conflict upgrade (D7). Auto-fetch on inspector focus with interval guard, silent failure, skipped under fixture (D16). AppStore: let remoteState, focusRemoteStateIfShown gated on inspectorIsVisible && activeInspectorSection == .changes at the 3 existing focusHistoryIfShown sites, handleRootBranchChange hook, fixture seed. New RemoteStateModelTests + VCSRemoteTriggerTests.

content.subject: Build VCSToolbar with fetch working
content.description: New Views/VCSToolbar.swift: VCSToolbarMetrics, 3 segments, full-bleed dividers, whole-cell hover, themeTick, TimelineView on the timestamp only. Segment 1 read-only routing to Cmd-O (D14, no chevron). Segment 3 arrow.down.circle. Degradation ladder with the staleness caveat outranking the count pill (T14). 4-line VStack insertion in ChangesPanel.swift gated on activeInspectorSection == .changes. Fetch live on arrival.

content.subject: Add push, then pull with abort
content.description: Push (git push --set-upstream when no upstream; jj --bookmark or --change with @ vs @- chosen by emptiness). Then pull: git fetch-at-root then pull --rebase --autostash, jj fetch then rebase -b @. Dirty-tree confirmation reusing RightInspector's confirmationDialog. rebase --abort affordance, never Retry for .rebaseInProgress. Each with its CommandMenu item (Fetch OptShiftCmdF, Push ShiftCmdP, Pull OptShiftCmdP), the isAppShortcut edit, focused values, and its flow test.

content.subject: Add UI tests and the file:// integration suite
content.description: Fixture action recording (D11) plus 9 UITests and 4 flow tests; applyFixtureDefaults must pin Defaults[.inspectorLayout] = .default per the recorded learning. New VCSRemoteIntegrationTests.swift with file:// remotes: counts identical under all four push.default values (pins D13), fetch-at-root moves a workroom's label (pins D15), jj git fetch does NOT touch FETCH_HEAD, cross-backend VCSTracking parity (pins the jj inversion), anonymous jj push creates push-<id>.

content.subject: Update TODOS.md (D18, D19)
content.description: Rewrite TODOS.md:118 (write ops now behind VCSWriting + VCS.writer, not VCSProviding; fetch/push/pull landed; commit/amend, bookmark mgmt and deep jj ops remain) and TODOS.md:324 (narrow to Settings toggle + cadence policy for the auto-fetch that now runs on inspector focus, keeping its staleness reasoning). **What landed in step 7:**
- `Core/RemoteStateModel.swift` — cloned from `HistoryModel`: pre-dispatch debounce, cancel-and-replace, 15s TTL, single-action guard, `keepPrior` on blips, auto-fetch with a 5-minute per-project interval.

- 43 tests across `RemoteStateModelTests` (28) and `VCSRemoteTriggerTests` (15).

**Two real bugs my own tests caught:**

1. **`awaitCurrentLoad` awaited in the wrong order.** It awaited the load task before the action task — but an action *schedules* a load when it finishes, so it returned before the post-fetch refresh existed. The jj fetch-stamp test failed on it. Fixed by awaiting the action first.

2. **My refocus assertion was wrong, not the code.** I expected one extra read; there are two, because a successful auto-fetch triggers its own post-mutation refresh. Corrected the assertion and documented why.

**One thing I did differently from the plan:** the trigger tests use a real model injected with a counting writer, not a spy subclass — `RemoteStateModel` is `final`, and `HistoryLiveRefreshTests` already established counting-provider as the house pattern for exactly this question.

**Notable:** the gate tests now cover something the plan didn't anticipate mattering as much — with auto-fetch enabled, an ungated trigger means automatic *network* calls behind a closed inspector, not just wasted reads. `testRefocusDoesNothingWhenHidden` pins that.

Next is step 8 — the toolbar view itself, with fetch live on arrival. That's the first step where you'll be able to see anything.

That's the populated case, and it caught a real layout bug. The branch reads `fe...gin` — `.middle` truncation working, but crushed to ~60pt of text in a ~410pt inspector.

Cause: giving the sync segment `layoutPriority(1)` **and** `maxWidth: .infinity` means it's offered space first and claims all of it, so the branch is pinned at its 100pt floor and `branchMaxWidth` never applies. Removing the priority overrides — the min widths already guarantee 260pt fits.

        divider

3	/// Every number the VCS toolbar uses, in one place.
4	///
5	/// The horizontal ones are chosen so the toolbar aligns *by construction* with the section header
6	/// beneath it rather than by eye: `outerInset` + `glyphSlot` + `glyphSpacing` puts the branch glyph's
7	/// centre and the branch name's left edge exactly where `SectionHeader`'s chevron centre and title land
8	/// (`InspectorSplitView.headerLabel` uses the same 12 / 12 / 7).
9	enum VCSToolbarMetrics {
10	  /// 11pt semibold title (13pt line) + 1pt + 10pt caption (12pt line) = 26, plus 5pt above and below.
11	  /// Two lines genuinely don't fit the section headers' 34pt, and 36 also reads as a distinct band.
12	  static let height: CGFloat = 36
13	  static let outerInset: CGFloat = 12
14	  /// Inner edges of the segments — tighter than `outerInset` so the middle segment isn't starved.
15	  static let innerInset: CGFloat = 8
16	  /// Matches `SectionHeader`'s chevron `.frame(width: 12)`.
17	  static let glyphSlot: CGFloat = 12
18	  /// Matches `SectionHeader`'s `HStack(spacing: 7)`.
19	  static let glyphSpacing: CGFloat = 7
20	  /// Between the inspector's 11pt header glyphs and the pane bar's 13pt action icons: it has to hold
21	  /// against a bold 11pt title without reading as a pane-bar button.
22	  static let glyph: CGFloat = 12
23	  /// 22pt well plus 4pt either side — `ToolbarIconButtonStyle.footprint` rounded to a divider-bounded cell.
24	  static let fetchWidth: CGFloat = 30
25	
26	  static let titleFont = Font.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)
27	  static let captionFont = Font.system(size: 10)
28	  /// The single-line states. A lone 10pt dim line in a 36pt bar reads as a rendering bug, so the solo
29	  /// subtitle is a step up in both size and contrast.
30	  static let soloFont = Font.system(size: 11)
31	
32	  /// Floors, chosen so the inspector's 260pt minimum fits with room to spare:
33	  /// `branchMin + syncMin + fetchWidth + 2 dividers = 258`.
34	  static let branchMinWidth: CGFloat = 100
35	  /// Caps the branch cell so a short name can't hoard space the sync segment can use.
36	  static let branchMaxWidth: CGFloat = 220
37	  static let syncMinWidth: CGFloat = 126
38	  /// Below this the "Current Branch" caption drops — the icon already says "branch", and it's the least
39	  /// useful pixel in the bar.
40	  static let branchCaptionThreshold: CGFloat = 120

42	  /// Verbatim from `PRNumberBadge`, so the toolbar's pill matches the ref pill 40pt below it.
43	  static let pillHorizontalPadding: CGFloat = 5
44	  static let pillVerticalPadding: CGFloat = 1
45	}

47	/// The VCS toolbar: current branch, a sync segment that shows and performs the right remote action, and
48	/// a fetch button — divided into three full-height cells.
49	///
50	/// Lives at the top of `RightInspector`, above the section stack, and only for the Changes activity
51	/// section. Deliberately a plain SwiftUI view inside the inspector's content and **never** a `.toolbar`
52	/// modifier: the window toolbar is kept an empty AppKit `NSToolbar` because a SwiftUI toolbar item's
53	/// overflow `menuFormRepresentation` caused a multi-second app hang.
54	struct VCSToolbar: View {
55	  /// Raised when an action needs confirming first — currently only a pull over a dirty working tree.
56	  /// The dialog lives in `RightInspector` beside the PR one rather than here, so the inspector keeps
57	  /// one confirmation mechanism.
58	  let onNeedsConfirmation: (VCSRemoteAction, SidebarID) -> Void
59	
60	  @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore
61	  @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
62	  /// `ThemeService.shared` isn't observed by SwiftUI, so a theme switch would otherwise leave the
63	  /// hairlines stale. Same pattern as `ActivityBar`.
64	  @State private var themeTick = 0
65	
66	  private var theme: ThemeTokens { ThemeService.shared.tokens }
67	  private var model: RemoteStateModel { store.remoteState }
68	
69	  /// The toolbar's whole state, resolved in one place so the three segments can't disagree.
70	  private func presentation(now: Date) -> VCSSyncPresentation {
71	    VCSSyncPresenter.make(
72	      state: model.snapshot, hasTarget: model.target != nil,

Step 8 complete — the toolbar is real and rendering. **1551 tests, 0 failures, lint clean.**

**Ran it live under an isolated `$HOME`**, not your real config — auto-fetch would otherwise have hit your actual jj remotes at Harley Therapy. Built a throwaway git repo with a `file://` origin, 5 commits ahead, dirty tree, plus a `coral-bone` worktree with no counterpart.

**A real layout bug that only running it would have found.** The branch name rendered as `fe…gin` in a ~410pt inspector. Cause: I gave the sync segment `layoutPriority(1)` *and* `maxWidth: .infinity`, so it was offered the full width first and claimed all of it — the branch cell got pinned at its 100pt floor and `branchMaxWidth` never applied. Removing both priority overrides fixes it; the min widths already guarantee 260pt fits. Now it reads "Current Branch" over **`feature/login`**, with the caption shown because there's room.

The alignment-by-construction paid off: `feature/login`'s left edge lands exactly on the "Changes" title below it, and the branch glyph on its chevron — same 12/12/7 as `SectionHeader`.

**What I couldn't verify live, and why:** synthetic clicks don't drive this SwiftUI sidebar (the documented failure mode in this codebase — I tried coordinate clicks and the accessibility `selected` API, both no-ops). So the *populated* remote states — "Push origin", the `5 ↑` pill, "Last fetched 9 minutes ago" — aren't yet visually confirmed. They're covered by 29 presenter unit tests, and step 10's XCUITest fixture is built precisely to seed those states. A real-mouse pass is yours.

Also added `VCSToolbarMetricsTests` (7 tests) asserting the geometry rather than eyeballing it: the floors sum to 258 ≤ 260, and the leading offsets match `SectionHeader`'s exactly.

### VCS write actions — Phase 2 (macapp) — roadmap pointer

**What:** The next VCS phase: turn the read-only foundation into a full in-app VCS UI. Write methods
behind `VCSProviding` — commit/amend, push/pull/fetch, branch (git) / bookmark (jj) management — then
the deep jj ops (undo/op-log, split, absorb, evolog, interdiff). A `CLIVCSProvider` fallback is
introduced here for ops the libraries don't expose ergonomically (each with tests), NOT as a parallel
read path.

**Why:** This is a roadmap phase, not a tactical follow-up — it's tracked in full in the issue #59
plan (Phase 2 section) + the `vcs-foundation-rust-core` design notes. This entry is only a pointer so
Phase 2 is discoverable from `TODOS.md`; the authoritative scope + sequencing live in the plan.

**How to start:** Read the plan's "Phase 2 — VCS write actions" section and issue #59. The read
foundation (this file's other VCS entries) is the prerequisite; land the deferred read follow-ups
first where they'd otherwise bite the write UI. All three that gated this — jj **rename detection**,
**conflict status**, and the **error taxonomy** — have now shipped, so nothing in the read layer blocks
Phase 2. What's left of the taxonomy is one-sided (git still flattens to `.io`) and the stale-working-copy
**repair** is itself a write, so it belongs to this phase, not before it.

**Depends on:** the VCS read foundation (shipped, Phase 1). Spans `vcs/` (Rust), `WrVcs` UniFFI,
`Core/VCSProviding.swift` + both providers, and new write-flow UI.

**Priority:** P2 (the product direction; large, sequenced after the read follow-ups — see the plan for the real breakdown).

input.new_string:
**What:** The next VCS phase: turn the read-only foundation into a full in-app VCS UI. **Fetch, push
and pull-with-rebase have SHIPPED** (the VCS toolbar). What remains: commit/amend, bookmark (jj) /
branch (git) management, and the deep jj ops (undo/op-log, split, absorb, evolog, interdiff).

**Where the write seam actually is — this changed.** The original plan put write methods on
`VCSProviding` with a `CLIVCSProvider` fallback. That is **not** what shipped, and new work should not
follow it. Writes live behind a **separate** `VCSWriting` protocol (`Core/VCSWriting.swift`) with its
own factory `VCS.writer(for:)`, conformed by `CLIVCSWriter`. Two reasons, both load-bearing:

- `VCSProviding`'s doc calls it "the single seam the app **reads** VCS data through", and four
  resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no gate. A `fetch` on that protocol means
  nothing structurally stops a read path firing a network mutation — the opposite of what
  `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee.
- A CLI-backed method needs an injected `StatusCommandRunning`, and `GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider` are
  stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one. A new conformer has
  somewhere.

So: add commit/amend and the rest as `VCSWriting` members, and they inherit the gate, the network
environment hardening and the failure taxonomy for free.

**Why:** This is a roadmap phase, not a tactical follow-up. The authoritative scope + sequencing live
in the issue #59 plan; this entry is the pointer that makes it discoverable.

**How to start:** Read `Core/VCSWriting.swift` — its doc comment carries the routing diagram, the
per-backend command table and the placement rules (fetch always runs at the project root, for both
backends; jj push too, because bookmarks are repo-global). The read layer blocks nothing. What's left
of the error taxonomy is one-sided (git still flattens to `.io`), and the stale-working-copy **repair**
is itself a write, so it belongs to this phase.

**Depends on:** the VCS read foundation (shipped, Phase 1) and the write seam (shipped with the
toolbar). Spans `Core/VCSWriting.swift`, possibly `vcs/` (Rust) + `WrVcs` UniFFI for native jj ops, and
new write-flow UI.

**Priority:** P2 (the product direction; large — see the plan for the real breakdown).

input.new_string:
**Priority:** P2 (efficiency/responsiveness, not correctness; no user-visible bug today).

### Gate git VCS *reads*, not just writes (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up

**What:** Route git status reads through the same per-project `JJSnapshotGate` the writes now use.

**Why:** The toolbar's write path gates git as well as jj, because a project's workrooms are
`git worktree add` worktrees sharing ONE `.git` — a lock lost mid-`pull --rebase` can leave a workroom
wedged in a rebase. But that only half-closes the contention: `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit`
never touches the gate (only `resolveJJ` does), so a fetch writing `packed-refs` while the ungated
status sweep runs `git status` across N sibling worktrees reproduces exactly the
`packed-refs.lock could not be obtained` failure the gate's own doc cites.

**Pros:** removes the last window where `.locked` is an *expected* outcome rather than an anomaly, so
the UI's Retry affordance becomes a genuine edge case.

**Cons:** serialising reads could measurably slow the status sweep, which fans out per workroom by
design. This wants measurement first — it may be that read/write contention is rare enough in practice
that the cost isn't worth it.

**Context / how to start:** `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit` (the ungated read) vs `resolveJJ` (the
gated one); `CLIVCSWriter.gated` for how the writes do it. Note the gate is key-based and
backend-agnostic, so if this lands, renaming `JJSnapshotGate` → `RepoWriteGate` (3 call sites + its
test suite) stops being speculative churn and starts being accurate.

**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).

**Priority:** P3 (a real but narrow race; needs measurement before it's worth the sweep's latency).

### jj sibling-workspace staleness after a rebase (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up

**What:** Detect and surface when a jj operation in one workroom leaves a *sibling* workspace stale.

**Why:** All workrooms of a jj project share one repo and op-store. `jj rebase -b @` — what
pull-with-rebase runs — rewrites commits, and any other workspace whose `@` descends from a rewritten
commit is marked stale and needs `jj workspace update-stale` before its next command. Today that
surfaces as an unexplained error in a **different** workroom from the one the user acted in, which is
the worst attribution problem available: nothing on screen connects cause to effect.

**Pros:** turns a mystery error into an explained one, and the repair is a single command Workroom
could offer as a button.

**Cons:** needs a cheap way to detect staleness across workspaces without reading each one (a per-op
check would multiply the cost of every pull).

**Context / how to start:** `VCSStatusFailure.staleWorkingCopy` already exists in the taxonomy, and
`RustJJProvider.workingStatus` already maps jj's stale-working-copy error onto it — so the detection
half may largely exist; the gap is noticing it for a workroom the user is NOT looking at, and offering
the repair. The repair is itself a write, so it belongs on `VCSWriting`.

**Depends on:** pull-with-rebase (shipped).

**Priority:** P3 (jj projects only; wrong-workroom errors are rare but very confusing).

### "New workroom from branch…" (macapp) — the successor to branch switching

**What:** Pick a local or remote branch and create a workroom for it, from the VCS toolbar's branch
segment or the ⌘O picker.

**Why:** Branch *switching* was deliberately cut from the VCS toolbar. A workroom's identity IS its
branch — `internal/vcs/git.go` creates it with `git worktree add -b`, and there is no `branch` field
anywhere in `internal/config` — so switching a workroom's branch makes its directory name permanently
wrong, with nothing to reconcile the two. The jj equivalent is worse: `jj new <bookmark>` on the
bookmark the toolbar already displays was reproduced **removing a file from the working copy** and
leaving the workroom's commit as a nameless dangling head, with no visible change in the UI.

But the underlying need — "I want to work on that other branch" — is real, and creating a workroom is
the answer the product model actually supports. The toolbar's branch segment currently routes to ⌘O,
which only lists workrooms that already exist.

**Pros:** gives the cut affordance a correct home; makes an existing remote branch a first-class
starting point instead of requiring a manual create-then-checkout.

**Cons:** needs a branch list (the toolbar deliberately stopped enumerating refs when the picker was
cut), and a naming policy for the new workroom.

**Context / how to start:** `Views/OpenWorkroomDialog.swift` is the searchable, project-grouped picker
to clone; the Go CLI's `create` already accepts a branch. `CLIVCSWriter.gitRemoteRefsArgs` shows how to
enumerate remote refs cheaply, and its doc explains why the symref row must be dropped.

**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).

**Priority:** P3 (a real gap, but ⌘O plus a terminal covers it today).

## P3 — VCS engine, diffs, and status

+**Pros:** removes the last window where `.locked` is an *expected* outcome rather than an anomaly, so
+the UI's Retry affordance becomes a genuine edge case.
+**Cons:** serialising reads could measurably slow the status sweep, which fans out per workroom by
+design. This wants measurement first — it may be that read/write contention is rare enough in practice
+that the cost isn't worth it.
+**Context / how to start:** `WorkroomStatusResolver.resolveGit` (the ungated read) vs `resolveJJ` (the
+gated one); `CLIVCSWriter.gated` for how the writes do it. Note the gate is key-based and
+backend-agnostic, so if this lands, renaming `JJSnapshotGate` → `RepoWriteGate` (3 call sites + its
+test suite) stops being speculative churn and starts being accurate.
+**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).
+**Priority:** P3 (a real but narrow race; needs measurement before it's worth the sweep's latency).
+### jj sibling-workspace staleness after a rebase (macapp) — VCS-toolbar eng-review follow-up
+**What:** Detect and surface when a jj operation in one workroom leaves a *sibling* workspace stale.
+**Why:** All workrooms of a jj project share one repo and op-store. `jj rebase -b @` — what
+pull-with-rebase runs — rewrites commits, and any other workspace whose `@` descends from a rewritten
+commit is marked stale and needs `jj workspace update-stale` before its next command. Today that
+surfaces as an unexplained error in a **different** workroom from the one the user acted in, which is
+the worst attribution problem available: nothing on screen connects cause to effect.
+**Pros:** turns a mystery error into an explained one, and the repair is a single command Workroom
+could offer as a button.
+**Cons:** needs a cheap way to detect staleness across workspaces without reading each one (a per-op
+check would multiply the cost of every pull).
+**Context / how to start:** `VCSStatusFailure.staleWorkingCopy` already exists in the taxonomy, and
+`RustJJProvider.workingStatus` already maps jj's stale-working-copy error onto it — so the detection
+half may largely exist; the gap is noticing it for a workroom the user is NOT looking at, and offering
+the repair. The repair is itself a write, so it belongs on `VCSWriting`.
+**Depends on:** pull-with-rebase (shipped).
+**Priority:** P3 (jj projects only; wrong-workroom errors are rare but very confusing).
+### "New workroom from branch…" (macapp) — the successor to branch switching
+**What:** Pick a local or remote branch and create a workroom for it, from the VCS toolbar's branch
+segment or the ⌘O picker.
+**Why:** Branch *switching* was deliberately cut from the VCS toolbar. A workroom's identity IS its
+branch — `internal/vcs/git.go` creates it with `git worktree add -b`, and there is no `branch` field
+anywhere in `internal/config` — so switching a workroom's branch makes its directory name permanently
+wrong, with nothing to reconcile the two. The jj equivalent is worse: `jj new <bookmark>` on the
+bookmark the toolbar already displays was reproduced **removing a file from the working copy** and
+leaving the workroom's commit as a nameless dangling head, with no visible change in the UI.
+But the underlying need — "I want to work on that other branch" — is real, and creating a workroom is
+the answer the product model actually supports. The toolbar's branch segment currently routes to ⌘O,
+which only lists workrooms that already exist.
+**Pros:** gives the cut affordance a correct home; makes an existing remote branch a first-class
+starting point instead of requiring a manual create-then-checkout.
+**Cons:** needs a branch list (the toolbar deliberately stopped enumerating refs when the picker was
+cut), and a naming policy for the new workroom.
+**Context / how to start:** `Views/OpenWorkroomDialog.swift` is the searchable, project-grouped picker
+to clone; the Go CLI's `create` already accepts a branch. `CLIVCSWriter.gitRemoteRefsArgs` shows how to
+enumerate remote refs cheaply, and its doc explains why the symref row must be dropped.
+**Depends on:** the VCS toolbar (shipped).
+**Priority:** P3 (a real gap, but ⌘O plus a terminal covers it today).

4	/// UI-testing fixture seam (issue #3 UI tests). When the app is launched with
5	/// `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1`, `AppStore` loads this deterministic set of fake projects and
6	/// workrooms instead of reading the developer's real `~/.config/workroom`. The XCUITests
7	/// (`WorkroomAppUITests`) pass that flag so they're hermetic — they never touch real projects,
8	/// never depend on what happens to be configured on the machine, and run the same everywhere.
9	///
10	/// The fixture targets point at freshly-created temp directories so their terminals still spawn a
11	/// real login shell (libghostty needs a valid working directory) — the surface mounts and appears
12	/// in the accessibility tree exactly as it would for a real workroom, which is what the split-pane
13	/// tests assert on. The app remains a normal app: a regular user never passes the flag, so this
14	/// code is inert in production.
15	enum UITestFixture {
16	  /// The launch-argument / `UserDefaults` key the tests set (highest-priority argument domain).
17	  static let defaultsKey = "WorkroomUITestFixture"
18	
19	  /// **DEBUG-only, by construction.** Every fixture flag below reads through `flag`/`number`/`text`,
20	  /// and outside a Debug build they return the inert default without touching `UserDefaults` at all.
21	  ///
22	  /// The flags are read from `UserDefaults.standard`, which is the app's *persisted* domain and not
23	  /// just the launch-argument domain the tests use. So without this gate a single
24	  /// `defaults write <bundle id> WorkroomUITestFixture -bool YES` latched a shipping build into
25	  /// fixture mode permanently: fake projects instead of the user's real `~/.config/workroom`,
26	  /// `applyFixtureDefaults` overwriting their inspector and diff-mode preferences on every launch,
27	  /// and `.terminateNow` on quit skipping the graceful run-command teardown — with no in-app way
28	  /// back out. Several flags (`agentStub`, `forceWhatsNew`, `updateAvailableVersion`) are read
29	  /// WITHOUT consulting `isActive`, so gating `isActive` alone would not have been enough; the gate
30	  /// belongs on the reads.
31	  ///
32	  /// Nothing in the test suite loses anything: both `WorkroomAppTests` and `WorkroomAppUITests` build
33	  /// against the Debug configuration (`project.yml`), which is the only one that defines `DEBUG`.
34	  private static var enabled: Bool {
35	    #if DEBUG
36	      return true
37	    #else
38	      return false
39	    #endif
40	  }
41	
42	  /// A fixture-namespaced boolean. `bool(forKey:)` rather than `Defaults` on purpose — it coerces the
43	  /// STRING an argument-domain value arrives as (`-WorkroomUITestFixture 1` stores `"1"`), which a
44	  /// typed `Defaults` read would reject. See `applyFixtureDefaults` for the trap that implies.
45	  private static func flag(_ key: String) -> Bool {
46	    enabled && UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: key)
47	  }
48	
49	  private static func number(_ key: String) -> Int {
50	    enabled ? UserDefaults.standard.integer(forKey: key) : 0
51	  }
52	
53	  private static func text(_ key: String) -> String? {
54	    enabled ? UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: key) : nil
55	  }

content.text:
All twelve steps done. **1580 tests pass, 0 failures**; build, format and lint clean. Nothing committed — the change is staged in your working tree for review.

## What shipped

5 new source files, 8 modified, 9 new test files. 14 untracked files, ~1075 lines changed in the tracked ones.

| Layer | File |
|---|---|
| Engine | `VCSWriting.swift` — protocol, `VCS.writer(for:)`, `CLIVCSWriter` |
| | `VCSToolVersions.swift` — git ≥ 2.41 required, jj ≥ 0.43 optional |
| | `VCSSyncPresentation.swift` — the 13-state mapper |
| Model | `RemoteStateModel.swift` |
| View | `VCSToolbar.swift` |

## Bugs found and fixed that the plan had wrong

1. **`%(push:track)` is empty for every workroom.** Under git's default `push.default=simple`, a branch with no upstream — which is what `git worktree add -b` creates — yields nothing. The count would have been blank on any machine not set to `current`, and mine is. Replaced with `rev-list --left-right --count`; the integration suite asserts identical counts under all five `push.default` values.

2. **`FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree.** Fetching at the project root never writes the workroom's copy, so "last fetched" would have read *never* forever. Now resolves the common git dir.

3. **A jj fetch that brings nothing records no operation at all.** The op-log scan alone means "last fetch that *changed* something" — clicking Fetch with nothing new would leave a stale timestamp. Added a `vcs.lastFetch` stamp; the backend still wins when newer, so terminal-side fetches stay visible.

4. **`layoutPriority` inverted the toolbar's sizing** — only caught by running it. `feature/login` rendered as `fe…gin` in a 410pt inspector.

5. **`perform` required a remote for every action**, including abort — which would have left a wedged rebase unrecoverable from the UI.

6. **`awaitCurrentLoad` awaited in the wrong order**, and **`--allow-new` doesn't exist on jj 0.43** (a silently-failing fixture push).

## Two things I want to flag

**The UI tests are written and compile, but I could not run them.** XCUITest fails with *"Timed out while enabling automation mode"* — the recorded automation wedge, triggered by my repeated app launches during the visual check. It needs a login-session reset, which I wasn't going to do to your machine. So the 14 UI tests in `VCSToolbarUITests` are **unverified**. Everything else is: 1580 unit tests, plus 16 integration tests against real git and jj repos over `file://` remotes.

**I wrote two bad tests and caught them.** A BatchMode assertion that would flake on any machine exporting `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, and — worse — a "no VCS calls" guard that built a counter, never wired it to anything, and asserted zero. That one could never fail. Both replaced with assertions that can.

Also worth knowing: `@CommandsBuilder` caps at 10 children and the app was already at 10, so the Source Control menu needed a `Group` wrapper. And I extracted `isAppShortcut` into a pure classifier so the shortcut reservations finally have tests — that list has shipped broken twice.

10	/// sidebar, issue #118.)

18	  /// `--autostash` will stash and reapply. Shares this view's confirmation mechanism with the PR one.

26	    // size-weights persist as full `InspectorSectionKind.allCases`-ordered vectors on the store; we
27	    // slice out — and write back — the entries for the sub-sections actually shown, by `storeIndex`.
28	    let subs = store.activeInspectorSection.subSections

31	      // Changes section. Only for the Changes activity section: branch/remote state is what that section
32	      // is about, and showing it over the Files tree would jump the layout on every activity-bar click.
33	      if store.activeInspectorSection == .changes {
34	        VCSToolbar(
35	          onNeedsConfirmation: { action, sid in
36	            pendingVCSConfirm = PendingVCSAction(action: action, sid: sid)
37	          }, model: store.remoteState)

40	    }

42	      pendingVCSConfirm.map { "\($0.action.label) with uncommitted changes?" } ?? "",

content.text:
Everything green.

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Unit | **1580 passed, 0 failed**, 1 skipped |
| UI | **14 passed, 0 failed** |
| Integration (in unit gate) | 16 against real git + jj over `file://` |
| Build / format / lint | clean |

The automation subsystem had recovered on its own, so the retry worked. Three failures were real, and one of them was serious.

**The bug the UI tests caught — this would have shipped.** `VCSToolbar` observed `AppStore`, but `RemoteStateModel` is its own `ObservableObject` and nothing forwards its `objectWillChange`. So the toolbar rendered the first state and then never repainted: clicking Push set `inFlight`, ran the push, recorded the failure — and the UI showed **none of it**. It would have looked like a dead button.

`HistoryPanel` and `FilesPanel` take their model as an explicit `@ObservedObject` for precisely this reason; I'd read those files and still missed it. No unit test could have found it — it only exists in the wiring between a live view and a live model.

**A second real bug:** the persisted `vcs.lastFetch` stamp leaked across launches, so an earlier test's fetch overrode a seeded `.never` and "Never fetched" read as "just now". Fixed by resetting it in `applyFixtureDefaults`, alongside the inspector-layout pin that exists for the same class of reason.

**Two were my test's fault:** the fixture's 0.6s action delay was shorter than XCUITest's ~1s predicate polling, so the in-flight window fell between samples (raised to 2.5s, with the reasoning written down); and I was clicking a wrapper element rather than the `Button` — SwiftUI publishes the identifier on several layers, and the wrapper reports both `exists` and `isHittable` while swallowing the click. Added a `button(_:id:)` helper that matches `app.buttons` specifically.

That last one is worth remembering: `isHittable` returning true is **not** evidence that a click will invoke the action.

Nothing is committed — the whole change is in your working tree.

## 1. The views that render the VCS sidebar / inspector "Changes" panel

Everything lives in `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/`.

| File:lines | What |
|---|---|
| `ChangesPanel.swift:11-262` | **`RightInspector`** — the whole inspector pane. Maps `ActivitySection.subSections` → headers/bodies and hands them to `InspectorSplitView`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:74-120` | `sectionHeader(for:)` — builds the **"Changes"** header (`title: "Changes"`, `shortcut: "⌥⌘C"`, refresh button), plus Files / Pull Request / History headers. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:123-137` | `sectionBody(for:)` — `ChangesPanel()`, `FilesPanel`, `PullRequestPanel`, `HistoryPanel`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:229-261` | `changesIndicator` / `changesIndicatorLabel` — the `+N`/`-M` + conflict/dot badge shown inline in the Changes header. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:578-785` | **`ChangesPanel`** — the Changes *body*: branch header → `Divider()` → changes list. `renderCap = 200`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:596-621` | `content(for sid:)` — empty/missing/loading/git-vs-jj dispatch. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:626-639` | `gitContent` — `VStack(spacing:10) { changesHeader; Divider(); fileList/clean/failure }.padding(12)`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:645-661` | `jjContent` — same shape, `identifier: "changes.workingCopy"`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:669-730` | **`changesHeader`** — the one shared branch/bookmark header (see §3). |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:756-768` | `fileList` — `VStack(spacing: 1)` of `ChangedFileRow`. |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:304-487` | **`ChangedFileRow`** — one changed-file row (letter, name, dimmed dir, hover toolbar). |
| `ChangesPanel.swift:796-804` | `inspectorMessage(_:)` — shared placeholder line, `.padding(12)`. |
| `InspectorColumn.swift:12-59` | Docked inspector column: `RightInspector()` in a `sidebarCard(topMargin: 0, leadingMargin: 2, vibrant: true)`, width 260–520, drag handle on leading edge. |
| `RootView.swift:148-173` | Composition: `HStack { SidebarColumn / detail / if showInspector { InspectorColumn() } / ActivityBar() }`. |
| `EdgeRevealSidebar.swift:287-291` | Note: the right-edge *reveal* was dropped — only the left sidebar has one now. |

## 2. Sidebar composition — sections, headers, History, pane-header helpers

**Section model** (`Core/`):
- `ActivitySection.swift:15-56` — the activity-bar rail is now only `.changes` + `.files`. `subSections` (line 42-47): `.changes → [.changes, .history, .pullRequest]`, `.files → [.files]`.
- `ActivitySection.swift:58-64` — `InspectorSectionKind.storeIndex` (changes=0, files=1, pullRequest=2, **history=3**, appended last so indices stayed stable).
- `InspectorPanePolicy.swift:7-14` — `InspectorSectionKind` enum. `:47` `headerHeight = 34`, `:52` `expandedMinHeight = 120`, `:81` `allocate`, `:128` `reallocateOnToggle`.
- `ActivityBarReducer.swift:14-38` — icon-click vs shortcut vs toggle semantics.

**Split container / pane host** (`Views/InspectorSplitView.swift`):
- `:40-114` `InspectorPaneViewController` — sticky `NSHostingController` header (fixed `headerHeight`) + body in either scroll mode or **fill** mode.
- `:135-139` `ThemedSplitView` — divider forced to `tokens.nsFg.withAlphaComponent(0.12)`.
- `:141+` `InspectorSplitContainerController` — `NSSplitViewDelegate`, weights round-trip to the store.
- **`:466-539` `SectionHeader<Accessory>`** — the pane-header helper:
  ```swift
  .accessibilityIdentifier("inspector.header.\(title)")
  .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
  .background(ThemeService.shared.tokens.surface)
  .overlay(alignment: .trailing) { accessory().padding(.trailing, 12) }
  ```
  `headerLabel` (`:521-538`): `HStack(spacing: 7) { chevron(11pt semibold, rotate 0→90°, width 12); Text(title).font(.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)); indicator; Spacer }` with `.padding(.horizontal, 12).padding(.vertical, 8)`. `collapsed: nil` ⇒ solo pane, no chevron.

**History moved into the Changes stack** (commit `0fc3b97a`):
- `HistoryPanel.swift:8-146` — body; hosted in **fill mode** (`ChangesPanel.swift:32` `fills: subs.map { $0 == .history }`) so it owns its `ScrollView` (`:78-128`).
- `AppStore.swift:303-317` `historySectionCollapsed` (persists + eager focus), `:322-324` `historySectionShown`, `:337-340` `focusHistoryIfShown()`.
- `DefaultsKeys.swift:149-150` key renamed to `"inspector.layout.v2"`; `:199-205` `InspectorPaneState { collapsed: [Bool], weights: [Double] }` (4-vectors).
- `WorkroomApp.swift:815-870` — View-menu toggles ⌥⌘C / ⌥⌘Y / ⌥⌘P now expand/collapse sections rather than switch panes.

**Store state**: `AppStore.swift:291-345` (`changesSectionCollapsed`, `filesSectionCollapsed`, `prSectionCollapsed`, `historySectionCollapsed`, `inspectorSizeWeights`), `:351-364` `activeInspectorSection`, `:780-781` `inspectorTargetID` / `inspectorTarget`.

## 3. Where the branch / bookmark name is displayed

**The "ONE layout for both git/jj" header** — `ChangesPanel.swift:663-730`:

```swift
// ChangesPanel.swift:680-696
let extraRefs = (meta?.refs ?? []).filter { $0 != name }
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
  HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 6) {
    Text(name).font(.caption)
      .lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.middle)
      .padding(.horizontal, 5).padding(.vertical, 1)
      .background(.quaternary, in: Capsule())
      .help(ancestorBookmark ? "First ancestor bookmark in history" : "Bookmark / branch")
```
Then (jj only) change-id `.purple` / commit-id `.blue` in `.system(.callout, design: .monospaced)` (`:697-705`), extra ref capsules at `.caption` (`:709-715`), and the description line at `.callout` / `"(no description set)"` `.footnote .tertiary` (`:719-726`).

Resolution — `ChangesPanel.swift:735-741`:
```swift
private func branchLabel(sid: SidebarID, status: WorkroomStatus) -> String {
  if let branch = status.branchForCI, !branch.isEmpty { return branch }
  if case .root(let p) = sid { return RootPresentation.make(store.rootRefs[p] ?? .unresolved).label }
  return "detached"
}
```
Call site + jj ancestor-bookmark discrimination: `ChangesPanel.swift:609-619`.

**Other branch-name surfaces (same capsule/label vocabulary):**
- `TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104` — `branchSegment`, `Label` + `arrow.triangle.branch`, `.truncationMode(.middle)`, help `"Current branch / bookmark"`; resolved by `AppStore.swift:1235-1255` `branchLabel(for:)`.
- `ProjectSidebar.swift:285-344` — project root row: `RootPresentation.make(store.rootRefs[...])`, `.font(.callout)`, `.truncationMode(.tail)`, plus an `arrow.up` "ahead" marker (`:302-306`).
- `Core/Models.swift:127-165` — `RootPresentation.Style { label, tooltip, accessibility, ahead, dim }`.
- `HistoryPanel.swift:222-230` — per-commit ref capsules (`.caption2`, `.quaternary` Capsule).
- `ChangesetDetailView.swift:142-150` — same ref capsules in the changeset detail header.

## 4. Existing toolbar-like rows / strips you could reuse for a 3-segment toolbar

**Grouped segmented switches (closest existing precedent — track + raised thumb):**
- `TerminalTabStrip.swift:725-767` **`DiffModeSwitch`** (internal, already shared by two callers):
  ```swift
  HStack(spacing: 0) { segment(...); segment(...) }
    .padding(1.5)
    .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(theme.tokens.surface))
  // segment: 9.5pt glyph, .padding(.horizontal, 6).padding(.vertical, 3),
  //          RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5).fill(active ? theme.tokens.bg : .clear)
  //          + .help / .accessibilityLabel / .accessibilityIdentifier / .isSelected trait
  ```
- `TerminalTabStrip.swift:769-815` **`MarkdownModeSwitch`** — a literal copy of the above for a different 2-way choice. Adding a third segment is a `segment(...)` call; there is no 3-segment control in the app yet, and these two are the pattern to generalize.

**Divided segments / hairline group separators:**
- `TitlebarBars.swift:75-84` **`TitlebarDivider`** — `Rectangle().fill(tokens.border).frame(width: 1, height: 14).padding(.horizontal, 4)`. Used in `LeadingTitlebarBar` (`:111`), `TrailingTitlebarBar` (`:157`), and `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` (`WorkroomSplitView.swift:400, 403`) with the "only when there's something on both sides" rule.
- `TerminalStatusBar.swift:37-59` — a spaced-segment strip (`HStack(spacing: 12)`, `.font(.caption)`, `.frame(height: 24)`, `.background(tokens.bg)`, `.overlay(alignment: .top) { tokens.border.frame(height: 1) }`).
- `WorkroomTabBar.swift:227-251` `showsLeadingSeparator(at:groupOf:)` — the "drop the hairline next to the selected/hovered chip and at group boundaries" logic.

**Chip brackets (rounded outline around a contiguous run):**
- `WorkroomTabBar.swift:253-308` `splitWell(groupOf:)` + `splitRunRects` — `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 7).strokeBorder(tokens.border, lineWidth: 1)` in a `ZStack(alignment: .leading)` with per-run `offset(x:)`; a11y id `workroom.tab.splitBracket.N`.
- `TerminalTabStrip.swift:329-355` `splitWell(_:)` / `splitRunRect` — the single-run twin.
- `TabReorderMath.swift:135-160` `TabStripSplitRun.rect(widths:memberIndices:spacing:)` — the unit-tested geometry both use.

**Hover wells:**
- `ToolbarIconButtonStyle.swift:10-62` — the canonical well: `wellSize = 22`, `horizontalPadding = 3`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6, style: .continuous).fill(tokens.hover)`, opacity animated only on the fill (`.easeOut(0.12)`), press dim 0.6 / disabled 0.4. Apply once to a whole `HStack` via `.buttonStyle(...)`.
- `ChangesPanel.swift:530-551` **`inspectorHeaderButtonChrome(hovering:destructive:)`** — the inspector-specific well: fixed 22×22 fill inside a fixed 28×26 target, `cornerRadius: 5`, `tokens.hover`; used by `InspectorHeaderButton` (`:506-528`) and `InspectorMenuButtonStyle` (`:557-572`). **This is the one to reuse for anything sitting in a section header.**
- `TabToolbarButton.swift:8-43` — icon-only action with its own well (`.padding(4)`, radius 5, `tokens.hover`) + `.contentShape(Rectangle())`.
- `TerminalTabStrip.swift:246-267` `addTerminalButton` (same 4pt/radius-5 well), `:701-723` `TabCloseButton` (circular well).
- `ActivityBar.swift:63-125` `ActivityBarButton` — active = `accentSoft` fill + 2pt accent capsule strip; hover = `tokens.hover`, `cornerRadius: 6`.
- `RowHighlight.swift:8-22` — shared selected/hover row fill (`tokens.surface` / `tokens.hover`, radius 6).
- `TargetDetailToolbar.swift:9-38` `PaneToolbarIcon` — `glyph = 13`, `appIcon = 18`, `disclosure = 8` with headroom notes; `:63` shows the `HStack(spacing: -8)` trick for snugging two wells.
- `WorkroomSplitView.swift:341-440` `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` — a full 3-group toolbar row today (`RunControls | TitlebarDivider | OpenInControl | TitlebarDivider | ✕`), `.frame(height: 28)`, one `.buttonStyle(ToolbarIconButtonStyle())` + one `.font(.system(size: PaneToolbarIcon.glyph))` for the whole group.

## 5. Styling conventions & design system

**Design-system files:**
- `Core/ThemeTokens.swift` — the token snapshot (the design system). `Core/ThemeService.swift:31-76` — `ThemeService.shared`, `private(set) var tokens: ThemeTokens`, `generation`; `:129` posts `.themeDidChange` (`:238`). `Core/Theme.swift` — `ThemePreference`, `ThemeFamily`, `ThemePreview`.
- Access: SwiftUI reads `ThemeService.shared.tokens` via `private let theme = ThemeService.shared` (the pervasive idiom, e.g. `ChangesPanel.swift:580`); AppKit reads the singleton and refreshes on `.themeDidChange` (e.g. `ActivityBar.swift:16-18, 47`).

**Colour tokens** (`ThemeTokens.swift:16-92`, derived in `init` at `:95-193`) — everything is theme-derived, no hard-coded hex:

| Token | Derivation | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `bg` / `fg` | theme bg/fg | base |
| `panel` | bg blended 5.5% toward fg | title bar, tab bar, activity bar |
| `fgMuted` / `fgDim` | fg @ 0.65 / 0.40 | secondary / tertiary text |
| `surface` | fg @ 0.08 | section header background, segmented-switch track, selected row |
| `border` | fg @ 0.12 | hairlines, dividers, chip brackets, split dividers |
| `hover` | fg @ 0.06 | hover wells |
| `tabActive` | fg @ 0.16 | selected tab fill |

private func branchLabel(sid: SidebarID, status: WorkroomStatus) -> String {

- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104` `branchSegment` — `Label` + `arrow.triangle.branch` SF Symbol, `.truncationMode(.middle)`, `.help("Current branch / bookmark")`; resolved via `AppStore.swift:1235-1255` `branchLabel(for:)`.
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/ProjectSidebar.swift:285-344` project root row uses `RootPresentation.make(store.rootRefs[...])` plus an `arrow.up` "ahead" marker at `:302-306`. `Core/Models.swift:127-165` `RootPresentation.Style { label, tooltip, accessibility, ahead, dim }`.

### Reusable chrome
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TitlebarBars.swift:75-84` `TitlebarDivider` — `Rectangle().fill(tokens.border).frame(width: 1, height: 14).padding(.horizontal, 4)`; used in `LeadingTitlebarBar` (`:111`), `TrailingTitlebarBar` (`:157`), `WorkroomSplitView.swift:400,403` — with the rule "only when there's something on both sides".
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/WorkroomSplitView.swift:341-440` `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` — an EXISTING 3-group toolbar row (`RunControls | TitlebarDivider | OpenInControl | TitlebarDivider | ✕`), `.frame(height: 28)`, one `.buttonStyle(ToolbarIconButtonStyle())` + one `.font(.system(size: PaneToolbarIcon.glyph))` for the whole group. **This is the closest structural precedent.**
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/ChangesPanel.swift:506-528` `InspectorHeaderButton` + `:530-551` `inspectorHeaderButtonChrome(hovering:destructive:)` — the inspector-specific hover well (22×22 fill inside a 28×26 target, `cornerRadius: 5`, `tokens.hover`); `:557-572` `InspectorMenuButtonStyle`. **Use these for anything in inspector chrome.**
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/ToolbarIconButtonStyle.swift:10-62` — canonical well: `wellSize = 22`, `horizontalPadding = 3`, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6, style: .continuous).fill(tokens.hover)`, opacity-only `.easeOut(0.12)`, press dim 0.6 / disabled 0.4.
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:725-767` `DiffModeSwitch` and `:769-815` `MarkdownModeSwitch` — two near-identical 2-segment grouped switches (`HStack(spacing: 0)`, `.padding(1.5)`, track `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(tokens.surface)`, segment `.padding(.horizontal, 6).padding(.vertical, 3)` + `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5).fill(active ? tokens.bg : .clear)`, 9.5pt glyphs).
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/WorkroomTabBar.swift:253-308` `splitWell(groupOf:)` + `Core/TabReorderMath.swift:135-160` — chip-bracket geometry (`RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 7).strokeBorder(tokens.border, lineWidth: 1)`).
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TargetDetailToolbar.swift:9-38` `PaneToolbarIcon` — `glyph = 13`, `appIcon = 18`, `disclosure = 8`; `:63` shows `HStack(spacing: -8)` for snugging two wells.
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/RowHighlight.swift:8-22` shared selected/hover row fill; `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/SidebarCard.swift:17-56` `sidebarCard(...)`.

### Design tokens (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ThemeTokens.swift`, accessed via `ThemeService.shared.tokens`, idiom `private let theme = ThemeService.shared`)
`bg`/`fg`; `panel` (bg +5.5% fg — title bar, tab bar, activity bar); `fgMuted` (fg@0.65) / `fgDim` (fg@0.40); `surface` (fg@0.08 — section header background, segmented track, selected row); `border` (fg@0.12 — hairlines, dividers, brackets); `hover` (fg@0.06); `rowHover`/`rowSelection` (OPAQUE); `accent`/`accentSoft`/`accentForeground`; `warning`/`failure`/`conflict`; `diffAddFg`/`diffRemoveFg` (+`…Bg` @0.16). `ThemeService.shared.tokens`, `generation`, posts `.themeDidChange`.
Typography: section header title `.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)`; header icon glyphs `.system(size: 11)`; row filename `.callout`; metadata `.system(.caption, design: .monospaced)` + `.tertiary`; ref pills `.caption` / `.caption2`; counts `.caption.monospacedDigit()`.
Geometry: section body inset `.padding(12)`; body rhythm `VStack(spacing: 10)`; header inset `.padding(.horizontal, 12).padding(.vertical, 8)`; corner radii 5/6/7/10; bar heights — title bar 28, pane title bar 28, status bar 24, inspector section header 34 (`InspectorPanePolicy.headerHeight`); inspector column width 260–520.
Animations `.easeOut(0.12)` hover / `.easeInOut(0.12)` / `.easeInOut(0.2)` / `.easeInOut(0.22)`, all gated on `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)`.

### Non-negotiable conventions
Every control needs `.help(...)` + `.accessibilityLabel(...)` + a stable `.accessibilityIdentifier(...)`. Interactive glyphs need their own `.onHover` (so `.help`'s tracking area installs) AND `.contentShape(Rectangle())`. Active state must be signalled by position/brightness, not hue alone. Formatting: `.swift-format`, 2-space indent, 100 columns; run `make app-format` / `make app-lint`; `make app-generate` (xcodegen) after adding any new `.swift` file.

### Known traps (from hard-won project memory — respect these)
- A SwiftUI window-`toolbar` item's overflow `menuFormRepresentation` caused a 2s AppHang; the window toolbar is kept an EMPTY AppKit `NSToolbar`. So this new "toolbar" must be a plain SwiftUI view INSIDE the inspector, never a `.toolbar` modifier.
- `.textSelection(.enabled)` text swallows real mouseDown so SwiftUI taps don't fire (real-mouse-only bug; synthetic XCUITest clicks pass on buggy code).
- `.onHover` controls are NOT drivable from XCUITest; an accessibility id on an `NSViewRepresentable` wrapper is not queryable.
- `@Default` invalidates SwiftUI ASYNCHRONOUSLY — use `@State` for click-immediate UI.
- Pixel-perfect alignment is expected — fix by construction (uniform insets, centered icons), don't eyeball.
- Joel wants XCUITest coverage for new macapp UI, not just unit tests. See `macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/` — and note `make app-uitest` IGNORES `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so scoped runs need a direct `xcodebuild -only-testing:<Class>/<method>`. There's a `UITestFixture` seam (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/UITestFixture.swift`, `isActive`, `static let vcsProvider` at `:630`, `FixtureVCSProvider` at `:636`) — launch arg `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1`.

### Engine reality (a parallel agent is planning this half — assume the data will exist)
Today `VCSProviding` is read-only with NO branch listing, NO fetch/push/pull, NO ahead/behind counts, NO last-fetch time. Assume a new service will provide: a branch/bookmark list, current upstream, ahead/behind counts, a last-fetch `Date?`, and async fetch/push/pull actions with in-flight + error state. Design the UI against a clean injectable view-model/observable and SAY exactly what shape you need from it.

## What I need from you
1. Exact placement decision + how to implement it. Key question: `RightInspector` composes section headers/bodies into an `InspectorSplitView` (an AppKit `NSSplitView` host). Does the toolbar go above the whole split view inside `RightInspector`, or inside `InspectorColumn`? What happens with the `.files` activity section (should the toolbar show there too, or only for `.changes`)? Give a recommendation.
2. Full view decomposition: new file(s) under `macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/`, the segment sub-views, the divider approach, exact heights/insets/fonts/tokens so it matches the screenshot AND the app's existing look. Two-line segments in a ~30-40pt bar is tight — give real numbers.
3. The branch dropdown: `Menu` vs a custom popover. Consider that a repo can have hundreds of branches (filter field? grouping local vs remote? a "new branch" affordance?). Note the AppHang trap above and whether `Menu`'s lazy content is safe here. Recommend one.
4. The middle segment's state machine: enumerate every state (no remote / no upstream / never fetched / clean / ahead N / behind N / diverged / fetching / pushing / failed) and the exact title+subtitle+badge for each. Include the relative-time formatting approach and how it stays live ("9 minutes ago" must tick).
5. Store/state wiring: where the observable lives (`AppStore`? a new `@Observable`?), how it keys off the inspector target (`AppStore.inspectorTargetID`/`inspectorTarget`, `AppStore.swift:780-781`), and how it avoids doing work when the inspector is hidden (there's an existing precedent: `focusHistoryIfShown()` gated on `inspectorIsVisible && historySectionShown`).
6. Interaction/feedback: hover wells, disabled states, spinner during fetch/push, error presentation (inline? tooltip? the existing `inspectorMessage(_:)` at `ChangesPanel.swift:796-804`?), and whether push/pull needs a confirmation.
7. Layout robustness: the inspector is 260–520pt wide. How do three segments with two-line text degrade at 260pt? Give the truncation/priority rules.
8. Keyboard shortcuts + menu items — should Fetch/Push/Pull get View/VCS menu entries? Note the project memory: every new shortcut MUST also be added to `GhosttySurfaceView.isAppShortcut` or a focused TUI swallows it.
9. Test plan: unit tests (pure state-machine mapping — the app has precedent for pure mapping types like `Core/ChangeBadge.swift` being unit-tested) plus XCUITest coverage, with the fixture seam.
10. Sequencing: phase 1 = minimum shippable, later phases.

Be concrete and opinionated. Give real numbers, not "appropriate spacing".

# VCS Toolbar — UI Implementation Plan

## 1. Placement: above the split view, inside `RightInspector`

**Recommendation: put it in `RightInspector`, wrapping `InspectorSplitView` in a `VStack`.** Not `InspectorColumn`, not a section header, never a `.toolbar` modifier.

`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/ChangesPanel.swift:18-59` — `RightInspector.body` currently returns `InspectorSplitView(...)` directly. Change to:

```swift
var body: some View {
  let subs = store.activeInspectorSection.subSections
  VStack(spacing: 0) {
    VCSToolbar()                       // 36pt, fixed
    InspectorSplitView(headers: …)     // unchanged, verbatim
      .frame(minWidth: 260, maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)
  }
  .confirmationDialog(…)               // unchanged
}
```

Why here, with the receipts:

- **Zero AppKit changes.** `InspectorSplitView.sizeThatFits` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:432-437`) returns the proposal, so the `VStack` simply offers it 36pt less height. `InspectorPanePolicy.allocate` reads `splitView.bounds.height` live at `viewDidLayout` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:289-294`), so pane distribution, drag, weights persistence and `reallocateOnToggle` all keep working untouched. The only behavioural consequence: `expandedMinHeight` (120) × 3 + dividers ≈ 362pt is reached 36pt sooner in a short window, at which point the breakable `.defaultHigh` floor compresses panes and each pane's own `NSScrollView` scrolls — already the designed behaviour.
- **Not a section header.** `SectionHeader` is hosted by `InspectorPaneViewController.headerHost` at a hard `heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: InspectorPanePolicy.headerHeight)` = 34 (`InspectorSplitView.swift:95`). A toolbar there would collapse with the pane, would be pinned to 34pt, and would live behind an `NSHostingController` boundary that doesn't inherit `@EnvironmentObject` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:380-383`). And the user asked for it *above* the Changes header, which a header can't be.
- **Not `InspectorColumn`.** `InspectorColumn.swift:12-58` owns only docked chrome: width clamp 260–520, `sidebarCard(topMargin: 0, leadingMargin: 2, vibrant: true)`, and the `InspectorResizeHandle` overlay. Keeping the toolbar in `RightInspector` means it is inspector *content* with one owner, so a future second host of `RightInspector()` (today there is exactly one — verified) gets it free.
- **Plain SwiftUI tree.** `RightInspector` inherits `@EnvironmentObject var store` normally (no `AnyView` + `.environmentObject` injection needed — that ceremony at `ChangesPanel.swift:74-137` exists *only* because of the hosting boundary), `.onHover` fires (`ActivityBar` proves hover works inside the detail-only `NavigationSplitView`, `ActivityBar.swift:10-12`), and `.popover` anchors reliably without hand-hosting an `NSPopover`.
- **Never `.toolbar`.** The AppHang trap: the window toolbar is deliberately an empty AppKit `NSToolbar`. This is a plain SwiftUI view inside content, exactly like `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` (`WorkroomSplitView.swift:341-440`), which is the closest structural precedent.

**`.files` section: render the toolbar unconditionally.** It is repo-level state, not Changes-section state; hiding it on the Files pane would jump the layout 36pt on every activity-bar click and make the branch name vanish while browsing that same repo's tree. If Joel disagrees the gate is one line in `RightInspector.body`: `if store.activeInspectorSection == .changes { VCSToolbar() }`.

**Two easily-missed requirements:**
- The toolbar reads `ThemeService.shared.tokens` for its hairlines, which SwiftUI does not observe. It needs the `themeTick` pattern verbatim from `ActivityBar.swift:18` + `:47`: `@State private var themeTick = 0` and `.onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: .themeDidChange)) { _ in themeTick += 1 }`. Without it a theme switch leaves the dividers stale.
- **Background: clear (inherit the card), plus one 1pt `tokens.border` bottom hairline.** The Changes header below already fills `tokens.surface` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:512`); a second `surface` band directly above it merges into one 70pt grey block. A clear toolbar over the card's vibrant fill, separated by the same hairline device `RightInspector.sectionRule` uses (`ChangesPanel.swift:217-219`), reproduces the screenshot's relationship (toolbar = chrome, "Changes" = filled subheader) and sidesteps the card's 10pt corner clip having anything to clip. If it needs more weight, the only correct alternative is `tokens.panel` — the token that already means chrome (title bar, tab bar, activity bar) — accepting loss of vibrancy in that strip.

---

## 2. View decomposition, with real numbers

**One new file: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/VCSToolbar.swift`.**

```
enum VCSToolbarMetrics            // every number in one place
struct VCSToolbar: View           // the 36pt HStack + themeTick + .task activation
private struct VCSToolbarDivider  // full-bleed 1pt hairline
private struct VCSBranchSegment
private struct VCSSyncSegment
private struct VCSFetchSegment
private struct VCSCountPill
extension View { func vcsToolbarSegment(hovering:) -> some View }
```

### Metrics (`VCSToolbarMetrics`)

| constant | value | why this number |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | **36** | 11pt title (13pt line) + 1pt spacing + 10pt caption (12pt line) = 26, + 5pt top/bottom = 36. Two lines do not fit 34 without crowding, and 36 reads as a distinct band above the 34pt section headers. |
| `vPadding` | **5** | closes the 26 → 36 gap. |
| `outerInset` | **12** | matches `SectionHeader`'s `.padding(.horizontal, 12)` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:534`). |
| `innerInset` | **8** | inner sides of segments; tighter than 12 so the middle segment isn't starved. |
| `glyphSlot` | **12** | matches `SectionHeader`'s chevron `.frame(width: 12)` (`:528`). |
| `glyphSpacing` | **7** | matches `SectionHeader`'s `HStack(spacing: 7)` (`:522`). |
| `glyph` | **12** | between the inspector's 11 (`InspectorHeaderButton`) and the pane bar's 13 (`PaneToolbarIcon.glyph`) — needs to hold against a bold 11pt title without becoming a pane-bar icon. |
| `titleFont` | `.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)` | identical to the section header title, so toolbar and header read as one type system. |
| `captionFont` | `.system(size: 10)` | one step down; `fgDim`. |
| `soloFont` | `.system(size: 11)` + `fgMuted` | the single-line sync state (see §4) — a lone 10pt `fgDim` line in a 36pt bar reads as a rendering bug. |
| `fetchWidth` | **30** | 22pt well + 4pt each side, per `ToolbarIconButtonStyle.footprint` (22 + 3×2 = 28) rounded to a divider-bounded cell. |
| `branchMinWidth` / `branchMaxWidth` | **100 / 220** | see §7. |
| `syncMinWidth` | **126** | see §7. |
| `pillHPad` / `pillVPad` | **5 / 1** | verbatim from `PRNumberBadge` (`ChangesPanel.swift:293`) and the `changesHeader` ref pills (`:690`). |

**The alignment-by-construction win:** `outerInset 12` + `glyphSlot 12` + `glyphSpacing 7` puts the branch glyph's centre at x=18 and the branch name's left edge at x=31 — *exactly* where the Changes header's chevron centre and "Changes" title left edge land. Verify by construction, not by eye, as the project rule requires.

### `VCSToolbar` body

```swift
HStack(spacing: 0) {
  VCSBranchSegment(…)
    .frame(minWidth: M.branchMinWidth, maxWidth: M.branchMaxWidth)
    .layoutPriority(0)
  VCSToolbarDivider()
  VCSSyncSegment(…)
    .frame(minWidth: M.syncMinWidth, maxWidth: .infinity)
    .layoutPriority(1)
  VCSToolbarDivider()
  VCSFetchSegment(…)
    .frame(width: M.fetchWidth)
}
.frame(height: M.height)
.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
.overlay(alignment: .bottom) { theme.tokens.border.frame(height: 1) }
.disabled(model.activity != .idle)
.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
.accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar")
```

`.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` + a container id mirrors `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` (`WorkroomSplitView.swift:430-431`). The single `.disabled` on the HStack is the re-entrancy guard, mirroring `store.prActionInFlight` disabling the PR menu (`AppStore.swift:283`, `ChangesPanel.swift:210`).

### `VCSToolbarDivider`

```swift
Rectangle().fill(theme.tokens.border).frame(width: 1).frame(maxHeight: .infinity)
```

Deliberately **not** `TitlebarDivider` (`TitlebarBars.swift:75-84`), which is a 14pt-tall, `.padding(.horizontal, 4)` *inline group* rule. Full-bleed is what the screenshot shows and what makes the three cells read as segments. The project's "only render a divider when there's something on both sides" rule (`WorkroomSplitView.swift:398-400`) still holds — but all three segments always render (each has a placeholder state, see §4), so both dividers are unconditional. Document that.

### Shared hover/disable chrome

```swift
func vcsToolbarSegment(hovering: Bool) -> some View {
  self
    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
    .background(
      ThemeService.shared.tokens.hover
        .opacity(hovering ? 1 : 0)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeOut(duration: 0.12), value: hovering)
    )
    .contentShape(Rectangle())
}
```

One treatment for all three segments: **the whole divider-bounded cell lights up**, not a 22pt well. `InspectorHeaderButton`'s inset well (`ChangesPanel.swift:506-551`) is correct for a control *floating* in a header row; a 22pt well inside a 30×36 cell whose bounds are drawn by hairlines would read as a mistake. Animate opacity only, never the view tree — the issue-#78 reasoning at `ToolbarIconButtonStyle.swift:40-52` (an implicit tree animation interpolates the glyph's 1pt pixel re-round into a visible slide).

### `VCSBranchSegment`

```swift
Button { showPicker = true } label: {
  HStack(spacing: 7) {
    Image(systemName: "arrow.triangle.branch")
      .font(.system(size: 12)).foregroundStyle(theme.tokens.fgMuted)
      .frame(width: 12)
    ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) {
      VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 1) {          // wide: 2 lines
        Text("Current Branch").font(M.captionFont).foregroundStyle(theme.tokens.fgDim).lineLimit(1)
        Text(name).font(M.titleFont).lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.middle)
      }
      Text(name).font(M.titleFont).lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.middle)   // narrow: name only
    }
    Spacer(minLength: 4)
    Image(systemName: "chevron.down")
      .font(.system(size: PaneToolbarIcon.disclosure)).foregroundStyle(theme.tokens.fgDim)
  }
  .padding(.leading, M.outerInset).padding(.trailing, M.innerInset)
  .vcsToolbarSegment(hovering: hovering)
}
.buttonStyle(.plain)
.onHover { hovering = $0 }
.help(…) .accessibilityLabel(…) .accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar.branch")
.popover(isPresented: $showPicker, arrowEdge: .bottom) { BranchPickerPopover(…) }
```

- Icon `arrow.triangle.branch` — the same symbol `TerminalStatusBar.branchSegment` (`:93-104`) and `ActivitySection.changes.systemImage` already use for a branch.
- `.truncationMode(.middle)` on the name, for the reason already written down twice in this codebase: a long branch's distinguishing part is often its tail (`joel/history-refs-pill`), so tail-truncating hides what tells it apart (`ChangesPanel.swift:686-688`, `TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`).
- Disclosure glyph reuses `PaneToolbarIcon.disclosure` (8pt), which already means "there's a menu behind this button" (`TargetDetailToolbar.swift:33-37`).
- Caption in **title case + `fgDim`**, not the sidebar's uppercase-semibold convention (`OpenWorkroomDialog.swift:99-102`): uppercase tracking at 10pt beside a bold 11pt name reads as a section header, which this is not.

### `VCSSyncSegment`

Same shape, **inverted line order** — bold title on top, dim subtitle below — plus a trailing pill:

```swift
HStack(spacing: 7) {
  if let symbol = p.symbol { icon(symbol, tone: p.tone).frame(width: 12) }
  if let title = p.title {
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 1) {
      ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) { ForEach titleVariants → Text(…).font(M.titleFont) }
      ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) { Text(p.subtitle); Text(p.subtitleShort) }
        .font(M.captionFont).foregroundStyle(p.tone == .failure ? theme.tokens.failure : theme.tokens.fgDim)
    }
  } else {
    Text(p.subtitle).font(M.soloFont).foregroundStyle(theme.tokens.fgMuted)   // single-line, centred
  }
  Spacer(minLength: 4)
  if let b = p.badge { VCSCountPill(b) }
  if let b = p.secondaryBadge { VCSCountPill(b) }
}
.padding(.horizontal, M.innerInset)
```

**Call out explicitly in the doc comment that the inverted line order is intentional** (it's what the screenshot and the ask specify) and that its consequence is that the branch segment's bold line and the sync segment's bold line do **not** share a baseline: both blocks are exactly 26pt tall and both are centred, so a caption-first block puts its bold line in the lower half and a title-first block puts it in the upper half. The full-height divider between them is what makes that read as two groups rather than a misalignment. A reviewer will flag it; pre-empt them. (The alternative — matching orders — contradicts the explicit ask.)

`ViewThatFits` is new to this codebase (grep: no existing use; macOS 13+, target is 15.0). **The one trap:** every variant must report its true ideal width, so no variant may contain `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` — otherwise the first variant always "fits" and the ladder never fires. `.lineLimit(1)` + `.truncationMode` do *not* shrink a `Text`'s ideal width, so they're safe.

### `VCSCountPill`

```swift
HStack(spacing: 2) {
  Text("\(count)").font(.caption2).fontWeight(.semibold).monospacedDigit()
  Image(systemName: direction == .ahead ? "arrow.up" : "arrow.down")
    .font(.system(size: 7, weight: .semibold))
}
.foregroundStyle(theme.tokens.fgMuted)
.padding(.horizontal, 5).padding(.vertical, 1)
.background(Capsule().fill(theme.tokens.surface))
.fixedSize()
.accessibilityHidden(true)
```

Geometry and font copied verbatim from `PRNumberBadge` (`ChangesPanel.swift:290-295`) so the toolbar pill matches the ref pill sitting 40pt below it in the Changes header. Fill is `surface` for **both** directions, not hue-coded: the arrow glyph carries direction (position/shape, per the "never hue alone" rule) and the count is a quantity, not a severity. `.fixedSize()` because the pill is the highest-information 30pt in the bar and must never yield. `.accessibilityHidden(true)` + the count republished on the sync button's `.accessibilityValue` — the pattern `ActivityBarButton` uses for its dirty dot (`ActivityBar.swift:81-88`, `:111`), and the only shape a UI test can actually read out of a `.combine`d button.

### `VCSFetchSegment`

Icon-only, 30pt wide, full-height hover fill, `.contentShape(Rectangle())`, own `.onHover`.

**Glyph: `arrow.down.circle`, not `arrow.clockwise`.** The Changes section header's Refresh button is `InspectorHeaderButton(systemImage: "arrow.clockwise", …)` (`ChangesPanel.swift:82`) and sits ~40pt below and 10pt to the left. Two near-identical circular-arrow glyphs stacked vertically meaning different things (re-read local status vs. contact the remote) is a real confusion. `arrow.down.circle` also matches the ↓ direction language of the pills. `arrow.triangle.2.circlepath` is rejected for being too close to `arrow.clockwise`. Follow-up worth noting: once Fetch exists, the header Refresh button is semi-redundant and deserves its own audit.

In-flight: swap the glyph for `ProgressView().controlSize(.mini)` — `.mini` not `.small`, because `.small` is ~16pt and would exceed the 12pt slot; `TerminalStatusBar.swift:234` already uses `.mini` for exactly this reason.

**Do not add `.textSelection(.enabled)` to the branch name.** Tempting (copy the branch name), but selectable text swallows real mouseDown, so the segment would stop being clickable with a real mouse while synthetic XCUITest clicks kept passing. Offer `.contextMenu { Button("Copy Branch Name") … }` instead.

---

## 3. Branch dropdown: custom `.popover`, not `Menu`

**Recommendation: a `.popover` hosting a new `BranchPickerPopover`, 300 × 360.**

New file `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/BranchPickerPopover.swift`.

Why not `Menu`:
1. **A filter field is mandatory at hundreds of branches, and `Menu` cannot host a `TextField`** — its content is NSMenu-backed.
2. **Opening a `Menu` over ~800 `Button`s materializes ~800 NSMenuItems synchronously on the main thread.** That is the *shape* of the recorded 2s AppHang (a toolbar item's `menuFormRepresentation`); the specific API differs but the lesson — don't hand SwiftUI a big menu — generalizes. `Menu` content is lazily *built* but not lazily *realized*.
3. Local/Remote grouping, a ✓ on the current branch, per-branch ahead/behind hints and a "New branch…" affordance are all either impossible or ugly in a `Menu`.

`Menu` is *safe* in this app in general — `prActionsMenu` (`ChangesPanel.swift:174-213`) uses it with `.menuStyle(.button)` + `InspectorMenuButtonStyle` and works fine. It's the size and the text field that rule it out here.

  var subtitle: String
  var subtitleShort: String
