Full table (`title` = bold 11pt semibold; `subtitle` = dim 10pt; `—` in title ⇒ single-line mode, subtitle rendered at `soloFont`/`fgMuted` and vertically centred):

| # | condition | title | subtitle | badge | glyph | click | enabled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `!hasTarget` | — | "No workroom selected" | — | — | none | no |
| 2 | `!isRepo` / status failed | — | "No repository" | — | `exclamationmark.triangle` (warning) | none | no |
| 3 | `!hasRemote` | — | "No remote configured" | — | — | none | no |
| 4 | `upstream == nil` | "Publish branch" | "`<branch>` isn't on origin yet" | `N ↑` if `ahead>0` | `arrow.up.circle` | `.publish` (push `--set-upstream`) | yes |
| 5 | `lastFetch == nil`, `ahead==0`, `behind==0` | — | "Never fetched" | — | — | `.fetch` | yes |
| 6 | clean, fetched | — | "Last fetched \(rel)" | — | — | `.fetch` | yes |
| 7 | `ahead>0`, `behind==0` | **"Push origin"** | "Last fetched \(rel)" / "Never fetched" | `N ↑` | `arrow.up` | `.push` | yes |
| 8 | `behind>0`, `ahead==0` | `pullRebase ? "Pull origin with rebase" : "Pull origin"` | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` | `arrow.down` | `.pull` | yes |
| 9 | **diverged** `ahead>0 && behind>0` | `pullRebase ? "Pull origin with rebase" : "Pull origin"` | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` **then** `N ↑` | `arrow.up.arrow.down` | `.pull` | yes |
| 10 | `.fetching` | "Fetching…" | "from origin" | — | spinner | none | no |
| 11 | `.pushing` | "Pushing…" | "to origin" | keep `N ↑` | spinner | none | no |
| 12 | `.pulling` | "Pulling…" | "from origin" | keep `M ↓` | spinner | none | no |
| 13 | `failure != nil`, idle | previous action's title | error's first line, `tone: .failure` | keep counts | `exclamationmark.triangle.fill` | `.retry` (= `lastAction`) | yes |

Precedence: 13 > 10/11/12 > 1 > 2 > 3 > 4 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 5 > 6.

**Two opinionated calls:**
- **Diverged → Pull, not Push.** git refuses a non-fast-forward push, and GitHub Desktop makes Pull primary for the same reason. Badge shows both pills, ↓ first (the one the action addresses).
- **`upstream == nil` + `ahead > 0` → `.publish`, not `.push`.** This is the workroom case: workrooms are `git worktree add -b` branches with no upstream — the exact scenario `VCSModels.swift:20-25` documents as why `VCSPushState` is origin-scoped rather than `@{u}`-scoped. Getting this wrong makes every workroom read "Push origin" against an upstream that doesn't exist.

`titleVariants`, longest first, feeding the `ViewThatFits` ladder:
- state 8/9: `["Pull origin with rebase", "Pull with rebase", "Pull"]`
- state 7: `["Push origin", "Push"]`
- state 4: `["Publish branch", "Publish"]`

`subtitle` / `subtitleShort`: `"Last fetched 9 minutes ago"` / `"Fetched 9 min. ago"`.

### Relative time

```swift
private static let fullFormatter: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = { $0.unitsStyle = .full; … }()
private static let shortFormatter: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = { $0.unitsStyle = .abbreviated; … }()

static func fetchedAgo(_ date: Date, now: Date, short: Bool = false) -> String
```
Under 60s → `"just now"` (so it reads "Last fetched just now", never "in 0 seconds"). `static let` formatters because they're expensive to construct — `NotificationsList.swift:265-270` already does this. **Do not reuse `NotificationsList.timeAgo`**: it's `private`, `.abbreviated`, and reads `Date()` internally, so it's untestable. `now` is a parameter here precisely so the whole mapper is pure and testable at fixed instants.

### Keeping it live

**The ticker lives on the view model, not the view.** A `Timer.publish` created inside `body` is re-created on every parent render and re-subscribes; a stored property on a `View` struct has the same problem. So `VCSSyncModel` owns a `Timer` started by `startTicking()` / stopped by `stopTicking()`, bumping `@Published private(set) var now: Date`. The view passes `model.now` into the mapper.

- **Interval 30s, tolerance 5s.** Under 60s the copy says "just now" anyway, so 30s bounds the visible staleness of "9 minutes ago" to ±30s — invisible. `tolerance` lets the OS coalesce wakeups.
- Started from the toolbar's `.task`, stopped in `.onDisappear`. Because the toolbar only exists inside `InspectorColumn`, which `RootView.swift:162-165` constructs inside `if showInspector`, a hidden inspector means **no timer at all** — zero idle wakeups, for free. That's the same mechanism `AppStore.swift:334-336` documents for History.
- Invalidation is scoped to the 36pt strip: the `@Published now` is read only by `VCSSyncSegment`, so the tick never re-renders `InspectorSplitView`.

### What the model needs from the engine — state this to the parallel agent

```swift
struct VCSSyncState: Equatable, Sendable {
  var branch: String?      // current local branch / jj bookmark
  var upstream: String?    // e.g. "origin/main"; nil ⇒ no tracking branch
  var hasRemote: Bool
  var ahead: Int           // vs UPSTREAM, not origin-wide
  var behind: Int
  var lastFetch: Date?     // PROVIDER-owned, read from the repo
  var pullRebase: Bool
}

struct VCSBranch: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var name: String; var isCurrent: Bool; var isRemote: Bool
  var upstream: String?; var ahead: Int?; var behind: Int?; var tip: String?
  var id: String { (isRemote ? "r:" : "l:") + name }
}

protocol VCSSyncProviding: Sendable {
  func syncState(root: URL) async throws -> VCSSyncState
  func branches(root: URL) async throws -> [VCSBranch]        // called lazily, popover only
  func fetch(root: URL) async throws
  func push(root: URL, setUpstream: Bool) async throws
  func pull(root: URL, rebase: Bool) async throws
  func checkout(root: URL, branch: String) async throws
  func createBranch(root: URL, name: String, from: String?) async throws   // phase 4
}
```

Two things the engine must get right, both flagged because the existing code gets them differently on purpose:
1. **`lastFetch` is provider-owned, read from the repo** (git: `.git/FETCH_HEAD` mtime; jj: the op log), never "when the app last called fetch". A `git fetch` typed in the workroom's own terminal must move the number.
2. **`ahead`/`behind` are upstream-scoped (`@{u}`)**, which is deliberately *different* from `VCSPushState`'s origin-wide scope. `VCSModels.swift:19-31` explains why push state is origin-scoped ("workrooms are `git worktree add -b` branches with no upstream, so the badge would never appear where it matters most") — that choice is right for the history badge and wrong for this toolbar, where "no upstream" is a first-class state (#4, Publish). Do not unify them.

Model surface: `state`, `branches`, `activity`, `failure`, `now` (all `@Published private(set)`), `root`, plus `focus/activate/refresh/loadBranches/fetch/push/pull/checkout/startTicking/stopTicking/awaitCurrentLoad`.

## 7. Layout robustness, 260 → 520pt

The toolbar gets **exactly** the inspector's content width: `InspectorColumn` applies `.frame(width: width)` to `RightInspector()` *before* `.sidebarCard(...)`, so the card's 2pt leading / 8pt trailing padding sits outside. At minimum that's **260pt**.

**Budget at 260:** fetch 30 + two dividers 2 = 32 ⇒ **228pt for branch + sync**. Measured ideals:
- Sync, two-line, full subtitle: `8 + 12 + 7 + ~120 + 4 + ~28 + 8 ≈ 187`
- Branch, two-line: `12 + 12 + 7 + name + 5 + 8 + 8 ≈ 100+`

187 + 100 = 287 > 228. It **must** degrade. Rules, in firing order:

- **R1 — Sync wins.** `sync.layoutPriority(1)`, `branch.layoutPriority(0)`. The sync segment carries the actionable state and the count; a truncated branch name is still identifiable and its full name is repeated in the Changes header 40pt below and in its own tooltip. (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:73` and `ChangesPanel.swift:341` set the precedent for priority-driven yielding.)
- **R2 — Truncate, never wrap.** Every `Text` is `.lineLimit(1)`. Branch name `.truncationMode(.middle)`; sync title and subtitle `.tail`.
- **R3 — Subtitle abbreviates before it truncates.** `ViewThatFits`: `"Last fetched 9 minutes ago"` → `"Fetched 9 min. ago"`. Both strings come from the mapper, so the choice is declarative and works at *every* width, not at one hardcoded breakpoint.
- **R4 — Title abbreviates too.** `ViewThatFits` over `titleVariants`: `"Pull origin with rebase"` → `"Pull with rebase"` → `"Pull"`.
- **R5 — The "Current Branch" caption drops first.** Below ~120pt of branch-segment width the second `ViewThatFits` variant kicks in: name only, `titleFont`, vertically centred. **At 260pt the caption is not shown** — the branch icon already says "branch", and it's the least useful pixel in the bar. This is the concession that makes 260 work; say it out loud rather than shipping a clipped caption.
- **R6 — The sync glyph drops next.** `symbol` renders only in the widest sync variant; the pill's arrow already carries direction. Saves 19pt (12 slot + 7 spacing).
- **R7 — The pill never yields.** `.fixedSize()`.
- **R8 — Fixed 36pt height at every width.** No wrapping, no horizontal scroll, no reflow of the split view below.

**Floors, chosen so 260 fits by construction with 2pt slack:** `branchMinWidth 100` + `syncMinWidth 126` + `fetchWidth 30` + `2` dividers = **258 ≤ 260**. Worth a cheap unit test asserting that sum stays ≤ 260, so a future tweak fails a test instead of clipping on screen.

**Growing to 520:** `branchMaxWidth = 220` caps the branch cell so a short name doesn't hoard 200pt of dead space; sync takes `maxWidth: .infinity` and absorbs all the extra, its text left-aligned with the pill pushed right by the `Spacer`. That's exactly the GitHub Desktop proportion, and the extra width goes to the segment that can actually use it (the full subtitle).

# VCS Toolbar — UI Implementation Plan

## 1. Placement: above the split view, inside `RightInspector`

**Recommendation: put it in `RightInspector`, wrapping `InspectorSplitView` in a `VStack`.** Not `InspectorColumn`, not a section header, never a `.toolbar` modifier.

`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/ChangesPanel.swift:18-59` — `RightInspector.body` currently returns `InspectorSplitView(...)` directly. Change to:

```swift
var body: some View {
  let subs = store.activeInspectorSection.subSections
  VStack(spacing: 0) {
    VCSToolbar()                       // 36pt, fixed
    InspectorSplitView(headers: …)     // unchanged, verbatim
      .frame(minWidth: 260, maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)
  }
  .confirmationDialog(…)               // unchanged
}
```

Why here, with the receipts:

- **Zero AppKit changes.** `InspectorSplitView.sizeThatFits` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:432-437`) returns the proposal, so the `VStack` simply offers it 36pt less height. `InspectorPanePolicy.allocate` reads `splitView.bounds.height` live at `viewDidLayout` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:289-294`), so pane distribution, drag, weights persistence and `reallocateOnToggle` all keep working untouched. The only behavioural consequence: `expandedMinHeight` (120) × 3 + dividers ≈ 362pt is reached 36pt sooner in a short window, at which point the breakable `.defaultHigh` floor compresses panes and each pane's own `NSScrollView` scrolls — already the designed behaviour.
- **Not a section header.** `SectionHeader` is hosted by `InspectorPaneViewController.headerHost` at a hard `heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: InspectorPanePolicy.headerHeight)` = 34 (`InspectorSplitView.swift:95`). A toolbar there would collapse with the pane, would be pinned to 34pt, and would live behind an `NSHostingController` boundary that doesn't inherit `@EnvironmentObject` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:380-383`). And the user asked for it *above* the Changes header, which a header can't be.
- **Not `InspectorColumn`.** `InspectorColumn.swift:12-58` owns only docked chrome: width clamp 260–520, `sidebarCard(topMargin: 0, leadingMargin: 2, vibrant: true)`, and the `InspectorResizeHandle` overlay. Keeping the toolbar in `RightInspector` means it is inspector *content* with one owner, so a future second host of `RightInspector()` (today there is exactly one — verified) gets it free.
- **Plain SwiftUI tree.** `RightInspector` inherits `@EnvironmentObject var store` normally (no `AnyView` + `.environmentObject` injection needed — that ceremony at `ChangesPanel.swift:74-137` exists *only* because of the hosting boundary), `.onHover` fires (`ActivityBar` proves hover works inside the detail-only `NavigationSplitView`, `ActivityBar.swift:10-12`), and `.popover` anchors reliably without hand-hosting an `NSPopover`.
- **Never `.toolbar`.** The AppHang trap: the window toolbar is deliberately an empty AppKit `NSToolbar`. This is a plain SwiftUI view inside content, exactly like `WorkroomPaneTitleBar` (`WorkroomSplitView.swift:341-440`), which is the closest structural precedent.

**`.files` section: render the toolbar unconditionally.** It is repo-level state, not Changes-section state; hiding it on the Files pane would jump the layout 36pt on every activity-bar click and make the branch name vanish while browsing that same repo's tree. If Joel disagrees the gate is one line in `RightInspector.body`: `if store.activeInspectorSection == .changes { VCSToolbar() }`.

**Two easily-missed requirements:**
- The toolbar reads `ThemeService.shared.tokens` for its hairlines, which SwiftUI does not observe. It needs the `themeTick` pattern verbatim from `ActivityBar.swift:18` + `:47`: `@State private var themeTick = 0` and `.onReceive(NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for: .themeDidChange)) { _ in themeTick += 1 }`. Without it a theme switch leaves the dividers stale.
- **Background: clear (inherit the card), plus one 1pt `tokens.border` bottom hairline.** The Changes header below already fills `tokens.surface` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:512`); a second `surface` band directly above it merges into one 70pt grey block. A clear toolbar over the card's vibrant fill, separated by the same hairline device `RightInspector.sectionRule` uses (`ChangesPanel.swift:217-219`), reproduces the screenshot's relationship (toolbar = chrome, "Changes" = filled subheader) and sidesteps the card's 10pt corner clip having anything to clip. If it needs more weight, the only correct alternative is `tokens.panel` — the token that already means chrome (title bar, tab bar, activity bar) — accepting loss of vibrancy in that strip.

---

## 2. View decomposition, with real numbers

**One new file: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/VCSToolbar.swift`.**

```
enum VCSToolbarMetrics            // every number in one place
struct VCSToolbar: View           // the 36pt HStack + themeTick + .task activation
private struct VCSToolbarDivider  // full-bleed 1pt hairline
private struct VCSBranchSegment
private struct VCSSyncSegment
private struct VCSFetchSegment
private struct VCSCountPill
extension View { func vcsToolbarSegment(hovering:) -> some View }
```

### Metrics (`VCSToolbarMetrics`)

| constant | value | why this number |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | **36** | 11pt title (13pt line) + 1pt spacing + 10pt caption (12pt line) = 26, + 5pt top/bottom = 36. Two lines do not fit 34 without crowding, and 36 reads as a distinct band above the 34pt section headers. |
| `vPadding` | **5** | closes the 26 → 36 gap. |
| `outerInset` | **12** | matches `SectionHeader`'s `.padding(.horizontal, 12)` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:534`). |
| `innerInset` | **8** | inner sides of segments; tighter than 12 so the middle segment isn't starved. |
| `glyphSlot` | **12** | matches `SectionHeader`'s chevron `.frame(width: 12)` (`:528`). |
| `glyphSpacing` | **7** | matches `SectionHeader`'s `HStack(spacing: 7)` (`:522`). |
| `glyph` | **12** | between the inspector's 11 (`InspectorHeaderButton`) and the pane bar's 13 (`PaneToolbarIcon.glyph`) — needs to hold against a bold 11pt title without becoming a pane-bar icon. |
| `titleFont` | `.system(size: 11, weight: .semibold)` | identical to the section header title, so toolbar and header read as one type system. |
| `captionFont` | `.system(size: 10)` | one step down; `fgDim`. |
| `soloFont` | `.system(size: 11)` + `fgMuted` | the single-line sync state (see §4) — a lone 10pt `fgDim` line in a 36pt bar reads as a rendering bug. |
| `fetchWidth` | **30** | 22pt well + 4pt each side, per `ToolbarIconButtonStyle.footprint` (22 + 3×2 = 28) rounded to a divider-bounded cell. |
| `branchMinWidth` / `branchMaxWidth` | **100 / 220** | see §7. |
| `syncMinWidth` | **126** | see §7. |
| `pillHPad` / `pillVPad` | **5 / 1** | verbatim from `PRNumberBadge` (`ChangesPanel.swift:293`) and the `changesHeader` ref pills (`:690`). |

**The alignment-by-construction win:** `outerInset 12` + `glyphSlot 12` + `glyphSpacing 7` puts the branch glyph's centre at x=18 and the branch name's left edge at x=31 — *exactly* where the Changes header's chevron centre and "Changes" title left edge land. Verify by construction, not by eye, as the project rule requires.

### `VCSToolbar` body

```swift
HStack(spacing: 0) {
  VCSBranchSegment(…)
    .frame(minWidth: M.branchMinWidth, maxWidth: M.branchMaxWidth)
    .layoutPriority(0)
  VCSToolbarDivider()
  VCSSyncSegment(…)
    .frame(minWidth: M.syncMinWidth, maxWidth: .infinity)
    .layoutPriority(1)
  VCSToolbarDivider()
  VCSFetchSegment(…)
    .frame(width: M.fetchWidth)
}
.frame(height: M.height)
.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
.overlay(alignment: .bottom) { theme.tokens.border.frame(height: 1) }
.disabled(model.activity != .idle)
.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
.accessibilityIdentifier("vcs.toolbar")

## 3. Branch dropdown: custom `.popover`, not `Menu`

**Recommendation: a `.popover` hosting a new `BranchPickerPopover`, 300 × 360.**

New file `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/BranchPickerPopover.swift`.

Why not `Menu`:
1. **A filter field is mandatory at hundreds of branches, and `Menu` cannot host a `TextField`** — its content is NSMenu-backed.
2. **Opening a `Menu` over ~800 `Button`s materializes ~800 NSMenuItems synchronously on the main thread.** That is the *shape* of the recorded 2s AppHang (a toolbar item's `menuFormRepresentation`); the specific API differs but the lesson — don't hand SwiftUI a big menu — generalizes. `Menu` content is lazily *built* but not lazily *realized*.
3. Local/Remote grouping, a ✓ on the current branch, per-branch ahead/behind hints and a "New branch…" affordance are all either impossible or ugly in a `Menu`.

`Menu` is *safe* in this app in general — `prActionsMenu` (`ChangesPanel.swift:174-213`) uses it with `.menuStyle(.button)` + `InspectorMenuButtonStyle` and works fine. It's the size and the text field that rule it out here.

`.popover` anchors reliably because the toolbar is in the plain SwiftUI tree; and even inside the hosted tree it works — `HistoryPanel.swift:255` uses `.popover(arrowEdge: .leading)` from inside an `NSHostingController`-hosted body. Contrast the old title-bar bell, which had to hand-host an `NSPopover` (`ActivityBar.swift:130-133`).

Content, structurally cloned from `OpenWorkroomDialog` (`/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/OpenWorkroomDialog.swift`) — the app's existing searchable-grouped-list picker:

- `searchField` copied verbatim (`:153-181`): magnifyingglass + plain `TextField` + clear button, `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 8).fill(surface)` + `strokeBorder(border, 0.5)`, `@FocusState` auto-focused `.onAppear`.
- `ScrollViewReader` + `LazyVStack(spacing: 2)`. `Lazy` is the cap — no `renderCap` needed.
- Filter: **`PickerModel.filtered`** (plain substring), *not* `fuzzyFiltered`. Branch names are hierarchical and users type prefixes; fuzzy would let `mnfx` hit `main-fix`, which is confusing when a wrong pick checks out the wrong branch.
- Groups: `LOCAL`, then `REMOTE` listing only remotes with no local counterpart (so `main` isn't shown twice as `main` and `origin/main`). Group headers use `OpenWorkroomDialog`'s exact style (`.system(size: 10, weight: .semibold)`, `fgMuted`, `.textCase(.uppercase)`).
- Rows: `BranchRow` cloned from `OpenTargetRow` (`:213-249`) — leading 14pt slot holding `checkmark` for the current branch (else empty), name at `.system(size: 12, weight: .medium)` `.lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.middle)`, trailing dim `N ↑ M ↓` caption (phase 4), `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6)` highlight + `strokeBorder(fgDim, 1.5)` for the keyboard highlight.

## 4. Middle segment state machine

**New file `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSSyncPresentation.swift`** — a pure mapper, unit-tested like `Core/ChangeBadge.swift`. No SwiftUI, no `Date()` read.

```swift
struct VCSSyncSnapshot: Equatable, Sendable {
  var hasTarget: Bool          // a statusable inspector target exists
  var isRepo: Bool
  var branch: String?
  var hasRemote: Bool
  var upstream: String?        // nil ⇒ no tracking branch
  var ahead: Int
  var behind: Int
  var lastFetch: Date?
  var pullRebase: Bool         // repo's pull.rebase → wording
  var activity: Activity       // .idle .fetching .pushing .pulling
  var failure: String?
  var lastAction: VCSSyncAction   // for retry-after-failure
}

struct VCSSyncPresentation: Equatable {
  var titleVariants: [String]  // longest first; [] ⇒ single-line mode
  var subtitle: String
  var subtitleShort: String
  var symbol: String?
  var badge: Badge?            // (count, .ahead/.behind)
  var secondaryBadge: Badge?
  var action: VCSSyncAction    // .none .fetch .push .publish .pull .retry
  var isEnabled: Bool
  var tone: Tone               // .normal .warning .failure — glyph/subtitle tint only
  var help: String
  var accessibility: String    // spoken label
  var accessibilityValue: String  // carries the a11y-hidden badge counts
}

static func make(_ s: VCSSyncSnapshot, now: Date) -> VCSSyncPresentation
```

Full table (`title` = bold 11pt semibold; `subtitle` = dim 10pt; `—` in title ⇒ single-line mode, subtitle rendered at `soloFont`/`fgMuted` and vertically centred):

| # | condition | title | subtitle | badge | glyph | click | enabled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `!hasTarget` | — | "No workroom selected" | — | — | none | no |
| 2 | `!isRepo` / status failed | — | "No repository" | — | `exclamationmark.triangle` (warning) | none | no |
| 3 | `!hasRemote` | — | "No remote configured" | — | — | none | no |
| 4 | `upstream == nil` | "Publish branch" | "`<branch>` isn't on origin yet" | `N ↑` if `ahead>0` | `arrow.up.circle` | `.publish` (push `--set-upstream`) | yes |
| 5 | `lastFetch == nil`, `ahead==0`, `behind==0` | — | "Never fetched" | — | — | `.fetch` | yes |
| 6 | clean, fetched | — | "Last fetched \(rel)" | — | — | `.fetch` | yes |
| 7 | `ahead>0`, `behind==0` | **"Push origin"** | "Last fetched \(rel)" / "Never fetched" | `N ↑` | `arrow.up` | `.push` | yes |
| 8 | `behind>0`, `ahead==0` | `pullRebase ? "Pull origin with rebase" : "Pull origin"` | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` | `arrow.down` | `.pull` | yes |
| 9 | **diverged** `ahead>0 && behind>0` | `pullRebase ? "Pull origin with rebase" : "Pull origin"` | "Last fetched \(rel)" | `M ↓` **then** `N ↑` | `arrow.up.arrow.down` | `.pull` | yes |
| 10 | `.fetching` | "Fetching…" | "from origin" | — | spinner | none | no |
| 11 | `.pushing` | "Pushing…" | "to origin" | keep `N ↑` | spinner | none | no |
| 12 | `.pulling` | "Pulling…" | "from origin" | keep `M ↓` | spinner | none | no |
| 13 | `failure != nil`, idle | previous action's title | error's first line, `tone: .failure` | keep counts | `exclamationmark.triangle.fill` | `.retry` (= `lastAction`) | yes |

Precedence: 13 > 10/11/12 > 1 > 2 > 3 > 4 > 9 > 8 > 7 > 5 > 6.

**Two opinionated calls:**
- **Diverged → Pull, not Push.** git refuses a non-fast-forward push, and GitHub Desktop makes Pull primary for the same reason. Badge shows both pills, ↓ first (the one the action addresses).
- **`upstream == nil` + `ahead > 0` → `.publish`, not `.push`.** This is the workroom case: workrooms are `git worktree add -b` branches with no upstream — the exact scenario `VCSModels.swift:20-25` documents as why `VCSPushState` is origin-scoped rather than `@{u}`-scoped. Getting this wrong makes every workroom read "Push origin" against an upstream that doesn't exist.

`titleVariants`, longest first, feeding the `ViewThatFits` ladder:
- state 8/9: `["Pull origin with rebase", "Pull with rebase", "Pull"]`
- state 7: `["Push origin", "Push"]`
- state 4: `["Publish branch", "Publish"]`

`subtitle` / `subtitleShort`: `"Last fetched 9 minutes ago"` / `"Fetched 9 min. ago"`.

### Relative time

```swift
private static let fullFormatter: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = { $0.unitsStyle = .full; … }()
private static let shortFormatter: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = { $0.unitsStyle = .abbreviated; … }()

static func fetchedAgo(_ date: Date, now: Date, short: Bool = false) -> String
```
Under 60s → `"just now"` (so it reads "Last fetched just now", never "in 0 seconds"). `static let` formatters because they're expensive to construct — `NotificationsList.swift:265-270` already does this. **Do not reuse `NotificationsList.timeAgo`**: it's `private`, `.abbreviated`, and reads `Date()` internally, so it's untestable. `now` is a parameter here precisely so the whole mapper is pure and testable at fixed instants.

### Keeping it live

**The ticker lives on the view model, not the view.** A `Timer.publish` created inside `body` is re-created on every parent render and re-subscribes; a stored property on a `View` struct has the same problem. So `VCSSyncModel` owns a `Timer` started by `startTicking()` / stopped by `stopTicking()`, bumping `@Published private(set) var now: Date`. The view passes `model.now` into the mapper.

- **Interval 30s, tolerance 5s.** Under 60s the copy says "just now" anyway, so 30s bounds the visible staleness of "9 minutes ago" to ±30s — invisible. `tolerance` lets the OS coalesce wakeups.
- Started from the toolbar's `.task`, stopped in `.onDisappear`. Because the toolbar only exists inside `InspectorColumn`, which `RootView.swift:162-165` constructs inside `if showInspector`, a hidden inspector means **no timer at all** — zero idle wakeups, for free. That's the same mechanism `AppStore.swift:334-336` documents for History.
- Invalidation is scoped to the 36pt strip: the `@Published now` is read only by `VCSSyncSegment`, so the tick never re-renders `InspectorSplitView`.

**New: `/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSSyncModel.swift`, owned by `AppStore` as `let vcsSync: VCSSyncModel`**, sitting beside `let fileTree = FileTreeModel()` (`AppStore.swift:400`) and `let commitHistory: HistoryModel` (`:407`).

### What the model needs from the engine — state this to the parallel agent

```swift
struct VCSSyncState: Equatable, Sendable {
  var branch: String?      // current local branch / jj bookmark
  var upstream: String?    // e.g. "origin/main"; nil ⇒ no tracking branch
  var hasRemote: Bool
  var ahead: Int           // vs UPSTREAM, not origin-wide
  var behind: Int
  var lastFetch: Date?     // PROVIDER-owned, read from the repo
  var pullRebase: Bool
}

struct VCSBranch: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable {
  var name: String; var isCurrent: Bool; var isRemote: Bool
  var upstream: String?; var ahead: Int?; var behind: Int?; var tip: String?
  var id: String { (isRemote ? "r:" : "l:") + name }
}

protocol VCSSyncProviding: Sendable {
  func syncState(root: URL) async throws -> VCSSyncState
  func branches(root: URL) async throws -> [VCSBranch]        // called lazily, popover only
  func fetch(root: URL) async throws
  func push(root: URL, setUpstream: Bool) async throws
  func pull(root: URL, rebase: Bool) async throws
  func checkout(root: URL, branch: String) async throws
  func createBranch(root: URL, name: String, from: String?) async throws   // phase 4
}
```

Two things the engine must get right, both flagged because the existing code gets them differently on purpose:
1. **`lastFetch` is provider-owned, read from the repo** (git: `.git/FETCH_HEAD` mtime; jj: the op log), never "when the app last called fetch". A `git fetch` typed in the workroom's own terminal must move the number.
2. **`ahead`/`behind` are upstream-scoped (`@{u}`)**, which is deliberately *different* from `VCSPushState`'s origin-wide scope. `VCSModels.swift:19-31` explains why push state is origin-scoped ("workrooms are `git worktree add -b` branches with no upstream, so the badge would never appear where it matters most") — that choice is right for the history badge and wrong for this toolbar, where "no upstream" is a first-class state (#4, Publish). Do not unify them.

Model surface: `state`, `branches`, `activity`, `failure`, `now` (all `@Published private(set)`), `root`, plus `focus/activate/refresh/loadBranches/fetch/push/pull/checkout/startTicking/stopTicking/awaitCurrentLoad`.

Mirror `focusHistoryIfShown()` (`AppStore.swift:325-340`) exactly:

Three layers, all already-proven:

## 6. Interaction, feedback, confirmation

- **Hover:** full-segment `tokens.hover`, opacity-only, `.easeOut(0.12)`, gated on `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)`. Every segment needs its **own** `.onHover` (so `.help`'s tracking area installs) *and* `.contentShape(Rectangle())` — the non-negotiable convention.
- **Disabled:** `.opacity(0.4)` (matching `ToolbarIconButtonStyle.swift:58`'s disabled dim) and no hover fill. The bar keeps its 36pt height in every state, so the layout never jumps.
- **Spinner:** `ProgressView().controlSize(.mini)` in the 12pt glyph slot (`.small` is ~16pt and overflows; `TerminalStatusBar.swift:234` sets the precedent). All three segments disable together via the single `.disabled(model.activity != .idle)`.
- **Error presentation — three tiers, and *not* `inspectorMessage`.** `inspectorMessage(_:)` (`ChangesPanel.swift:796-804`) is a `.body`-sized, 12pt-padded full-width placeholder for a section *body*; it is the wrong shape for a 36pt bar.
  1. **Inline** in the sync segment's subtitle: first line of the error, `tokens.failure` tint, `exclamationmark.triangle.fill` glyph, segment stays clickable to retry. Primary surface.
  2. **Full text in `.help(...)`**, since the subtitle truncates.
  3. **Escalate to the existing error alert** (`store.errorTitle`/`errorMessage` → `RootView.swift:180-198`) only for failures that leave the repo needing action — push rejected, pull produced conflicts, auth failure. Rule: read/transient failures (fetch timed out) stay inline; state-changing failures also alert, because a silently rejected push is a real problem.
- **Confirmation:**
  - Fetch: **never**.
  - Push / Publish: **never** — non-destructive, and it's the whole point of the button (GitHub Desktop doesn't confirm either).
  - Pull, **and** branch checkout: confirm **only when the working tree is dirty** (`store.workroomStatuses[sid]?.dirty == true`) — a rebase-pull or a checkout over uncommitted changes either fails or stashes. Reuse `RightInspector`'s existing mechanism verbatim: a second `@State private var pendingVCSConfirm: PendingVCSAction?` + `.confirmationDialog` beside the PR one (`ChangesPanel.swift:15-16`, `:48-58`, `:264-270`). Zero new machinery.
  - Phase 1 ships fetch-only, so phase 1 needs no confirmation at all.

## 7. Layout robustness, 260 → 520pt

The toolbar gets **exactly** the inspector's content width: `InspectorColumn` applies `.frame(width: width)` to `RightInspector()` *before* `.sidebarCard(...)`, so the card's 2pt leading / 8pt trailing padding sits outside. At minimum that's **260pt**.

**Budget at 260:** fetch 30 + two dividers 2 = 32 ⇒ **228pt for branch + sync**. Measured ideals:
- Sync, two-line, full subtitle: `8 + 12 + 7 + ~120 + 4 + ~28 + 8 ≈ 187`
- Branch, two-line: `12 + 12 + 7 + name + 5 + 8 + 8 ≈ 100+`

187 + 100 = 287 > 228. It **must** degrade. Rules, in firing order:

- **R1 — Sync wins.** `sync.layoutPriority(1)`, `branch.layoutPriority(0)`. The sync segment carries the actionable state and the count; a truncated branch name is still identifiable and its full name is repeated in the Changes header 40pt below and in its own tooltip. (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:73` and `ChangesPanel.swift:341` set the precedent for priority-driven yielding.)
- **R2 — Truncate, never wrap.** Every `Text` is `.lineLimit(1)`. Branch name `.truncationMode(.middle)`; sync title and subtitle `.tail`.
- **R3 — Subtitle abbreviates before it truncates.** `ViewThatFits`: `"Last fetched 9 minutes ago"` → `"Fetched 9 min. ago"`. Both strings come from the mapper, so the choice is declarative and works at *every* width, not at one hardcoded breakpoint.
- **R4 — Title abbreviates too.** `ViewThatFits` over `titleVariants`: `"Pull origin with rebase"` → `"Pull with rebase"` → `"Pull"`.
- **R5 — The "Current Branch" caption drops first.** Below ~120pt of branch-segment width the second `ViewThatFits` variant kicks in: name only, `titleFont`, vertically centred. **At 260pt the caption is not shown** — the branch icon already says "branch", and it's the least useful pixel in the bar. This is the concession that makes 260 work; say it out loud rather than shipping a clipped caption.
- **R6 — The sync glyph drops next.** `symbol` renders only in the widest sync variant; the pill's arrow already carries direction. Saves 19pt (12 slot + 7 spacing).
- **R7 — The pill never yields.** `.fixedSize()`.
- **R8 — Fixed 36pt height at every width.** No wrapping, no horizontal scroll, no reflow of the split view below.

**Floors, chosen so 260 fits by construction with 2pt slack:** `branchMinWidth 100` + `syncMinWidth 126` + `fetchWidth 30` + `2` dividers = **258 ≤ 260**. Worth a cheap unit test asserting that sum stays ≤ 260, so a future tweak fails a test instead of clipping on screen.

**Growing to 520:** `branchMaxWidth = 220` caps the branch cell so a short name doesn't hoard 200pt of dead space; sync takes `maxWidth: .infinity` and absorbs all the extra, its text left-aligned with the pill pushed right by the `Spacer`. That's exactly the GitHub Desktop proportion, and the extra width goes to the segment that can actually use it (the full subtitle).

  macapp AppStore eager commitHistory.focus is NOT a cheap pointer move: HistoryModel.focus -> load -> VCSProviding.log = repo open + 101-commit revwalk + ref enumeration + GitGraph.unpushed range walk. It is also undebounced and runBlocking cannot be cancelled mid-flight, so N rapid selections dispatch N concurrent revwalks that each hold a GCD thread to completion (the History-loads-forever starvation shape). Gate every eager focus on inspectorIsVisible AND historySectionShown, and keep the debounce inside HistoryModel.load (pre-dispatch sleep) so the panel .task and the metadata watcher are covered too, not just the store call sites. - [multigroup-prune-survivor-must-honour-former-selection] (confidence: 9/10, cross-model, 2026-07-30)
  When a per-window model goes from ONE collection to a LIST (macapp workroomSplit -> workroomSplits), every self-heal that re-points selection must know WHICH member of the list the user was viewing. AppStore.apply nils a dead selection BEFORE calling pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves, so the prune has to be handed the pre-validation selection (formerSelection:) or it picks survivors.first and lands the user in a split group they were never looking at. Claude adversarial subagent and Codex independently flagged this as the one real regression of the multi-group refactor. - [focusedvalue-menu-enablement-refreshes-async-in-uitests] (confidence: 9/10, observed, 2026-07-27)

An XCUITest that dismisses a dialog and immediately typeKey()s a menu shortcut races that refresh: the key equivalent lands while the item is still disabled and is silently DROPPED, with no retry, so the test fails on correct code. Fix: observe the item become enabled first (open the File menu and poll isEnabled) before sending the shortcut. Also note enablement is only queryable with the menu OPEN. To assert real keyboard focus in XCUITest, type without clicking and check where the characters land (e.g. a filter field value), which is also the user-visible behaviour. Gate every eager focus on inspectorIsVisible AND historySectionShown, and keep the debounce inside HistoryModel.load (pre-dispatch sleep) so the panel .task and the metadata watcher are covered too, not just the store call sites. (files: macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift, macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/HistoryModel.swift)
- [multigroup-prune-survivor-must-honour-former-selection] (confidence: 9/10, cross-model, 2026-07-30)
  When a per-window model goes from ONE collection to a LIST (macapp workroomSplit -> workroomSplits), every self-heal that re-points selection must know WHICH member of the list the user was viewing. AppStore.apply nils a dead selection BEFORE calling pruneWorkroomSplitToLiveLeaves, so the prune has to be handed the pre-validation selection (formerSelection:) or it picks survivors.first and lands the user in a split group they were never looking at. Claude adversarial subagent and Codex independently flagged this as the one real regression of the multi-group refactor. (files: macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore+WorkroomSplit.swift, macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift)
- [focusedvalue-menu-enablement-refreshes-async-in-uitests] (confidence: 9/10, observed, 2026-07-27)
  macapp menu-item enablement flows through focusedSceneValue/@FocusedValue, which re-publishes ASYNCHRONOUSLY. An XCUITest that dismisses a dialog and immediately typeKey()s a menu shortcut races that refresh: the key equivalent lands while the item is still disabled and is silently DROPPED, with no retry, so the test fails on correct code. Fix: observe the item become enabled first (open the File menu and poll isEnabled) before sending the shortcut. Also note enablement is only queryable with the menu OPEN. (files: macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/NewWorkroomDialogUITests.swift, macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/RootView.swift)
- [pane-isSelected-is-model-focus-not-first-responder] (confidence: 9/10, observed, 2026-07-27)

So it CANNOT be used to assert that a terminal gave up/regained keyboard focus: TerminalContainerView.isFocusedPane drives the responder while the ring/find-bar/a11y trait keep reading the model value, and a fix that resigns the responder deliberately leaves the ring up. Corrects the implication in single-pane-fixture-has-no-queryable-focus-signal — fixture-gating the trait makes single-pane MODEL focus queryable, nothing more. To assert real keyboard focus in XCUITest, type without clicking and check where the characters land (e.g. a filter field value), which is also the user-visible behaviour. (files: macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/PaneTreeView.swift, macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalContainerView.swift, macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/NewWorkroomDialogUITests.swift)
- [single-pane-fixture-has-no-queryable-focus-signal] (confidence: 9/10, observed, 2026-07-27)
  macapp PaneTreeView.swift:460 adds .isSelected only when focused && multiPane, so in the single-pane UITestFixture there is NO a11y signal for terminal keyboard focus — any XCUITest asserting the terminal has focus is vacuous. Combined with the recorded fact that synthetic events lie about focus/hover, single-pane focus behaviour is currently unverifiable at any tier. Fix by fixture-gating the trait: focused && (multiPane || UITestFixture.isActive) — fixture-gated, not unconditional, since a lone pane reporting selected to VoiceOver is wrong. (files: macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/PaneTreeView.swift)
- [isEditingTextField-makes-cmdR-behind-sheet-tests-tautological] (confidence: 9/10, cross-model, 2026-07-27)
  macapp AppStore.isEditingTextField (AppStore.swift:1557-1562, NSApp.keyWindow?.firstResponder is NSText) ALREADY guards runOrFocusRunCommand/stopSelectedRunCommand/restartSelectedRunCommand at :1595/:1638/:1646 — added by review #8 for exactly this reason. So any test asserting that Cmd-R does not fire behind a sheet with a text field (Add Project, Project Settings, Delete Project, Workroom Label) PASSES on unmodified code and proves nothing. Use Cmd-T (New Terminal), which has no such guard. It also means a focus fix that moves first responder into a dialog text field buys Cmd-R/Shift-Cmd-R/Opt-Cmd-R blocking for free. (files: macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift)
- [panetreeview-contentpanel-param-shadows-content] (confidence: 9/10, cross-model, 2026-07-27)
  In macapp PaneTreeView, PaneLeafView has a stored `let content: TabContent` (:349) AND a helper `contentPanel(_ content: some View)` (:531) whose parameter shadows it. Code inside contentPanel that says `content` resolves to the View, not the TabContent, so `content.filePath` targets the wrong type and does not compile. When threading a tab-content-derived value into the footer, pass it as an explicit parameter from paneContent (where the descriptor is already in scope) rather than reading the property inside contentPanel. (files: macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/PaneTreeView.swift)
- [nshostingview-no-a11y-children-in-unit-tests] (confidence: 9/10, cross-model, 2026-07-27)

PaneRenderingTests works only because GhosttySurfaceView is a real NSView it can count in the AppKit hierarchy; a SwiftUI Text is not a subview and is unreachable. Do NOT plan in-gate render assertions for SwiftUI content: test the DECISION (a pure accessor/predicate) in the unit gate and leave rendering to XCUITest. attachment.planContent:
# VCS toolbar: branch label + push/pull/fetch status

> Revised after `/plan-eng-review`. 7 review findings + 25 outside-voice findings folded across 17
> decisions (D3–D19). **Branch switching was cut (D14)**; two verified engine bugs were fixed
> (D13, D15). See the review report at the end.

## Context

The VCS inspector can only *read*. `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`)
is a strictly read-only protocol — 8 members, no mutations, no network. There is **no** branch
listing, **no** fetch/push/pull, **no** ahead/behind counts, and **no** last-fetch time anywhere in
the app or the Rust core. The only branch name on screen is a `.caption` capsule in the Changes body
(`ChangesPanel.swift:669-730`) and one in the status bar (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`).

So a user in a workroom leaves the app for every remote interaction: they can see what changed but
not whether it's pushed, how far behind origin they are, or when they last fetched.

**Outcome:** a 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector, shown only when the Changes
activity section is active. Current branch as a read-only label, a sync segment that reads
"Push origin / Last fetched 9 minutes ago" with an ahead/behind pill and performs the action on
click, and a fetch icon. Working for both git and jj.

**Cut during review (D14):** branch *switching*. Workrooms **are** branches — identity is the
directory basename (`internal/vcs/git.go:70-80`; no `branch` key in `internal/config/`) — so
switching a workroom's branch makes its name permanently wrong, and the jj path was reproduced
deleting a working-copy file and orphaning the workroom's commit. Segment 1's click opens the
existing ⌘O workroom picker instead. "New workroom from branch…" is filed as the product-correct
successor.

---

## Decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D3 | Write ops go behind a **new** `VCSWriting` protocol + `VCS.writer(for:)`, conformed by a CLI-backed type holding the injected runner. `VCSProviding` untouched — reads stay structurally unable to mutate. Supersedes `TODOS.md:118`. |
| D4 | **git** write ops also route through `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`. Worktrees share one `.git`; a lock loss mid-`pull --rebase` wedges a workroom. Rename deferred. |
| D5 | `StatusCommandRunner` pins `stdin` to `/dev/null` and, for network ops, sets `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"` + `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`, clearing `SSH_ASKPASS`/`DISPLAY`. |
| D6 | Two ASCII diagrams, in this plan and mirrored as code comments. |
| D7 | The post-pull conflict determination lives in the **model**, after the gate releases — not in the writer. |
| D8 | One state struct. The mapper takes `(state, activity, failure, pullRebase, now)`. `VCSSyncSnapshot` deleted. |
| D9 | All four branch-name implementations unify onto **one shared cache**. |
| D10 | A counting stub asserts a branch-label read spawns **zero** VCS calls. |
| D11 | The UI-test fixture records requested actions; 4 flow tests assert the button→engine seam. |
| D12 | Remote-ref data is cached **per project root**, not per workroom. |
| D13 | Ahead/behind come from `git rev-list --left-right --count`. **`%(push:*)` is deleted** — see below. |
| D14 | **Switch cut.** Push + pull stay; pull gains a `rebase --abort` affordance. |
| D15 | A workroom reads the **shared** git dir's `FETCH_HEAD`, not its own. |
| D16 | **Auto-fetch on inspector focus**, interval-guarded. Knowingly supersedes `TODOS.md:324`. |
| D17 | Forward `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`/`SSH_AGENT_PID`/`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` from `ShellEnvironment.environment()` for network ops only. |

**Backend:** shell out to `git`/`jj` via `StatusCommandRunning`. Auth is the user's own agent and
credential helpers; the app already shells `gh`. SwiftGitX is unusable for this — `Repository+fetch.swift:30`
and `+push.swift:49` pass `NULL` for the options struct, so there is no credential path at all, and
`pull` doesn't exist. **Zero Rust/UniFFI changes; no `make app-vcs`.**

### Two bugs the review caught, both verified on git 2.55

**`%(push:track)` does not work for the branches this product creates.** Under `push.default=simple`
— git's built-in default — a branch with no upstream yields `PUSH=[]` and `PUSHT=[]`. Only `current`
and `matching` populate them. Every workroom is `git worktree add -b` (no upstream), so the headline
count would be blank on any machine not set to `current`. It looked fine only because this machine is
`current`. Measured:

```
push.default=simple    UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[]                PUSHT=[]
push.default=current   UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[origin/feat]     PUSHT=[[gone]]
push.default=upstream  UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[]                PUSHT=[]
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null (what the integration test does)  PUSH=[] PUSHT=[]
```

**`FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree, so fetching at the root never writes the workroom's copy.**
`git rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD` returns `.git/FETCH_HEAD` at the root but
`.git/worktrees/<n>/FETCH_HEAD` inside a workroom. The original plan fetched at the root *and* read
the per-worktree path — so every workroom would have read "never fetched" forever.

### Sync-segment state precedence (D6 — mirror above `VCSSyncPresentation.make`)

Three orthogonal axes collapse to one order. Read top-down; first match wins.

```
  failure?  ──yes──►  [13] retry previous action        tone: failure
     │no
  in flight? ──yes──►  [10/11/12] Fetching…/Pushing…/Pulling…    disabled
     │no
  target valid? ──no──►  [1] no workroom  ·  [2] no repository    disabled
     │yes
  has remote? ──no───►  [3] "No remote configured"               disabled
     │yes
  upstream missing / gone? ──yes──►  [4] "Publish branch"   → push --set-upstream
     │no
  ahead>0 && behind>0 ──yes──►  [9] "Pull <remote> with rebase"  badge: M↓ then N↑
     │no                              (pull, NOT push — git refuses non-ff)
  behind>0 ──yes──►  [8] "Pull <remote> with rebase"             badge: M↓
     │no
  ahead>0  ──yes──►  [7] "Push <remote>"                         badge: N↑
     │no
  never fetched ──yes──►  [5] "Never fetched"          → fetch
     │no
                        [6] "Last fetched <rel>"       → fetch
```

`<remote>` is interpolated from `primaryRemote`, **never** the literal "origin" —
`remote.pushDefault` can make that wrong (verified: `-c remote.pushDefault=upstream` →
`PUSH=[upstream/feat]`).

## Engine

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift`

A new protocol + one CLI-backed conformer + `VCS.writer(for:)`, alongside the existing
`VCS.provider(for:)` (`VCSProviding.swift:87`). This is the growth surface for the rest of Phase 2
(commit/amend, bookmark management, jj split/absorb/undo), which is why it's a protocol and not a
standalone resolver — but it is deliberately **separate** from `VCSProviding` so a read path cannot
reach a mutation.

```swift
protocol VCSWriting: Sendable {
  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
  func fetch(path:projectRoot:remote:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func push(path:projectRoot:current:remote:setUpstream:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func pullRebase(path:projectRoot:current:remote:tracking:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func abortRebase(path:projectRoot:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult          // D14
}

enum VCS {
  /// Routes by `repoKind(at:)`, same as `provider(for:)`. Throws `.unsupportedRepo`.
  static func writer(for root: URL, projectRoot: URL,
                     runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner(),
                     makeProvider: @escaping @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
                       = { try VCS.provider(for: $0) }) throws -> VCSWriting
}
```

One conformer, `CLIVCSWriter`, holds the runner (the reason this can't go on `VCSProviding` —
`GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider` are stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere
to put it). It switches on repo kind internally and keeps all semantics in `static` pure
arg-builders/parsers/classifiers — the `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` testability pattern.

Timeouts: `refTimeout 5`, `fetch/push 120`, `pull 300`, gate `.shared`.
Reuse `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`:63`) verbatim on every git call. jj gets
`--color never --no-pager`; **reads** get `--ignore-working-copy`, **mutations must not**.

`currentRef` comes from `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)` — the app's existing canonical answer
including `.ancestor`/`.detached`. Do not re-derive it.

### git — reads

```
# 1. remote refs + the remotes list (no cap needed — the picker is gone)
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref --format='%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(symref)' refs/remotes

# 2. exact two-way divergence, config-independent  (D13)
git -c core.fsmonitor= rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>
```

- **Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)`** — that's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose short name
  is the bare remote. Its target also yields the default branch for free.
- `primaryRemote` = `origin` if present, else the first remote, else `nil`.
- The counterpart ref is `refs/remotes/<primaryRemote>/<current-branch>`, existence-checked against
  the list from (1). Absent ⇒ state 4 ("Publish branch"), no counts — this is the workroom default.
- `rev-list` runs only when the counterpart exists. Output is `<ahead>\t<behind>`.
- **`%(push:*)` and `%(upstream:*)` are not used for counts.** That also dissolves the "upstream is a
  local branch" case (measured: `UP=[main] UPT=[[ahead 3]] PUSH=[]`), because we only ever compare
  against `refs/remotes/`.

**Last fetch (D15):** mtime of `<common gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD`. Resolve purely — `.git` as a directory
⇒ `<path>/.git`; `.git` as a **file** ⇒ read it, strip `gitdir: `, then strip the trailing
`/worktrees/<name>` to reach the common dir. No subprocess. Unit-test all three shapes plus a
malformed pointer.

### git — actions

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git … fetch <remote>` | **project root** |
| push | `git … push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| pull | `git … fetch <remote>` (root), then `git … pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| abort | `git … rebase --abort` | workroom |

No `--prune` (let `fetch.prune` decide), no `--no-write-fetch-head` (we need it), **never**
`--force`/`--force-with-lease`. `--set-upstream` only when there is no upstream yet. `--autostash` is
mandatory — workroom trees are always dirty.

### jj — reads

`jj bookmark list --all-remotes --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager -T '<template>'`,
NUL-separated: `name`, `remote`, `commit_id`, `present`, `conflict`, `tracked`,
`tracking_ahead_count`, `tracking_behind_count`. Verified on jj 0.43:

- The template keyword is **`self`**, not `ref`.
- The `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing — calling
  `tracking_*_count()` on a local ref renders the literal `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>`.
- **Drop `remote == "git"`** — a colocated repo has that pseudo-remote and `--all-remotes` includes it.
- **jj's counts are inverted relative to git.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means the
  *remote* is ahead = git's **behind**. Swap on ingest, in one commented line, pinned by a
  cross-backend integration test.
- `present == 0` ⇒ `gone`. `tracked == 0` ⇒ `comparedTo` set, counts `nil`.
- Reads take no lock, so they stay ungated. Measured ~72ms on a 30-bookmark repo.

**Anonymous `@`** (`currentRef.kind == .ancestor` — the normal workroom state, since
`jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark): the bookmark row's counts describe the *ancestor*, not
the user's work. Only then, two extra revset counts:

```
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@' -T '"x\n"'   → ahead
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r '@..remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)' -T '"x\n"'   → behind
```

`remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@` is exactly what bare `jj git push` sends, so the count and the
button agree by construction.

**Last fetch:** jj-lib 0.43 shells `git fetch … --no-write-fetch-head`
(`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`), so `FETCH_HEAD` is never written — confirmed
empirically. Scan the op log instead:

```
jj op log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager --limit 200
  -T 'self.time().end().format("%s") ++ "\x00" ++ self.description().first_line() ++ "\n"'
```

Newest-first; first line whose description starts with `fetch from git remote`. Fragile to a jj
rewording — mitigated by prefix matching, a graceful failure (one absent label, never a wrong one),
and an integration test that reddens on a jj bump.

### jj — actions (all inside the gate)

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | **project root** |
| push (bookmarked) | `jj git push --remote <r> --bookmark <name>` | **project root** |
| push (anonymous) | `jj git push --remote <r> --change <rev>` | **project root** |
| pull | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` (root), then `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote>` (workroom) | — |

- **`--change` is jj's built-in anonymous-branch push** (confirmed on 0.43): creates the bookmark,
  tracks it automatically, names it via `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
  `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`). No hand-rolled naming policy.
- **Revision choice:** `@` if it has changes or a description, else `@-` — jj refuses to push a commit
  with an empty description, and a fresh `@` has neither. `WorkroomStatus.jjWorkingCopy`
  (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`) already carries `description` + `files`, so this costs no process. Pure
  decision function; unit-test it.
- **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock** — even a read (`jj git remote
  list` fails with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export"*). So derive the remote list from
  `bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes; never call `jj git remote list` on the read path.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocesses** — it
  exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, but `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout`
  and `killTree`s at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely gone. Compose
  `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }` with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Document this — it
  reads like a violation and isn't.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`** — `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@`, the pull-rebase shape.
  Run unconditionally; already-a-descendant prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts.** Never infer success from the exit code — see D7.

### Models — appended to `Core/VCSModels.swift`

`VCSTracking { comparedTo, ahead: Int?, behind: Int?, gone }` — counts from the *local* ref's view;
`nil` means unanswerable, never zero.
`VCSLastFetch { at(Date), never, unknown }` — three-way, not `Date?`; `.unknown` must never render as
"never" (the `VCSPushState.unknown` rule).
`VCSRemoteState { current: VCSRef, tracking: VCSTracking?, remotes: [String], primaryRemote: String?, lastFetch: VCSLastFetch, resolvedAt: Date }`

**Cut by review:** `VCSBranchRef` and its `checkedOutIn`/`committedAt`/`isCurrent` (no picker — D14);
`refCap`/`refsTruncated`/`pickerOrder` (nothing enumerates 500 refs any more); `VCSTracking.pullFrom`,
`hasUnbookmarkedWork` (redundant with `current.kind == .ancestor`), per-row tracking, and

At the top of `VCSWriting.swift`: `VCSRemoteAction { fetch, push, pull, abortRebase }`,
`VCSRemoteFailure { toolMissing, timedOut, authRequired, hostKeyUnverified, noRemote, rejected, dirtyWorkingTree, rebaseInProgress, locked, other }`,
`VCSRemoteResolution { state, absent, keepPrior, failed }`,
`VCSRemoteActionResult { ok, failed }` — deliberately **not** folded into `VCSError`, which is the

### Error classification

`static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?` — one pure function, `nil` on
success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `Host key verification failed` | `.hostKeyUnverified` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<common gitdir>/worktrees/<n>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

Copy that matters:
- `.authRequired` — *"Workroom never prompts for credentials. Load your key into ssh-agent, or
  configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`)."* With D5 this
  fails instantly instead of hanging; with D17 agent users don't reach it at all.
- `.hostKeyUnverified` — *"`<host>` isn't in your known_hosts. Connect once from a terminal to accept
  its key."* `BatchMode=yes` makes this a hard failure rather than a stall.
- `.rebaseInProgress` — *"A rebase is in progress in this workroom."* Offers **Abort rebase**, never
  Retry (D14).
- `.rejected` — offers **Pull**, never Force.

### New: `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift` (D24)

Old tools were the review's one critical failure gap: `git for-each-ref` fails **atomically** on an
unknown atom (verified — `--format='%(bogusatom)'` produces `fatal: unknown field name`, no partial
output), and `jj bookmark` was `jj branch` before ~0.18 with `tracking_*_count()` newer still. The app
bundles neither binary — `ShellEnvironment.path()` takes whatever is on PATH. So one old tool turned
the whole feature into `.other` with raw stderr. Declaring a floor closes it.

**git is required; jj is optional.** Both are floor-checked when present, but they mean different
things: no `git` is a broken install (the Go CLI shells `git worktree add` to create a workroom at
all), whereas no `jj` is the normal state for a git-only user and must be silent.

```swift
enum VCSToolVersions {
  static let gitFloor = SemVer(2, 41, 0)   // jj-lib 0.43's own MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION
  static let jjFloor  = SemVer(0, 43, 0)   // the jj-lib the app links

  enum Status: Equatable, Sendable { case ok(SemVer), belowFloor(SemVer), notInstalled, unknown }
  struct Report: Equatable, Sendable {
    let git: Status            // required
    let jj: Status             // optional — `.notInstalled` is not a problem on its own
    /// Whether remote actions are permitted for a project of this VCS. git projects need only git;
    /// jj projects need both, since a colocated jj repo drives git underneath.
    func allowsRemoteActions(vcs: String) -> Bool
    /// Warnings to publish. Never includes jj `.notInstalled` unless a jj project is registered.
    func warnings(hasJJProject: Bool) -> [ToolWarning]
  }

  static func parseGit(_ stdout: String) -> SemVer?   // "git version 2.55.0" / Apple's "(Apple Git-154)"
  static func parseJJ(_ stdout: String) -> SemVer?    // "jj 0.43.0"
  static func probe(runner: StatusCommandRunning, probeJJ: Bool) async -> Report
}
```

**Why these numbers, not arbitrary ones:** git 2.41 is the floor **jj itself** enforces for its git
subprocess (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:48` `MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION = "2.41.0"`), so it excludes
nobody a jj user isn't already excluded by; and jj 0.43 matches the jj-lib the Rust core links, which
matters because an older CLI may not understand the repo format that library writes. Both sit
comfortably above what the plan actually issues (`%(symref)` needs 2.8, `pull --autostash` needs 2.9).

**Scoping is per project VCS, not global.** A git project's toolbar must not be disabled because the
user's `jj` is old, and vice versa. Concretely:

| Condition | git project | jj project | Warning |
|---|---|---|---|
| git ok, jj ok | enabled | enabled | none |
| git ok, jj absent | enabled | actions disabled | only if a jj project is registered |
| git ok, jj below floor | enabled | actions disabled | yes, jj-specific |
| git below floor | actions disabled | actions disabled | yes, git-specific (jj drives git underneath) |
| git absent | actions disabled | actions disabled | yes — broken install; workroom creation is already impossible |

**When:** background, at app start, *after* `ShellEnvironment` sets the PATH floor
(`WorkroomApp.swift:23`) — the probe needs PATH to find the binaries at all. One `git --version` and,
only when a jj project is registered, one `jj --version`; 5s each, never blocking launch.

**Below floor ⇒ two consequences, kept in agreement:**
1. A persistent notification via the existing `NotificationCenterStore` (the left-sidebar list, issue
   #118) naming both the found and required versions. Non-modal — a too-old tool must never stop the
   app being useful for terminals and diffs, which issue none of these commands.
2. `canFetch`/`canPush`/`canPull` AND in `allowsRemoteActions(vcs:)`, so the actions disable with the
   reason in their `.help(...)`. The warning and the behaviour agree; nobody sees a warning *and* then
   the raw-stderr failure it was meant to prevent.

`.notInstalled` (exit 127) stays a **distinct** state from `.belowFloor` — different copy, and for git
it is effectively fatal. `.unknown` (probe timed out or output unparseable) is treated as **ok** —
never cry wolf, the same rule `classifyGitHubCLI` (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:425-444`) follows.

### New: `Views/VCSToolbar.swift`

```

private struct VCSToolbarDivider / VCSBranchSegment / VCSSyncSegment / VCSFetchSegment / VCSCountPill
extension View { func vcsToolbarSegment(hovering:) -> some View }

| Metric | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | 36 | 11pt title (13pt line) + 1 + 10pt caption (12pt line) = 26, + 5 top/bottom |
| `outerInset` / `innerInset` | 12 / 8 | 12 matches `SectionHeader`'s `.padding(.horizontal, 12)` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:534`) |
| `glyphSlot` / `glyphSpacing` | 12 / 7 | matches `SectionHeader`'s chevron frame + `HStack(spacing: 7)` (`:522,:528`) |
| `glyph` | 12 | between the inspector's 11 and the pane bar's 13 |
| `titleFont` / `captionFont` / `soloFont` | 11 semibold / 10 `fgDim` / 11 `fgMuted` | title matches the section header exactly |
| `fetchWidth` | 30 | 22pt well + 4 each side (`ToolbarIconButtonStyle` footprint) |
| branch min/max, `syncMinWidth` | 100 / 220, 126 | 100 + 126 + 30 + 2 = **258 ≤ 260**, so the minimum width fits by construction |

**Alignment by construction:** `outerInset 12` + `glyphSlot 12` + `glyphSpacing 7` puts the branch
glyph centre at x=18 and the name's left edge at x=31 — exactly where the Changes header's chevron
centre and title land. Assert the arithmetic; don't eyeball it.

**Background:** clear (inherit the card) + one 1pt `tokens.border` bottom hairline. The Changes header
below already fills `tokens.surface` (`InspectorSplitView.swift:512`); a second `surface` band above
merges into one 70pt grey block.

**Dividers:** `Rectangle().fill(tokens.border).frame(width: 1).frame(maxHeight: .infinity)` —
full-bleed, deliberately not `TitlebarDivider` (a 14pt inline group rule).

**Hover:** the whole divider-bounded cell fills with `tokens.hover`, opacity-only, `.easeOut(0.12)`,
gated on `accessibilityReduceMotion`. Animate opacity only — an implicit tree animation interpolates
the glyph's 1pt pixel re-round into a visible slide (`ToolbarIconButtonStyle.swift:40-52`).

**Segment 1 — branch (read-only, D14):** `arrow.triangle.branch` + `ViewThatFits` over
`[caption+name, name only]`, `.truncationMode(.middle)` on the name (its tail is what distinguishes
`joel/history-refs-pill` — `ChangesPanel.swift:686`). Click opens the existing ⌘O workroom picker. No
chevron — a disclosure glyph would promise a dropdown that no longer exists. `.contextMenu` offers
"Copy Branch Name". Do **not** add `.textSelection(.enabled)` — selectable text swallows real
mouseDown, so the segment would stop being clickable with a real mouse while synthetic XCUITest
clicks kept passing.

**Segment 2 — sync:** same shape, **inverted line order** (bold title over dim subtitle) per the
screenshot, plus trailing pill(s). Document the inversion: both blocks are 26pt and centred, so a
caption-first block sits low and a title-first block sits high, and the full-height divider is what
makes that read as two groups rather than a misalignment. A reviewer will flag it — pre-empt them.

**Segment 3 — fetch:** `arrow.down.circle`, **not** `arrow.clockwise` — the Changes header's Refresh
button is already `arrow.clockwise` (`ChangesPanel.swift:82`) 40pt below, and two circular-arrow
glyphs meaning different things is real confusion. In-flight ⇒ `ProgressView().controlSize(.mini)`
(`.small` is ~16pt and overflows the 12pt slot; `TerminalStatusBar.swift:234` sets the precedent).

**Theme:** the toolbar reads `ThemeService.shared.tokens`, which SwiftUI doesn't observe. Needs
`ActivityBar.swift:18`+`:47`'s pattern — `@State themeTick` + `.onReceive(.themeDidChange)`. Without
it a theme switch leaves the dividers stale.

**Timestamp ticks** via `TimelineView(.periodic(from: .now, by: 30))` wrapping *only* that `Text`,
calling the pure `fetchedAgo`. Redraws stay confined, it pauses off-screen, no `Timer` to leak.

`ViewThatFits` is new to this codebase (zero existing uses). The one trap: no variant may contain
`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`, or the first always "fits" and the ladder never fires.

### Degradation, 260 → 520pt

1. **Sync wins** — `layoutPriority(1)` vs branch `0`.
2. Truncate, never wrap; every `Text` is `.lineLimit(1)`.
3. **The staleness caveat outranks the count.** Reversed from the first draft: "Last fetched N ago"
   abbreviates ("Fetched 9 min. ago") but survives; the caveat must not be the first casualty while
   the unverified number it qualifies is pinned. (Finding 9 — folded as a strict improvement.)
4. Title abbreviates: "Pull origin with rebase" → "Pull with rebase" → "Pull".
5. The "Current Branch" caption drops below ~120pt of branch width. At 260pt it is not shown — the
   icon already says "branch", and it's the least useful pixel in the bar.
6. Sync glyph drops next; the pill's arrow carries direction.
7. Fixed 36pt height at every width. No reflow of the split view below.

## Failure modes

| Codepath | Realistic failure | Test? | Handled? | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rev-list` counterpart missing | No remote branch yet | ✅ integration | ✅ state 4 | "Publish branch" |
| `for-each-ref` on an old git | Unknown atom ⇒ atomic failure, no partial output | ✅ unit (D24 parse + floor) | ✅ D24 probe | Notification naming found vs required; actions disabled |
| `jj bookmark` on jj < 0.18 | Subcommand didn't exist (was `jj branch`) | ✅ unit (D24 floor) | ✅ D24 probe | jj-scoped warning; git projects unaffected |
| `jj` absent, git-only user | Nothing to warn about | ✅ unit | ✅ D24 (jj optional) | **Nothing** — no warning, no probe |
| `git` absent | Required tool missing; workroom creation already impossible | ✅ unit | ✅ D24 | Broken-install copy; all actions disabled |
| Version probe times out | Can't tell | ✅ unit | ✅ `.unknown` ⇒ treated as ok | Nothing — never cry wolf |
| ssh needs a passphrase, no agent | Prompt with nowhere to ask | ✅ unit (stdin EOF) | ✅ D5 `BatchMode` | Instant `.authRequired` |
| Agent socket invisible to the child | `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` unset in GUI env | ✅ unit (env forwarding) | ✅ D17 | Works; else actionable copy |
| Unknown host key | `BatchMode` hard-fails | ✅ unit (classify) | ✅ `.hostKeyUnverified` | "Connect once from a terminal" |
| Concurrent git writes, one `.git` | `packed-refs.lock` | ✅ gate test | ✅ D4 | Serialized; no wedge |
| Concurrent git write vs ungated *read* | Same lock, sweep side | ❌ | ⚠️ `.locked` + Retry | **Known gap — TODO filed** |
| `pull --rebase` SIGKILLed at 300s | `rebase-merge` left behind | ✅ integration | ✅ probe ⇒ `.rebaseInProgress` | "Abort rebase" button |
| jj pull conflicts, exit 0 | Success inferred wrongly | ✅ integration + model | ✅ D7 | Reported conflicted |
| jj op-log wording changes | Last-fetch label blanks | ✅ integration | ✅ degrades to `.unknown` | No timestamp, never a wrong one |
| Auto-fetch fails repeatedly | Silent network failures | ✅ model test | ✅ D16 no escalation | Tooltip only |
| Branch label read hits the provider | Thread-pool starvation | ✅ D10 counting stub | ✅ shared cache | — |

**Critical gaps: 0.** The review's one critical gap — an old `git`/`jj` degrading the whole feature to
raw stderr — is closed by D24's version floor, probe, notification and action-disabling. Every failure
mode above now has a test, error handling, and a message the user can act on.

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.
