# VCS toolbar: branch label + push/pull/fetch status

> Revised after `/plan-eng-review`. 7 review findings + 25 outside-voice findings folded across 17
> decisions (D3–D19). **Branch switching was cut (D14)**; two verified engine bugs were fixed
> (D13, D15). See the review report at the end.

## Context

The VCS inspector can only *read*. `VCSProviding` (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSProviding.swift:16`)
is a strictly read-only protocol — 8 members, no mutations, no network. There is **no** branch
listing, **no** fetch/push/pull, **no** ahead/behind counts, and **no** last-fetch time anywhere in
the app or the Rust core. The only branch name on screen is a `.caption` capsule in the Changes body
(`ChangesPanel.swift:669-730`) and one in the status bar (`TerminalStatusBar.swift:93-104`).

So a user in a workroom leaves the app for every remote interaction: they can see what changed but
not whether it's pushed, how far behind origin they are, or when they last fetched.

**Outcome:** a 3-segment toolbar at the top of the VCS inspector, shown only when the Changes
activity section is active. Current branch as a read-only label, a sync segment that reads
"Push origin / Last fetched 9 minutes ago" with an ahead/behind pill and performs the action on
click, and a fetch icon. Working for both git and jj.

**Cut during review (D14):** branch *switching*. Workrooms **are** branches — identity is the
directory basename (`internal/vcs/git.go:70-80`; no `branch` key in `internal/config/`) — so
switching a workroom's branch makes its name permanently wrong, and the jj path was reproduced
deleting a working-copy file and orphaning the workroom's commit. Segment 1's click opens the
existing ⌘O workroom picker instead. "New workroom from branch…" is filed as the product-correct
successor.

---

## Decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| D3 | Write ops go behind a **new** `VCSWriting` protocol + `VCS.writer(for:)`, conformed by a CLI-backed type holding the injected runner. `VCSProviding` untouched — reads stay structurally unable to mutate. Supersedes `TODOS.md:118`. |
| D4 | **git** write ops also route through `JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)`. Worktrees share one `.git`; a lock loss mid-`pull --rebase` wedges a workroom. Rename deferred. |
| D5 | `StatusCommandRunner` pins `stdin` to `/dev/null` and, for network ops, sets `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"` + `SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never`, clearing `SSH_ASKPASS`/`DISPLAY`. |
| D6 | Two ASCII diagrams, in this plan and mirrored as code comments. |
| D7 | The post-pull conflict determination lives in the **model**, after the gate releases — not in the writer. |
| D8 | One state struct. The mapper takes `(state, activity, failure, pullRebase, now)`. `VCSSyncSnapshot` deleted. |
| D9 | All four branch-name implementations unify onto **one shared cache**. |
| D10 | A counting stub asserts a branch-label read spawns **zero** VCS calls. |
| D11 | The UI-test fixture records requested actions; 4 flow tests assert the button→engine seam. |
| D12 | Remote-ref data is cached **per project root**, not per workroom. |
| D13 | Ahead/behind come from `git rev-list --left-right --count`. **`%(push:*)` is deleted** — see below. |
| D14 | **Switch cut.** Push + pull stay; pull gains a `rebase --abort` affordance. |
| D15 | A workroom reads the **shared** git dir's `FETCH_HEAD`, not its own. |
| D16 | **Auto-fetch on inspector focus**, interval-guarded. Knowingly supersedes `TODOS.md:324`. |
| D17 | Forward `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`/`SSH_AGENT_PID`/`GIT_SSH_COMMAND`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` from `ShellEnvironment.environment()` for network ops only. |
| D24 | **`git >= 2.41` is required; `jj >= 0.43` is optional but floor-checked when present.** Probed at app start; below floor ⇒ a persistent notification **and** remote actions disabled, scoped per project VCS. In scope, not a TODO. |

**Backend:** shell out to `git`/`jj` via `StatusCommandRunning`. Auth is the user's own agent and
credential helpers; the app already shells `gh`. SwiftGitX is unusable for this — `Repository+fetch.swift:30`
and `+push.swift:49` pass `NULL` for the options struct, so there is no credential path at all, and
`pull` doesn't exist. **Zero Rust/UniFFI changes; no `make app-vcs`.**

### Two bugs the review caught, both verified on git 2.55

**`%(push:track)` does not work for the branches this product creates.** Under `push.default=simple`
— git's built-in default — a branch with no upstream yields `PUSH=[]` and `PUSHT=[]`. Only `current`
and `matching` populate them. Every workroom is `git worktree add -b` (no upstream), so the headline
count would be blank on any machine not set to `current`. It looked fine only because this machine is
`current`. Measured:

```
push.default=simple    UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[]                PUSHT=[]
push.default=current   UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[origin/feat]     PUSHT=[[gone]]
push.default=upstream  UP=[] UPT=[] PUSH=[]                PUSHT=[]
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null (what the integration test does)  PUSH=[] PUSHT=[]
```

**`FETCH_HEAD` is per-worktree, so fetching at the root never writes the workroom's copy.**
`git rev-parse --git-path FETCH_HEAD` returns `.git/FETCH_HEAD` at the root but
`.git/worktrees/<n>/FETCH_HEAD` inside a workroom. The original plan fetched at the root *and* read
the per-worktree path — so every workroom would have read "never fetched" forever.

---

## Diagrams

### Operation routing (D6 — mirror above the writer's `opDirectory`)

```
                 ┌──────────────── every network op ────────────────┐
                 │ stdin=/dev/null · BatchMode=yes · askpass=never   │  D5
                 │ + SSH_AUTH_SOCK, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_CONFIG_*    │  D17
                 └──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                        │
              ┌─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐
              │   JJSnapshotGate.shared.run(projectRoot:)         │  D4 (git too)
              │   never re-enter for the same root  ── D7         │
              └─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                                        │
        git ────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────── jj
                                        │
  fetch   → PROJECT ROOT                │        fetch  → PROJECT ROOT
           (FETCH_HEAD is per-worktree; │                 (workspace has no .git)
            root = one shared answer)   │        push   → PROJECT ROOT
  push    → workroom                    │                 (bookmarks are repo-global)
  pull    → workroom (fetch step: root) │        pull    → root (fetch) + workroom (rebase)
                                        │
  READ (ungated, no lock):              │        READ (ungated, --ignore-working-copy):
   for-each-ref refs/remotes  ──┐       │         bookmark list --all-remotes  ──┐
   rev-list --left-right --count ┤ D13  │         (+ 2 revset counts if @        ┤
   stat <common-gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD ┘ D15│          is unbookmarked)              ┘
                                        │         op log → last fetch
```

### Sync-segment state precedence (D6 — mirror above `VCSSyncPresentation.make`)

Three orthogonal axes collapse to one order. Read top-down; first match wins.

```
  failure?  ──yes──►  [13] retry previous action        tone: failure
     │no
  in flight? ──yes──►  [10/11/12] Fetching…/Pushing…/Pulling…    disabled
     │no
  target valid? ──no──►  [1] no workroom  ·  [2] no repository    disabled
     │yes
  has remote? ──no───►  [3] "No remote configured"               disabled
     │yes
  upstream missing / gone? ──yes──►  [4] "Publish branch"   → push --set-upstream
     │no
  ahead>0 && behind>0 ──yes──►  [9] "Pull <remote> with rebase"  badge: M↓ then N↑
     │no                              (pull, NOT push — git refuses non-ff)
  behind>0 ──yes──►  [8] "Pull <remote> with rebase"             badge: M↓
     │no
  ahead>0  ──yes──►  [7] "Push <remote>"                         badge: N↑
     │no
  never fetched ──yes──►  [5] "Never fetched"          → fetch
     │no
                        [6] "Last fetched <rel>"       → fetch
```

`<remote>` is interpolated from `primaryRemote`, **never** the literal "origin" —
`remote.pushDefault` can make that wrong (verified: `-c remote.pushDefault=upstream` →
`PUSH=[upstream/feat]`).

---

## Engine

### New: `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/VCSWriting.swift`

A new protocol + one CLI-backed conformer + `VCS.writer(for:)`, alongside the existing
`VCS.provider(for:)` (`VCSProviding.swift:87`). This is the growth surface for the rest of Phase 2
(commit/amend, bookmark management, jj split/absorb/undo), which is why it's a protocol and not a
standalone resolver — but it is deliberately **separate** from `VCSProviding` so a read path cannot
reach a mutation.

```swift
protocol VCSWriting: Sendable {
  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
  func fetch(path:projectRoot:remote:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func push(path:projectRoot:current:remote:setUpstream:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func pullRebase(path:projectRoot:current:remote:tracking:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
  func abortRebase(path:projectRoot:) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult          // D14
}

enum VCS {
  /// Routes by `repoKind(at:)`, same as `provider(for:)`. Throws `.unsupportedRepo`.
  static func writer(for root: URL, projectRoot: URL,
                     runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner(),
                     makeProvider: @escaping @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
                       = { try VCS.provider(for: $0) }) throws -> VCSWriting
}
```

One conformer, `CLIVCSWriter`, holds the runner (the reason this can't go on `VCSProviding` —
`GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider` are stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere
to put it). It switches on repo kind internally and keeps all semantics in `static` pure
arg-builders/parsers/classifiers — the `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` testability pattern.

Timeouts: `refTimeout 5`, `fetch/push 120`, `pull 300`, gate `.shared`.
Reuse `WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening` (`:63`) verbatim on every git call. jj gets
`--color never --no-pager`; **reads** get `--ignore-working-copy`, **mutations must not**.

`currentRef` comes from `makeProvider(root).currentRef(root:)` — the app's existing canonical answer
including `.ancestor`/`.detached`. Do not re-derive it.

### git — reads

```
# 1. remote refs + the remotes list (no cap needed — the picker is gone)
git -c core.fsmonitor= for-each-ref --format='%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(symref)' refs/remotes

# 2. exact two-way divergence, config-independent  (D13)
git -c core.fsmonitor= rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>
```

- **Skip records with a non-empty `%(symref)`** — that's `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, whose short name
  is the bare remote. Its target also yields the default branch for free.
- `primaryRemote` = `origin` if present, else the first remote, else `nil`.
- The counterpart ref is `refs/remotes/<primaryRemote>/<current-branch>`, existence-checked against
  the list from (1). Absent ⇒ state 4 ("Publish branch"), no counts — this is the workroom default.
- `rev-list` runs only when the counterpart exists. Output is `<ahead>\t<behind>`.
- **`%(push:*)` and `%(upstream:*)` are not used for counts.** That also dissolves the "upstream is a
  local branch" case (measured: `UP=[main] UPT=[[ahead 3]] PUSH=[]`), because we only ever compare
  against `refs/remotes/`.

**Last fetch (D15):** mtime of `<common gitdir>/FETCH_HEAD`. Resolve purely — `.git` as a directory
⇒ `<path>/.git`; `.git` as a **file** ⇒ read it, strip `gitdir: `, then strip the trailing
`/worktrees/<name>` to reach the common dir. No subprocess. Unit-test all three shapes plus a
malformed pointer.

### git — actions

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `git … fetch <remote>` | **project root** |
| push | `git … push [--set-upstream] <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| pull | `git … fetch <remote>` (root), then `git … pull --rebase --autostash <remote> <branch>` | workroom |
| abort | `git … rebase --abort` | workroom |

No `--prune` (let `fetch.prune` decide), no `--no-write-fetch-head` (we need it), **never**
`--force`/`--force-with-lease`. `--set-upstream` only when there is no upstream yet. `--autostash` is
mandatory — workroom trees are always dirty.

### jj — reads

`jj bookmark list --all-remotes --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager -T '<template>'`,
NUL-separated: `name`, `remote`, `commit_id`, `present`, `conflict`, `tracked`,
`tracking_ahead_count`, `tracking_behind_count`. Verified on jj 0.43:

- The template keyword is **`self`**, not `ref`.
- The `self.remote() && self.tracked() && self.tracking_present()` guards are load-bearing — calling
  `tracking_*_count()` on a local ref renders the literal `<Error: Not a tracked remote ref>`.
- **Drop `remote == "git"`** — a colocated repo has that pseudo-remote and `--all-remotes` includes it.
- **jj's counts are inverted relative to git.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an `@origin` ref means the
  *remote* is ahead = git's **behind**. Swap on ingest, in one commented line, pinned by a
  cross-backend integration test.
- `present == 0` ⇒ `gone`. `tracked == 0` ⇒ `comparedTo` set, counts `nil`.
- Reads take no lock, so they stay ungated. Measured ~72ms on a 30-bookmark repo.

**Anonymous `@`** (`currentRef.kind == .ancestor` — the normal workroom state, since
`jj workspace add --name` creates no bookmark): the bookmark row's counts describe the *ancestor*, not
the user's work. Only then, two extra revset counts:

```
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r 'remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@' -T '"x\n"'   → ahead
jj log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy -r '@..remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)' -T '"x\n"'   → behind
```

`remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)..@` is exactly what bare `jj git push` sends, so the count and the
button agree by construction.

**Last fetch:** jj-lib 0.43 shells `git fetch … --no-write-fetch-head`
(`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:185`), so `FETCH_HEAD` is never written — confirmed
empirically. Scan the op log instead:

```
jj op log --no-graph --ignore-working-copy --color never --no-pager --limit 200
  -T 'self.time().end().format("%s") ++ "\x00" ++ self.description().first_line() ++ "\n"'
```

Newest-first; first line whose description starts with `fetch from git remote`. Fragile to a jj
rewording — mitigated by prefix matching, a graceful failure (one absent label, never a wrong one),
and an integration test that reddens on a jj bump.

### jj — actions (all inside the gate)

| Action | Command | Dir |
|---|---|---|
| fetch | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` | **project root** |
| push (bookmarked) | `jj git push --remote <r> --bookmark <name>` | **project root** |
| push (anonymous) | `jj git push --remote <r> --change <rev>` | **project root** |
| pull | `jj git fetch --remote <r>` (root), then `jj rebase -b @ -d <name>@<remote>` (workroom) | — |

- **`--change` is jj's built-in anonymous-branch push** (confirmed on 0.43): creates the bookmark,
  tracks it automatically, names it via `templates.git_push_bookmark` (default
  `"push-" ++ change_id.short()`). No hand-rolled naming policy.
- **Revision choice:** `@` if it has changes or a description, else `@-` — jj refuses to push a commit
  with an empty description, and a fresh `@` has neither. `WorkroomStatus.jjWorkingCopy`
  (`WorkroomStatus.swift:111`) already carries `description` + `files`, so this costs no process. Pure
  decision function; unit-test it.
- **Every `jj git …` subcommand takes the repo's git import/export lock** — even a read (`jj git remote
  list` fails with *"Failed to take lock for Git import/export"*). So derive the remote list from
  `bookmark list`'s `@<remote>` suffixes; never call `jj git remote list` on the read path.
- **`JJSnapshotGate`'s "never time the innermost call" rule is safe to relax for subprocesses** — it
  exists because `withTimeout` can't cancel jj-lib, but `StatusCommandRunner` SIGTERMs at `+timeout`
  and `killTree`s at `+timeout+2`, so the process is genuinely gone. Compose
  `gate.run { await runner.run(…, timeout:) }` with **no** outer `withTimeout`. Document this — it
  reads like a violation and isn't.
- **`jj rebase -b @`, not `-s @`** — `-b` moves the whole branch containing `@`, the pull-rebase shape.
  Run unconditionally; already-a-descendant prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
- **`jj rebase` exits 0 with conflicts.** Never infer success from the exit code — see D7.

### Models — appended to `Core/VCSModels.swift`

`VCSTracking { comparedTo, ahead: Int?, behind: Int?, gone }` — counts from the *local* ref's view;
`nil` means unanswerable, never zero.
`VCSLastFetch { at(Date), never, unknown }` — three-way, not `Date?`; `.unknown` must never render as
"never" (the `VCSPushState.unknown` rule).
`VCSRemoteState { current: VCSRef, tracking: VCSTracking?, remotes: [String], primaryRemote: String?, lastFetch: VCSLastFetch, resolvedAt: Date }`

**Cut by review:** `VCSBranchRef` and its `checkedOutIn`/`committedAt`/`isCurrent` (no picker — D14);
`refCap`/`refsTruncated`/`pickerOrder` (nothing enumerates 500 refs any more); `VCSTracking.pullFrom`,
`hasUnbookmarkedWork` (redundant with `current.kind == .ancestor`), per-row tracking, and
`VCSRemoteFailure.noUpstream`/`.alreadyCheckedOut` (D3, D14).

At the top of `VCSWriting.swift`: `VCSRemoteAction { fetch, push, pull, abortRebase }`,
`VCSRemoteFailure { toolMissing, timedOut, authRequired, hostKeyUnverified, noRemote, rejected, dirtyWorkingTree, rebaseInProgress, locked, other }`,
`VCSRemoteResolution { state, absent, keepPrior, failed }`,
`VCSRemoteActionResult { ok, failed }` — deliberately **not** folded into `VCSError`, which is the
backend-*read* taxonomy that `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)` (`:90`) switches over
exhaustively to pick a sidebar badge.

### Error classification

`static func classify(_ r: CommandResult, action:) -> VCSRemoteFailure?` — one pure function, `nil` on
success, matched against real git 2.55 / jj 0.43 strings:

| Signal | Failure |
|---|---|
| exit `CommandResult.commandNotFound` (127) | `.toolMissing` |
| `r.timedOut` | `.timedOut(action)` |
| `terminal prompts disabled` \| `could not read Username/Password` \| `Authentication failed` \| `Permission denied (publickey)` | `.authRequired` |
| `Host key verification failed` | `.hostKeyUnverified` |
| `local changes … would be overwritten` \| `untracked working tree files would be overwritten` | `.dirtyWorkingTree` |
| `does not appear to be a git repository` \| `No such remote` \| jj `No git remotes to fetch from` | `.noRemote` |
| `Updates were rejected` \| `! [rejected]` | `.rejected` |
| `.lock` + (`could not be obtained` \| `File exists`) \| jj `Failed to take lock for Git import/export` | `.locked` |
| pull failed **and** `<common gitdir>/worktrees/<n>/rebase-merge`\|`rebase-apply` exists | `.rebaseInProgress` |
| `!r.ok` otherwise | `.other` |

Copy that matters:
- `.authRequired` — *"Workroom never prompts for credentials. Load your key into ssh-agent, or
  configure a credential helper (`git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`)."* With D5 this
  fails instantly instead of hanging; with D17 agent users don't reach it at all.
- `.hostKeyUnverified` — *"`<host>` isn't in your known_hosts. Connect once from a terminal to accept
  its key."* `BatchMode=yes` makes this a hard failure rather than a stall.
- `.rebaseInProgress` — *"A rebase is in progress in this workroom."* Offers **Abort rebase**, never
  Retry (D14).
- `.rejected` — offers **Pull**, never Force.

### New: `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift` (D24)

Old tools were the review's one critical failure gap: `git for-each-ref` fails **atomically** on an
unknown atom (verified — `--format='%(bogusatom)'` produces `fatal: unknown field name`, no partial
output), and `jj bookmark` was `jj branch` before ~0.18 with `tracking_*_count()` newer still. The app
bundles neither binary — `ShellEnvironment.path()` takes whatever is on PATH. So one old tool turned
the whole feature into `.other` with raw stderr. Declaring a floor closes it.

**git is required; jj is optional.** Both are floor-checked when present, but they mean different
things: no `git` is a broken install (the Go CLI shells `git worktree add` to create a workroom at
all), whereas no `jj` is the normal state for a git-only user and must be silent.

```swift
enum VCSToolVersions {
  static let gitFloor = SemVer(2, 41, 0)   // jj-lib 0.43's own MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION
  static let jjFloor  = SemVer(0, 43, 0)   // the jj-lib the app links

  enum Status: Equatable, Sendable { case ok(SemVer), belowFloor(SemVer), notInstalled, unknown }
  struct Report: Equatable, Sendable {
    let git: Status            // required
    let jj: Status             // optional — `.notInstalled` is not a problem on its own
    /// Whether remote actions are permitted for a project of this VCS. git projects need only git;
    /// jj projects need both, since a colocated jj repo drives git underneath.
    func allowsRemoteActions(vcs: String) -> Bool
    /// Warnings to publish. Never includes jj `.notInstalled` unless a jj project is registered.
    func warnings(hasJJProject: Bool) -> [ToolWarning]
  }

  static func parseGit(_ stdout: String) -> SemVer?   // "git version 2.55.0" / Apple's "(Apple Git-154)"
  static func parseJJ(_ stdout: String) -> SemVer?    // "jj 0.43.0"
  static func probe(runner: StatusCommandRunning, probeJJ: Bool) async -> Report
}
```

**Why these numbers, not arbitrary ones:** git 2.41 is the floor **jj itself** enforces for its git
subprocess (`jj-lib-0.43.0/src/git_subprocess.rs:48` `MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION = "2.41.0"`), so it excludes
nobody a jj user isn't already excluded by; and jj 0.43 matches the jj-lib the Rust core links, which
matters because an older CLI may not understand the repo format that library writes. Both sit
comfortably above what the plan actually issues (`%(symref)` needs 2.8, `pull --autostash` needs 2.9).

**Scoping is per project VCS, not global.** A git project's toolbar must not be disabled because the
user's `jj` is old, and vice versa. Concretely:

| Condition | git project | jj project | Warning |
|---|---|---|---|
| git ok, jj ok | enabled | enabled | none |
| git ok, jj absent | enabled | actions disabled | only if a jj project is registered |
| git ok, jj below floor | enabled | actions disabled | yes, jj-specific |
| git below floor | actions disabled | actions disabled | yes, git-specific (jj drives git underneath) |
| git absent | actions disabled | actions disabled | yes — broken install; workroom creation is already impossible |

**When:** background, at app start, *after* `ShellEnvironment` sets the PATH floor
(`WorkroomApp.swift:23`) — the probe needs PATH to find the binaries at all. One `git --version` and,
only when a jj project is registered, one `jj --version`; 5s each, never blocking launch.

**Below floor ⇒ two consequences, kept in agreement:**
1. A persistent notification via the existing `NotificationCenterStore` (the left-sidebar list, issue
   #118) naming both the found and required versions. Non-modal — a too-old tool must never stop the
   app being useful for terminals and diffs, which issue none of these commands.
2. `canFetch`/`canPush`/`canPull` AND in `allowsRemoteActions(vcs:)`, so the actions disable with the
   reason in their `.help(...)`. The warning and the behaviour agree; nobody sees a warning *and* then
   the raw-stderr failure it was meant to prevent.

`.notInstalled` (exit 127) stays a **distinct** state from `.belowFloor` — different copy, and for git
it is effectively fatal. `.unknown` (probe timed out or output unparseable) is treated as **ok** —
never cry wolf, the same rule `classifyGitHubCLI` (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:425-444`) follows.

6. Fetch ⇒ "Fetching…" → "Last fetched just now".
7. Failure ⇒ inline error, still clickable.
8. Nothing selected ⇒ disabled.
9. Branch segment click opens the ⌘O workroom picker (D14).

**D11 — fixture records actions; 4 flow tests** asserting the button→engine seam:
ahead→push→counts clear; behind+dirty→confirm→pull; auth failure→inline error; second click while
in-flight is dropped.

**Out of XCUITest reach — say so in the file's doc comment:** hover wells and `.help` tooltips
(`.onHover` isn't driven by synthetic hover) and the `ViewThatFits` degradation at 260pt (a dropped
caption isn't in the a11y tree). Covered by the `titleVariants`-ordering and floor-sum unit tests.
Also per `nshostingview-no-a11y-children-in-unit-tests`: no in-gate render assertions — test the
decision, leave rendering to XCUITest. And per `focusedvalue-menu-enablement-refreshes-async-in-uitests`:
any menu-driven test must poll `isEnabled` with the menu open before sending the shortcut.

Scoped runs (`make app-uitest` ignores `APP_TEST_FLAGS`):
```bash
cd macapp && xcodebuild -project WorkroomApp.xcodeproj -scheme WorkroomAppUITests \
  -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData -destination 'platform=macOS' \
  -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/VCSToolbarUITests/testToolbarSitsAboveTheChangesHeader test
```

## What already exists (reused, not rebuilt)

| `WorkroomStatusResolver` | The writer's shape; `gitHardening:63` reused verbatim; `ghProbeDirectory:364` is the jj-root rule `opDirectory` generalises; `classifyGitHubCLI:425` is the tool-missing pattern |
| `HistoryModel` | `RemoteStateModel`'s exact shape — `State`/`isSettled`, the pre-dispatch debounce and *why*, `focus`/`activate`/`refresh`/`awaitCurrentLoad` |
| `JJSnapshotGate` | Per-project write serialization, now for git too (D4) |
| `rootBranchWatchers` + `handleRootBranchChange` | Already watches exactly the dirs that change on fetch/push. **Zero new watchers.** |
| `VCSProviding.currentRef` | The branch name incl. `.ancestor`/`.detached`. Not re-derived. |
| `StatusCommandRunner` + `ShellEnvironment` | Process execution, 3-layer timeout, PATH floor + probe; the probe supplies D17's auth vars |
| `OpenWorkroomDialog` | Segment 1's click target (D14) — already the correct "go work on that other thing" affordance |

| Deferred | Why |

| Rust / UniFFI changes | Everything is CLI-shaped. No `make app-vcs`. |

## Failure modes

| Codepath | Realistic failure | Test? | Handled? | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rev-list` counterpart missing | No remote branch yet | ✅ integration | ✅ state 4 | "Publish branch" |
| `for-each-ref` on an old git | Unknown atom ⇒ atomic failure, no partial output | ✅ unit (D24 parse + floor) | ✅ D24 probe | Notification naming found vs required; actions disabled |
| `jj bookmark` on jj < 0.18 | Subcommand didn't exist (was `jj branch`) | ✅ unit (D24 floor) | ✅ D24 probe | jj-scoped warning; git projects unaffected |
| `jj` absent, git-only user | Nothing to warn about | ✅ unit | ✅ D24 (jj optional) | **Nothing** — no warning, no probe |
| `git` absent | Required tool missing; workroom creation already impossible | ✅ unit | ✅ D24 | Broken-install copy; all actions disabled |
| Version probe times out | Can't tell | ✅ unit | ✅ `.unknown` ⇒ treated as ok | Nothing — never cry wolf |
| ssh needs a passphrase, no agent | Prompt with nowhere to ask | ✅ unit (stdin EOF) | ✅ D5 `BatchMode` | Instant `.authRequired` |
| Agent socket invisible to the child | `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` unset in GUI env | ✅ unit (env forwarding) | ✅ D17 | Works; else actionable copy |
| Unknown host key | `BatchMode` hard-fails | ✅ unit (classify) | ✅ `.hostKeyUnverified` | "Connect once from a terminal" |
| Concurrent git writes, one `.git` | `packed-refs.lock` | ✅ gate test | ✅ D4 | Serialized; no wedge |
| Concurrent git write vs ungated *read* | Same lock, sweep side | ❌ | ⚠️ `.locked` + Retry | **Known gap — TODO filed** |
| `pull --rebase` SIGKILLed at 300s | `rebase-merge` left behind | ✅ integration | ✅ probe ⇒ `.rebaseInProgress` | "Abort rebase" button |
| jj pull conflicts, exit 0 | Success inferred wrongly | ✅ integration + model | ✅ D7 | Reported conflicted |
| jj op-log wording changes | Last-fetch label blanks | ✅ integration | ✅ degrades to `.unknown` | No timestamp, never a wrong one |
| Auto-fetch fails repeatedly | Silent network failures | ✅ model test | ✅ D16 no escalation | Tooltip only |
| Branch label read hits the provider | Thread-pool starvation | ✅ D10 counting stub | ✅ shared cache | — |

**Critical gaps: 0.** The review's one critical gap — an old `git`/`jj` degrading the whole feature to
raw stderr — is closed by D24's version floor, probe, notification and action-disabling. Every failure
mode above now has a test, error handling, and a message the user can act on.

## Build order

Interleaved so no dead UI ships (finding 25).

1. Models into `VCSModels.swift`; the two ASCII diagrams as code comments (D6).
2. `Core/VCSWriting.swift` — protocol, `VCS.writer(for:)`, `CLIVCSWriter`, `opDirectory`, all pure
   parsers/arg-builders/`classify`, both backends' reads. **`VCSWritingTests` alongside** — every
   semantic lives here.
3. `StatusCommandRunner` hardening (D5, D17) + its tests. Do this *before* any network op exists.
   Then `Core/VCSToolVersions.swift` (D24) + its tests, wired into `WorkroomApp.swift` after the PATH
   floor — the floor check gates every action added later, so it must exist before they do.
4. `Core/VCSSyncPresentation.swift` + tests — the state machine is the risky part and is fully
   testable headless, before any view.
5. `Core/RemoteStateModel.swift` + tests, incl. the per-project cache and the D7 upgrade.
6. `AppStore` wiring: the D9 unified branch cache **first** (with `BranchLabelTests` + the D10
   counting stub green before anything else lands), then `remoteState`, the visibility gates, the
   `handleRootBranchChange` hook, the fixture seed.
7. `Views/VCSToolbar.swift` + the 4-line `ChangesPanel.swift` insertion — **with fetch working**, so
   segment 3 is live on arrival. Auto-fetch (D16) lands here.
8. Push, then pull (with the abort affordance). Each with its menu item, `isAppShortcut` edit, focused
   value, and its flow test (D11) in the same step.
9. Integration suite; then the TODOS.md edits (D18) and the four new entries (D19) — **plan mode
   blocked these, so they are implementation tasks, not done**.

`make app-*` needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`. No `make app-vcs` — zero Rust changes.

Then `make app-run` against this repo (git) **and** a throwaway colocated jj repo:
- **Set `git config push.default simple` first** — this machine is `current`, which is what hid the
  D13 bug. Counts must match `git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...@{push}` under both settings.
- Branch label matches `git branch --show-current`, and the sidebar, status bar and Changes capsule
  all agree with the toolbar.
- "Last fetched" matches `stat -f %Sm "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/FETCH_HEAD"`, updates after a
  terminal `git fetch` (proving the FSEvents path, not just our optimistic write), and is the **same
  value in every workroom of the project**.
- Auto-fetch fires on inspector focus once, then not again inside the interval.
- Push and pull work; failure copy is legible for: HTTPS with no helper, an unknown host key, and a
  diverged branch (push ⇒ `.rejected` ⇒ offered Pull).
- **jj:** an unbookmarked workroom `@` pushes via `--change` and creates a tracked `push-<id>`; a
  conflicting pull surfaces as conflicted rather than silently ok.
- Resize 260 → 520: the caption drops at 260, the staleness line survives longer than the pill, no
  horizontal scroll, fixed 36pt height.
- Hover and tooltips **with a real mouse** — synthetic hover lies in this codebase.
- **D24:** launch with PATH pointing at a git older than 2.41 and confirm the notification names found
  vs required and the actions disable with the reason in their tooltip. Then confirm a **git-only**
  machine with no `jj` installed produces **no warning at all** and spawns no `jj --version`; and that
  with a jj project registered but an old `jj`, a **git** project's toolbar stays fully enabled.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

## plugin:github:github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

content.text:
Verified from `desktop/desktop` @ `development` + `desktop/dugite` @ `master`.

## Desktop shells out. For everything.

App deps carry exactly two git-related packages:

```json
"desktop-trampoline": "file:../vendor/desktop-trampoline",
"dugite": "^3.2.2",
```

No `nodegit`, no libgit2, no `isomorphic-git`. `dugite` is a subprocess wrapper — its own README: *"using the same command line interface that core Git offers."* Every git op in Desktop goes through `exec` from dugite (`app/src/lib/git/core.ts`).

So the biggest git GUI shipping, built by GitHub, went CLI for the **whole** surface — not just the network half I was arguing for.

## It bundles its own git

`dugite` `postinstall: node ./script/download-git.js`, resolved at runtime via `LOCAL_GIT_DIRECTORY`, and it pins the plumbing around it:

```ts
env.set('GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM', path.join(gitDir, 'etc', 'gitconfig'))
env.set('GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR', templateDir)
env.set('GIT_SSL_CAINFO', sslCABundle)
```

That kills version drift dead — no floor check, no probe, no "your git is too old" notification. It's the direct answer to the caveat I raised last turn, and the one thing they do that we don't.

## Credentials: they register *as a git credential helper*

They didn't reimplement acquisition. They hooked git's own mechanism:

```ts
GIT_ASKPASS: '',
GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS: `${gitEnvConfigPrefix}'credential.helper=' 'credential.helper=desktop'`,
DESKTOP_PORT: await trampolineServer.getPort(),
DESKTOP_TRAMPOLINE_TOKEN: token,
```

Empty `credential.helper=` clears the user's helpers, then installs `desktop`. The `desktop-trampoline` binary git invokes calls back into the app over a local TCP port with a token, and the app answers from its OAuth accounts. Two details worth stealing the reasoning from:

- **Env var, not `-c`** — their comment: *"commands invoked by filters (i.e. Git LFS) to be able to pick up our configuration. Arguments passed to git commands are not passed down to filters."*
- **Askpass retired for the helper** — their comment: askpass returned empty strings, git authenticated *with* those and failed confusingly; the helper lets git say "couldn't read username, prompts disabled" instead.

And `useExternalCredentialHelperDefault = false` — they override your helpers by default, opt-in flag to use yours. They can, because they own an account. **We can't and shouldn't** — Workroom has no account, so the user's own helpers *are* the correct answer, and shelling out gets that for free with zero code. That's the whole argument in one line.

## Where they're looser than my recommendation

No locale pin anywhere in dugite's env setup — no `LC_ALL`, no `LANG`. Their error detection is a regex table over English stderr. Our `LC_ALL=C` is stricter than GitHub's own. So the "never parse prose" rule I stated is aspirational for them too; the difference is they bundle the git whose prose they're matching, and we don't.

## What this changes

**Nothing about the split, one thing about D24.** Desktop is strong evidence for CLI on network/credentials and no evidence against native local reads — they had no native option worth taking (nodegit/libgit2 in JS was the alternative they passed on). We already have typed jj-lib and SwiftGitX reads working; throwing those away to match Desktop's shape would be cargo-culting a constraint we don't have.

The genuinely interesting import is bundling git — it dissolves the whole `VCSToolVersions` floor/probe/notification apparatus. Cost is real: universal binary, notarization, ~40MB, and the Go CLI would want the same git for consistency. Worth filing, not worth doing now.

git add -A macapp && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
fix(macapp): close the four defects the VCS toolbar review found

Each was a real failure, not a style call.

**The dirty-tree confirmation only guarded one of two entry points.** The gate
lived in `VCSToolbar.perform`, but the Source Control menu calls
`performRemoteAction` directly — so the button warned before `--autostash`
stashed a dirty tree and ⌥⇧⌘P did it silently. Moved to
`AppStore.performRemoteAction`, which every caller funnels through.
`PendingVCSAction` moves to `VCSWriting.swift` and becomes store-owned
`@Published` state, so it also counts in `hasModalPresentation` (the shortcuts
go inert while the dialog is up) and clears when the selection changes. The
confirmed action runs via `runRemoteAction(_:on:)`, which verifies the `sid`:
the dialog is not modal to the sidebar, so re-deriving the target at click time
could pull a different workroom than the one the warning described.

**A completing action wrote its result onto whatever workroom was selected.**
`inFlight` is a model-wide lock — one action at a time, since the writer and
`JJSnapshotGate` are shared — but the toolbar renders per selection. So
switching workrooms mid-push showed "Pushing…" on a workroom that wasn't
pushing, and the push's failure landed on it too. `inFlightTarget` +
`activeAction` split "an action is running" from "an action is running *here*",
`finish` now guards its published writes with the same target check `apply`
has, and `handleRemoteMutation`/`noteConflictState` take the `sid` the action
ran in rather than reading back the current selection — which had a pull in one
workroom attributing the *next* workroom's conflict flag to itself.

**A non-English locale destroyed the whole failure taxonomy.** Every consumer
of `StatusCommandRunner` classifies failures by matching English substrings of
git's stderr, and git ships translated catalogs — Homebrew git 2.55 under
`fr_FR.UTF-8` answers `erreur : le spécificateur de chemin …`, so auth,
host-key, rejected-push, dirty-tree and leftover-lock all collapsed to
`.other(rawStderr)` with no recovery offered. Pins `LC_ALL=C`, not
`LC_MESSAGES`: the env is seeded from `ProcessInfo.environment`, so an
inherited `LC_ALL` outranks the narrower variable and silently defeats it
(measured). Verified that `LC_ALL=C` renders `café-ünï.txt` byte-identically —
git writes pathnames as raw bytes regardless of locale.

**`Defaults[.vcsLastFetch]` leaked on project removal.** Keyed by project root
path in a persisted dictionary with no other pruning, so an entry survived the
life of the install and a re-add of the same path inherited a stale "last
fetched". Pruned alongside the branch labels.

Also drops dead code the review surfaced (`VCSRemoteAction.touchesNetwork`,
`VCSTracking.isInSync`/`.isDiverged`, `FixtureVCSWriter.requested`) and names
the pill arrow's magic 7 as `VCSToolbarMetrics.pillArrowGlyph`.

Tests: 4 stale-target cases in `RemoteStateModelTests`, 5 confirmation-gate
cases in `VCSRemoteTriggerTests` — including that the menu path confirms.

content.text:
Verified. "Own account" is literal — Desktop is a GitHub client that signs you in and keeps its own credential store.

## The GitHub path

OAuth, browser flow, three scopes:

```ts
const oauthScopes = ['repo', 'user', 'workflow']
```

Token goes in the OS keychain via `TokenStore`, keyed per endpoint:

```ts
export function getKeyForEndpoint(endpoint: string): string {
  const appName = __DEV__ ? 'GitHub Desktop Dev' : 'GitHub'
  return `${appName} - ${endpoint}`
}
```

When git asks the trampoline for credentials, Desktop picks which signed-in account by **URL origin match**:

```ts
return accounts.find(
  a => new URL(getHTMLURL(a.endpoint)).origin === parsedUrl.origin
)
```

Covers github.com and any GitHub Enterprise Server you've added. Your `credential.helper` never enters it — remember they blank it first (`'credential.helper=' 'credential.helper=desktop'`).

## The part that matters for us: the *non*-GitHub path

Origin match fails for GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted, anything. So Desktop had to become a **general-purpose credential store** — `generic-git-auth.ts`:

```ts
export const genericGitAuthUsernameKeyPrefix = 'genericGitAuth/username/'
export function setGenericCredential(endpoint, username, password) {
  setGenericUsername(endpoint, username)      // localStorage
  return setGenericPassword(endpoint, username, password)  // keychain
}
```

Username in `localStorage`, password in the keychain, its own prompt UI, its own invalidation. A second credential store running parallel to git's, for hosts they know nothing about. And the code carries the scars — `memoizeOne` because git asks username-then-password and they didn't want two keychain round-trips, `hasRejectedCredentialsForEndpoint` bookkeeping per trampoline token, and the whole askpass→credential-helper migration whose comment explains askpass returned empty strings that git then tried to *authenticate with*.

Tell too: the escape hatch exists but is off.

```ts
export const useExternalCredentialHelperDefault = false
```

They ship a flag to defer to your real helpers, defaulted off. That flag's existence is them walking back toward what shelling out gives for free.

## Why Workroom shouldn't have one

Desktop pays that cost because *being the GitHub client is the product* — accounts, PR list, sign-in state, GHES support. Workroom's product is workrooms. If we shelled out and let git use the user's own helpers, we get:

- every host on day one, including ones we've never heard of
- osxkeychain, GCM, `credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential`, corporate custom helpers — all free
- identical credentials to the user's terminal, which is the compatibility property you named
- zero keychain writes, zero prompt UI, zero invalidation logic, zero OAuth client secret to ship

What we give up: no "signed in as X", and a user with HTTPS and no helper configured gets a hard `.authRequired` instead of a sign-in sheet. Our copy already tells them to run `git config --global credential.helper osxkeychain`. Fair trade — and note we're already consistent here, since the PR status shells `gh` and rides `gh`'s token rather than minting our own.

Four buckets. Ordered by what I'd actually do.

## Do now — cheap, all correctness

1. **Write the split into `TODOS.md` Phase 2.** It currently says only "add them as `VCSWriting` members". Should say: local ops native (libgit2/jj-lib), network ops CLI, **and "Workroom does not store credentials" as a stated non-goal** — otherwise a future session adds a sign-in sheet, which is precisely the Desktop cost we're declining. That non-goal is the load-bearing half; without it the split reads as a preference instead of a boundary.

2. **Quote the remote name in the jj revsets.** `jjAheadRevset`/`jjBehindRevset` interpolate it bare into `remote_bookmarks(remote=<r>)`. A remote with a quote or revset metacharacter breaks the expression. Left over from the review, one-line fix, real.

3. **`git push --porcelain`.** `.rejected` currently keys off `! [rejected]` — English. Porcelain gives a locale-independent per-ref flag column plus the nonzero exit, which decides rejected-vs-ok without prose. Worth verifying the flag column covers all our reject cases before ripping the string match out.

`LC_ALL=C` stays load-bearing regardless — fetch has no porcelain mode, so auth/host-key/lock stay prose-matched forever.

## Then

4. **Fold `commonGitDir`/`worktreeGitDir`.** ~14 duplicated lines from the review. Mechanical.

5. **Test the `.keepPrior` timeout path.** The only branch of the resolution enum with no coverage.

6. **Finish manual QA** — resize 260→520, real-mouse hover, live `.authRequired`. Still outstanding, and two of the three can't be automated in this codebase (synthetic hover lies; `.onHover` isn't drivable). Blocked on the windowless-launch degradation, so it wants a log out/in first.

## File, don't build

**Bundling git.** Desktop's `dugite` downloads its own build and pins `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`/`GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR`/`GIT_SSL_CAINFO` around it. That deletes all of `VCSToolVersions` — floor, probe, notification, per-VCS scoping. Tempting, and wrong now: universal binary, notarization, ~40MB, and the Go CLI would want the same binary for consistency. File it as the thing to revisit if the version floor ever actually bites a user.

## Won't do — worth stating so it doesn't get re-litigated

**A credential trampoline.** Desktop needs one because it's the GitHub client; the fallout is `generic-git-auth.ts` — a parallel credential store, with prompt UI and invalidation, for hosts they know nothing about. We get every host free by shelling out, and their own `useExternalCredentialHelperDefault` flag is them reaching back toward that.

**Native fetch/push.** SwiftGitX passes `nil` options and has `// TODO: Implement pull`; libgit2 reads no `credential.helper` key. Settled.

Want me to take 1–3? Roughly one pass, all three testable.

## P2 — perf, correctness, and the next VCS phase

### VCS write actions — Phase 2 (macapp) — roadmap pointer

**What:** The next VCS phase: turn the read-only foundation into a full in-app VCS UI. **Fetch, push
and pull-with-rebase have SHIPPED** (the VCS toolbar). What remains: commit/amend, bookmark (jj) /
branch (git) management, and the deep jj ops (undo/op-log, split, absorb, evolog, interdiff).

**Where the write seam actually is — this changed.** The original plan put write methods on
`VCSProviding` with a `CLIVCSProvider` fallback. That is **not** what shipped, and new work should not
follow it. Writes live behind a **separate** `VCSWriting` protocol (`Core/VCSWriting.swift`) with its
own factory `VCS.writer(for:)`, conformed by `CLIVCSWriter`. Two reasons, both load-bearing:

- `VCSProviding`'s doc calls it "the single seam the app **reads** VCS data through", and four
  resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no gate. A `fetch` on that protocol means
  nothing structurally stops a read path firing a network mutation — the opposite of what
  `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee.
- A CLI-backed method needs an injected `StatusCommandRunning`, and `GitProvider`/`RustJJProvider` are
  stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one. A new conformer has
  somewhere.

So: add commit/amend and the rest as `VCSWriting` members, and they inherit the gate, the network
environment hardening and the failure taxonomy for free.

**Why:** This is a roadmap phase, not a tactical follow-up. The authoritative scope + sequencing live
in the issue #59 plan; this entry is the pointer that makes it discoverable.

**How to start:** Read `Core/VCSWriting.swift` — its doc comment carries the routing diagram, the
per-backend command table and the placement rules (fetch always runs at the project root, for both
backends; jj push too, because bookmarks are repo-global). The read layer blocks nothing. What's left
of the error taxonomy is one-sided (git still flattens to `.io`), and the stale-working-copy **repair**
is itself a write, so it belongs to this phase.

**Depends on:** the VCS read foundation (shipped, Phase 1) and the write seam (shipped with the
toolbar). Spans `Core/VCSWriting.swift`, possibly `vcs/` (Rust) + `WrVcs` UniFFI for native jj ops, and
new write-flow UI.

**Priority:** P2 (the product direction; large — see the plan for the real breakdown).

# macapp/CLAUDE.md

The Workroom macOS app: a SwiftUI (macOS 15+) front-end that bundles the `workroom`
Go binary and drives it over the CLI's `--json` contract. See README.md for full
architecture, signing, and notarization detail — this file is the quick reference.

## Dev tasks (Makefile)

Every dev task runs through the **repo-root `Makefile`**, namespaced `app-*` (run from the repo
root, not `macapp/`):

```bash
make app-run        # canonical local loop: xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug) → relaunch
make app-build      # xcodegen → xcodebuild (Debug)
make app-test       # xcodebuild test (WorkroomAppTests) — parallel; APP_TEST_FLAGS= to serialize
make app-generate   # force-regenerate the (gitignored) .xcodeproj from project.yml
make app-vcs        # build the Rust VCS core → WrVcs SwiftPM package (auto-run before app builds)
make app-format     # swift-format, rewrite sources in place
make app-lint       # swift-format --strict (non-zero on any violation — the hard gate)
make app-release    # Release build → notarize → staple → DMG installer (Scripts/release.sh)
make app-icon       # regenerate AppIcon PNGs (Scripts/make-icon.swift)
make app-clean      # remove DerivedData + .xcodeproj
```

Builds reuse `macapp/DerivedData/` so the Swift packages (incl. the GhosttyKit xcframework)
aren't re-resolved/re-downloaded every build. (`cli-*` targets cover the Go CLI — see the root
CLAUDE.md.)

## VCS core (Rust jj + SwiftGitX git)

Workroom reads VCS data through **two backends behind one Swift layer** (the app is growing into a
VCS-first IDE — issue #59 is the first brick):

- **jj → Rust `jj-lib` via UniFFI.** The `vcs/` Rust workspace (jj-only) builds a static xcframework
  + generated Swift into the local SwiftPM package `vcs/swift/WrVcs` — the app does `import WrVcs`.
- **git → SwiftGitX (libgit2), pure Swift.** git has a mature native Swift path; jj has none — so
  only jj needs the Rust/UniFFI bridge. (An all-Rust core with gix was tried and dropped: gix bought
  no real unification and libgit2 is the more complete git engine.)

**Three reads reach past SwiftGitX**, all linking the `libgit2` C API **directly** (its own SPM package
in `project.yml`, URL + version identical to SwiftGitX's own dependency so SwiftPM sees one package
identity). `Core/LibGit2.swift` owns the single `git_libgit2_init` and hands out raw `git_repository`
handles (SwiftGitX inits inside `Repository.open`, which a direct C caller can't rely on); these four
files are the only ones in the app touching raw libgit2:

- **Push state — `Core/GitGraph.swift`.** SwiftGitX cannot express a commit *range*: its
  `CommitSequence` only calls `git_revwalk_push`, never `git_revwalk_hide`, it exposes no
  merge-base/graph helper, and its repository pointer is `internal` — so "which commits aren't on
  `origin` yet" (`HEAD --not refs/remotes/origin/*`) needs the C API. The jj side answers the same
  question natively with one `ancestors(<tracked @origin tips>)` revset. Push state is
  **origin-scoped** and any unreadable ref degrades the WHOLE page to "unknown" (no badge) rather than
  a partial answer.
- **Commit diffs — `Core/GitCommitDiff.swift`.** Rename detection is `git_diff_find_similar` run over a
  live `git_diff`, and a SwiftGitX `Diff` materializes its deltas/patches in an `internal` init and
  frees the `git_diff` before returning, so there's nothing left to detect on. Without it a committed
  rename read as delete + add while `git show` showed one rename row (git defaults to
  `diff.renames=true`), and a root commit's diff came back empty (SwiftGitX diffs it against itself).
  Detection options are NULL, which is what makes libgit2 read the repo's own `diff.renames` /
  `diff.renamelimit` — naming a flag explicitly suppresses that config read, so a repo set to
  `diff.renames=false` or `=copies` would silently disagree with its own CLI. Typechanges are included
  (`GIT_DIFF_INCLUDE_TYPECHANGE`); without it libgit2 splits a file↔symlink change into delete + add
  on the SAME path, giving the file list two rows with one `id`. `GitProvider.changeset`/`.fileDiff`
  both read through it, so the History file list and the patch text can't disagree.
- **Working-tree ± line counts — `Core/GitDiffStats.swift`**, via `git_diff_get_stats`. SwiftGitX
  surfaces no diffstat, and its `Diff` is **eager**: `Diff.init` builds a `Patch` per delta and
  materializes every hunk line into a Swift `String` before the caller sees it. Summing those for the
  badge cost one `String` per changed line of the whole worktree on **every** status refresh, so the
  counts moved to libgit2, which counts in C and allocates nothing Swift-side. The diff itself is
  irreducible — that's what `git diff --shortstat` costs too. With `changeset` now counting through
  `GitCommitDiff`, **no** `+N −M` in the app is summed off SwiftGitX hunk lines any more, which also
  ends a real bug: that sum counted the EOFNL markers (`\ No newline at end of file`) as lines, so
  changing only a file's trailing newline reported two deletions where git reports `1 insertion(+),
  1 deletion(-)`. libgit2 skips them, as `git diff --shortstat`/`--numstat` do. It runs
  `git_diff_find_similar` too, for the same reason `GitCommitDiff` does: the file list beside these
  counts already pairs renames (libgit2 status' `.renamesIndex`/`.renamesWorkingTree`), so without it
  a staged rename rendered as one "renamed" row badged `+N −N` while `git diff HEAD --shortstat`
  reported `0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)`.

**Read surface & routing.** `Core/VCSProviding.swift` is the one Swift protocol; `VCS.provider(for:)`
routes by repo kind. `RustJJProvider` maps `WrVcs.*` → app-native models, `GitProvider` wraps
SwiftGitX. `WorkroomStatusResolver` and `BranchResolver` read through this layer — **the jj CLI
parsers are gone** (log/changeset/currentRef/workingStatus are all native jj-lib).

**The one mutating read: `RustJJProvider.workingStatus`.** jj's working copy is itself a commit, so
on-disk edits don't exist to jj-lib until snapshotted — a working-copy status read therefore *must*
snapshot `@` first: it takes the working-copy lock and rewrites `@` (modeled on jayjay's
`refresh_working_copy`). Everything else (log/changeset/currentRef) is a read-only `load_at_head`
with no lock. Because it mutates, **only test snapshot changes on throwaway repos** (corruption
risk). Line counts come from the SAME native read — `changed_files` materializes each changed file's
two sides and counts them, so `resolveJJ` fires no `jj diff --stat` process (it used to; see
`40456bae`). Oversized and binary files report no count rather than being read whole. Cargo coverage:
`vcs/crates/wr-vcs-core/tests/working_status.rs` + `line_stats.rs`; Swift coverage:
`WorkroomStatusIntegrationTests.testJJ*`.

`make app-vcs` (→ `vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh`) builds the Rust artifacts and **runs automatically
before `app-build`/`app-test`/`app-generate`** (a Makefile prerequisite). Requirements:

- **`protoc`** on PATH (`brew install protobuf`) — a build-time dep of jj-lib.
- arm64 by default; **`make app-release` builds universal** (`VCS_APPLE_FLAGS=--universal`), which
  needs **rustup `stable` ≥ 1.93** + `rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin aarch64-apple-darwin`
  (Homebrew's rust can't cross-compile; the script preflights this and errors clearly).
- **Unchanged inputs are a no-op.** The script hashes the Rust sources, manifests/lockfile, itself,
  `rustc --version` and the arch flavour into `vcs/swift/WrVcs/Frameworks/.build-stamp`, and exits
  early when that matches and the outputs exist. `WR_VCS_FORCE=1 make app-vcs` rebuilds regardless.
  CI leans on this: it caches the *outputs* keyed on the same inputs, so a commit that doesn't touch
  `vcs/` skips the ~4-minute crate-graph build (and `make app-test`'s own `app-vcs` prerequisite
  stays free).
- **Xcode-driven builds are gated, not auto-fixed.** ⌘R/⌘U (and a raw `xcodebuild`) skip the
  Makefile, so they'd otherwise link the last-built core. A `Rust VCS core up to date` pre-build
  phase runs `build-apple.sh --check` and **fails the build** with `run 'make app-vcs'` when the
  stamp doesn't match `vcs/`. It can't rebuild for you: SPM extracts the binaryTarget's xcframework
  before target build phases run, so a fresh `.a` wouldn't reach that build's link. Silently linking
  a stale core cost a debugging session once — conflicted files read as `.modified` because the
  linked core predated a merged per-file-conflict fix.

The xcframework + generated Swift are **gitignored and regenerated**; only `Package.swift` + a
`shim.c` are tracked. Packaging note: the xcframework is **library-only** (no headers) and the FFI
Clang module (`wr_vcs_uniffiFFI`) is a separate SPM C target — a headers-bearing static xcframework
copies its `module.modulemap` into the shared `Debug/include/` and collides with GhosttyKit's
("Multiple commands produce include/module.modulemap").

## Formatting & linting

Swift is formatted/linted with **swift-format** (bundled with the Xcode toolchain — run via
`xcrun swift-format`, no install). Config `macapp/.swift-format` (2-space, 100 cols) covers
`WorkroomApp/` + `WorkroomAppTests/` only (not the `Scripts/*.swift` tools). Use `make app-format`
/ `make app-lint`. Every Xcode/`xcodebuild` build also runs a `swift-format lint` pre-build phase
that surfaces violations as **warnings** (non-fatal — `make app-lint` is the hard gate). Run
`make app-format` before committing.

## Gotchas

- **The Swift module is `Workroom`** (the target is `WorkroomApp`; `PRODUCT_MODULE_NAME` is pinned
  to `Workroom` in `project.yml`). Tests use `@testable import Workroom`. The pin matters because
  `PRODUCT_NAME` is **per-config**: `Workroom` for Release, `Workroom Dev` for Debug (see below) —
  without the pin the Debug module would become `Workroom_Dev` and break the import. A test
  target's `TEST_HOST` must point at the Debug product (`Workroom Dev.app/Contents/MacOS/Workroom
  Dev`); XcodeGen's auto-derived (target-name-based) host is wrong and fails with "Could not find
  test host".
- **Debug builds run side by side with the release build.** The Debug config has a distinct
  identity — bundle id `com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev`, product/display name `Workroom Dev`,
  and the amber `AppIcon-Dev` icon set — so a local build doesn't fight the installed release
  `Workroom` for activation, the key window, preferences (separate UserDefaults domain via the
  bundle id), or the system-wide ⌘§ hotkey. The Debug build deliberately **doesn't register ⌘§**
  and **doesn't run Sparkle scheduled checks** (`#if DEBUG` in `WorkroomApp.swift` / `Updater.swift`)
  so it can't grab the global hotkey or try to "update" itself to the release DMG. Both builds
  still share the CLI config at `~/.config/workroom/config.json` (the bundled CLI has no
  config-path override), so they show the same projects/workrooms. `make app-run` only kills the
  `Workroom Dev` instance, never your release build. The two app icons (`make app-icon` renders
  both) are identical except for the tile gradient.
- **Adding/removing/renaming a `.swift` file needs an `xcodegen generate`.** XcodeGen
  expands the source glob into explicit file refs in the (gitignored) `.xcodeproj`, so
  the change is invisible (or, for a deleted/renamed file, a hard "Build input file
  cannot be found" error) until the project is regenerated. The `make app-*` build
  targets now run `xcodegen generate` every time, so this is handled automatically —
  it only bites when building from Xcode directly (regenerate, or run `make app-generate`).
- **SourceKit "Cannot find type X in scope" is usually noise.** The single-file indexer
  doesn't see sibling files; a clean `xcodebuild` is authoritative.
- **The terminal is libghostty** (`libghostty-spm`'s `GhosttyKit` xcframework, pinned
  `exactVersion: 1.2.3` in project.yml). The embedding C API is not yet stable, so pin EXACT —
  don't float it. The terminal surface (`Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`) + runtime
  (`GhosttyApp`/`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter`) are ours; the bundled `Resources/ghostty` (terminfo +
  shell-integration) must ship for the engine to start. Pre-GA, the plan is to move to a
  self-built xcframework from a pinned Ghostty fork.
- **The child environment has two layers, and only one of them is reliable** (`Core/ShellEnvironment.swift`).
  A Finder-launched `.app` gets a minimal PATH, so: the **floor** (`floorPath()`) reads `/etc/paths`
  + `/etc/paths.d/*` — `path_helper`'s own inputs — with no shell at all, and that alone resolves
  Postgres.app's `psql`; the **probe** (`refresh()`) then runs one `$SHELL -ilc` for what only an
  interactive login shell knows (`.zshrc` PATH entries, mise shims). The probe is best-effort by
  design: its failures degrade to the floor, so a `.zshrc` that ends `exec tmux` costs enrichment
  and never the bug. Three traps worth knowing: **`path_helper` APPENDS** the PATH it's handed, so
  the probe must be spawned with a *cleared* `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin` or Homebrew ends
  up at the tail; the payload is a **raw `env -0` stream between UUID markers** because command
  substitution strips NULs and the user's `base64` may be GNU's (wraps at 76 cols); and the deadline
  is a `DispatchWorkItem` **inside** the blocking closure, because `withTimeout` cannot cancel a
  `runBlocking` call and would leak a shell per invocation. `setenv("PATH", …)` happens exactly once,
  in `WorkroomApp.init` — a later write would race the status sweep's `ProcessInfo.environment`
  reads. Everything else reads `ShellEnvironment.path()` (PATH only, for the automatic sweep) or
  `.environment()` (the full environment, for setup/teardown scripts).
- **Menu enable/disable must flow through `focusedSceneValue` + `@FocusedValue`**
  (see `WorkroomApp.swift`); a `Commands` body does not re-evaluate when the shared
  `AppStore` mutates. ⌘1–9 are handled by an `NSEvent` local monitor in `AppDelegate`,
  not menu items, so they fire before the terminal swallows the keys.

## Layout

**VCS info that only the GUI needs** (e.g. the sidebar root row's current branch/bookmark)
is resolved app-side in `Core/BranchResolver.swift` (per project, async, with a per-call
timeout) — deliberately NOT added to the `workroom --json` contract, which the human CLI
never shows.

`WorkroomApp/Core/` — store, CLI wrapper, terminal sessions, models, theme.
`WorkroomApp/Views/` — `NavigationSplitView` tree sidebar + terminal detail.
`Scripts/` — `run.sh` (local), `build-helper.sh` (embeds+signs the Go binary), `release.sh`
(build → notarize → staple → DMG → EdDSA-sign for Sparkle), `appcast.sh` (publishes the Sparkle
appcast to the fixed `appcast` release), `appcast-notes.sh` (re-renders a published item's
`<description>` from the current release body — see "Auto-update" below), `make-icon.swift`
(regenerates the `AppIcon` PNGs in `Assets.xcassets` — run `swift Scripts/make-icon.swift`).

## Auto-update (Sparkle)

`Core/Updater.swift` wraps Sparkle's `SPUStandardUpdaterController` (the "Check for Updates…"
menu item + the Settings toggle bind to it). The `SU*` keys in `project.yml` (`SUFeedURL`,
`SUPublicEDKey`, `SUEnableAutomaticChecks`) configure it. **Versioning is tag-driven** —
`CFBundleShortVersionString`/`CFBundleVersion` resolve from `$(MARKETING_VERSION)`/
`$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`, which `release.sh` injects from the git tag (build number =
commit count, so it only ever increases — Sparkle compares it). The appcast feed is an asset
on the fixed `appcast` GitHub release. See `README.md` ("Auto-update") for the one-time keypair
setup and the `SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY` secret.

**Release channels (issue #91) — two build identities.** The **main** app (`Release` config)
switches `stable`⟷`pre` at runtime via the *Settings ▸ General ▸ Release channel* picker
(`ReleaseChannel.pickerCases` = stable/pre only). **Workroom Nightly** is a separate side-by-side
product — the `Nightly` build config in `project.yml` (bundle id `…workroom.nightly`, name, violet
`AppIcon-Nightly`, `WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL=nightly` → the `WorkroomReleaseChannel` Info.plist
marker read by `ReleaseChannel.current`/`isNightlyBuild`), extending the Debug/"Workroom Dev"
per-config identity pattern to a third identity.

`Updater.allowedChannels(for:)` returns `{nightly}` on the nightly build and the picked stable/pre
floor otherwise; one appcast feed carries all channels (`Scripts/appcast.sh` tags items via the
shared `Scripts/channel-helper.sh`; stable stays untagged = Sparkle default), and Sparkle's
bundle-id check stops either identity installing the other's DMG. Nightly is a single **rolling**
item; appcast idempotency keys on `(channel, build)`. `build-helper.sh` bakes both
`-X main.version=$(MARKETING_VERSION)` and `-X main.channel=$(WORKROOM_RELEASE_CHANNEL)` into the
bundled CLI, and `CommandLineInstaller` symlinks it as `workroom` (main) or `workroom-nightly`
(nightly build) so both coexist in PATH. `Updater.migrateReleaseChannelIfNeeded` opts an upgrading
beta user into `pre` and coerces a legacy `.nightly` selection to `.stable` (main build only).

**Release-notes in the update dialog.** Sparkle's dialog renders the appcast item's
`<description>`. `appcast.sh` (run during the release) embeds the GitHub release body as that
description — but at release time the body is still goreleaser's raw commit list, since the
curated notes are written afterwards. So a second path keeps them in sync: the
`.github/workflows/appcast-notes.yml` workflow fires on every `release: edited` event and runs
`Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`, which re-renders the matching item's `<description>` from the
release's *current* body. Curating a release's notes therefore auto-refreshes what the update
dialog shows; no rebuild needed. To fix an already-published feed by hand, run it directly:
`TAG=vX.Y.Z REPO=owner/repo GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) macapp/Scripts/appcast-notes.sh`.

mkdir -p "$P"

$G config user.email t@t; $G config user.name t

#!/bin/zsh
# Fresh pair, guaranteed non-fast-forward, tested under two locales.
G=/opt/homebrew/bin/git
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null
P="$1"; mkdir -p "$P"; cd "$P"
$G init -q --bare o.git
$G init -q a; cd a; $G config user.email t@t; $G config user.name t
echo 1 > f; $G add f; $G commit -qm 1; $G remote add origin ../o.git; $G push -q origin master
cd "$P"; $G clone -q o.git b; cd b; $G config user.email t@t; $G config user.name t
echo 2 > g; $G add g; $G commit -qm 2; $G push -q origin master     # origin now ahead of a
cd "$P/a"; echo 3 > h; $G add h; $G commit -qm 3                    # a diverges

for LOC in C fr_FR.UTF-8; do
  echo "######## LC_ALL=$LOC"
  echo "-- porcelain STDOUT:"
  LC_ALL=$LOC $G push --porcelain origin master 2>/dev/null
  echo "   EXIT=$?"
  echo "-- porcelain STDERR:"
  LC_ALL=$LOC $G push --porcelain origin master 2>&1 >/dev/null
  echo "-- plain (no porcelain) STDERR:"
  LC_ALL=$LOC $G push origin master 2>&1 >/dev/null
done

input.old_string:
So: add commit/amend and the rest as `VCSWriting` members, and they inherit the gate, the network
environment hardening and the failure taxonomy for free.
input.new_string:
So: add commit/amend and the rest as `VCSWriting` members, and they inherit the gate, the network
environment hardening and the failure taxonomy for free.

**Which backend each op uses — decided, don't re-litigate.** `VCSWriting` says *where* writes live,
not *how* they run. The split:

| Ops | Backend | Why |
|---|---|---|
| commit/amend, branch + bookmark management, jj undo/op-log/split/absorb/evolog | **native** (libgit2/SwiftGitX, jj-lib) | Local. Typed APIs, no output to parse, no tool-version floor, no locale exposure. This is where every remaining Phase-2 feature lands, so the CLI surface **stops growing here.** |
| fetch, push, pull | **CLI** — permanently, not a stopgap | Three independent blockers, all verified from checked-out sources: SwiftGitX passes NULL options (`git_remote_fetch(remotePointer, nil, nil, nil)`, and `pull` is a `// TODO`), so it has no credential callback at all; **libgit2 implements no `credential.helper` protocol** — nothing in its `src` reads that config key, so native auth means reimplementing helper invocation ourselves; and jj-lib shells to `git` for remote ops anyway (that's where its `MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION` comes from), so a "native jj push" is a git subprocess wearing a Rust coat. |

**Non-goal: Workroom does not store credentials.** No OAuth client, no keychain writes, no auth
prompt, no account concept. The user's own helpers (`osxkeychain`, GCM, `!gh auth git-credential`,
anything corporate) are the correct answer, and shelling out gets every host — including ones we've
never heard of — for free, with the same credentials their terminal uses. GitHub Desktop is the
instructive counterexample: it also shells out (via `dugite`, which bundles its own git), but blanks
your helpers and registers itself as `credential.helper=desktop` because being *the GitHub client* is
its product. The cost of that choice is `app/src/lib/generic-git-auth.ts` — a second credential store,
with its own prompt UI, keychain keys and invalidation, for every non-GitHub host. We are not that
product, and the app's one GitHub dependency (PR status) already rides `gh`'s own token.

**When you do shell out, never parse prose.** `--porcelain`, `-z`, `%(…)`, `-T`, exit codes. Measured:
`Updates were rejected` becomes `Les mises à jour ont été rejetées` under `fr_FR.UTF-8`, so a prose
match loses the whole failure taxonomy for a non-English user. `StatusCommandRunner` pins `LC_ALL=C`
as a backstop; it is not the plan.

*Filed, not planned:* bundling our own `git` the way `dugite` does would delete all of
`Core/VCSToolVersions.swift` — floor, probe, notification, per-VCS scoping. Real cost (universal
binary, notarization, ~40MB, and the Go CLI would want the same binary), so revisit only if the
version floor actually bites a user.

docs: settle which backend each VCS write op uses

The Phase-2 entry said only "add them as `VCSWriting` members" — where writes
live, with nothing about how they run. So the CLI-vs-native question was open,
and the next session would either re-litigate it or default to more subprocess
code.

Records the split: native (libgit2/SwiftGitX, jj-lib) for every local op —
commit/amend, branch and bookmark management, the deep jj ops — and CLI for
fetch/push/pull, permanently. Three verified blockers on the network half:
SwiftGitX passes NULL options (`git_remote_fetch(remotePointer, nil, nil, nil)`,
`pull` is a `// TODO`) so it has no credential callback at all; libgit2
implements no `credential.helper` protocol, nothing in its `src` reads that
config key; and jj-lib shells to `git` for remote ops anyway, which is where its
`MINIMUM_GIT_VERSION` comes from. Every remaining Phase-2 feature is local, so
the CLI surface stops growing.

Also states the non-goal that makes the split hold: Workroom does not store
credentials. No OAuth, no keychain writes, no auth prompt, no account. The user's
own helpers are the answer and shelling out gets every host free, with the same
credentials their terminal uses. GitHub Desktop is the counterexample worth
knowing — it shells out too (`dugite`, bundling its own git) but blanks your
helpers for `credential.helper=desktop`, and pays for it with
`generic-git-auth.ts`: a second credential store with its own prompt UI, keychain
keys and invalidation for every non-GitHub host.

And the rule the review earned: when you shell out, never parse prose.
`Updates were rejected` is `Les mises à jour ont été rejetées` under
`fr_FR.UTF-8`; `LC_ALL=C` is a backstop, not a plan.

input.command:
git add macapp && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
fix(macapp): stop two CLI reads depending on incidental text behaviour

Both were found by the toolbar review and both are measured against the real
tools, not reasoned about.

**A remote name interpolated bare into a jj revset.** `jjAheadRevset` /
`jjBehindRevset` built `remote_bookmarks(remote=<name>)`, which is a parse bug
for any name that isn't a plain symbol. Verified against jj 0.43: `a b`, `a)b`
and `a:b` fail with `Failed to parse revset: Syntax error`, and — worse — `a|b`
*succeeds*, parsing as the UNION of two patterns, so the ahead/behind count comes
back wrong with nothing to notice. New `jjQuote` escapes `\` then `"` (that order,
so the quote pass's own escapes aren't re-escaped) and wraps the name; all five
cases parse correctly quoted.

**A push rejection detected by matching English.** `.rejected` keyed off
`Updates were rejected` / `! [rejected]`, and the first of those is translated —
Homebrew git 2.55 under `fr_FR.UTF-8` answers `Les mises à jour ont été
rejetées …`. `StatusCommandRunner` pins `LC_ALL=C`, so this worked, but
`.rejected` is the one failure whose recovery is a *different action* (offer Pull,
never Retry), and hanging that on an env var is thin.

`git push` now runs `--porcelain`, which puts a machine-readable
`<flag>\t<from>:<to>\t<summary>` line on stdout while leaving stderr's hints
alone. The flag is the contract — `!` rejected, ` ` updated, `*` new, `=` up to
date — and it is identical under both locales (measured). The prose checks stay as
a fallback: `--porcelain` is ours to pass on the push path only, so a rejection
arriving by any other route still classifies.

Nothing else reads push stdout, and `.rejected`'s copy is bespoke, so the added
`To …`/`Done` lines never reach the user.

Tests: the flag column across all five flags, a rejection classified from a
stdout flag paired with entirely French stderr, quoting and escaping per
character class — plus the existing end-to-end reject test now asserts the
porcelain line is present in what it classified, so dropping the flag reddens
against real git rather than silently falling back to the prose match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Xek6V5gttggL8veyT39yh5
EOF
